**Presentation slice, milestone 3 phases 3 and 4 (goal 213, 2026-11-13, source only, committed and pushed as 086b41ce; not browser-accepted):** implementation is committed and pushed on `master` as 086b41ce. What it does:

- One persisted CoK scale preference, `greybox.presentation-scale.cok`. `integer` is the default, and `fit` is the option. Absent, unavailable or corrupt storage reads as `integer`. Every live CoK surface follows it through `goldbox:presentation-scale`. Non-CoK surfaces keep their fit default.
- Integer = whole native-row snap. The width follows the 4:3 box, so the horizontal stretch is not whole. A container shorter than one row set falls back to the fitted box, reports `integer: false`, and is never cropped.
- Paint and pointer share one rectangle through `ScreenSurface.nativePointAt`. Letterbox bars return null. The automap click, which used to map across the whole canvas, now uses it.
- Availability is `verified` only for `dos-ega`. Other ids return `no-data`. Amiga combat shows `Amiga battle grid: no measured data; DOS-EGA grid shown`. Amiga art stays selectable. Accepted 2026-11-13 on Sol's recommendation.

The code is committed and pushed as 086b41ce and not browser-accepted.

## Current storage pilot handoff — 2026-11-06

The user approved the metadata-storage experiment. The [PIC1 pilot](data/graphics/README.md)
is implemented with six Git-owned normalized JSON files and
`tools/graphics_metadata_pilot.py` for extraction, lossless checking, compatibility
export and disposable SQLite indexing. It preserves 31 original asset IDs and

`(2,1)` and `(2,4)`; `11F:0039` scales them by 3 to `(6,3)` and `(6,12)` for `027F:09C3`, then
the EGA backend `027F:226C`, then reaches the `027F:12E8` screen update. The backend reads source
and surface dimensions from their graphics-object headers, clips the sprite and writes the pixel
and mask payload at `+0x17`; the first coordinate is vertical in 8-scanline units, the second is a
horizontal byte column (8 pixels). Static tracing maps the 168-row by 21-byte surface to the EGA
page origin, so the preview calls land at `(x=24,y=48)` and `(x=96,y=48)`. The tuple's
loader temporarily builds slot 12, then `A4:3E20` copies that frame into the saved slot 0; the later
preview draw still uses slot 12. A descriptor-31 runtime draw path now reads the character's
`+0x137` slot and sends it to `11F:0039`, establishing the saved slot-0 consumer. The public-stub resolver

## A manufactured null, a wiring lie in the file that briefs every agent, and DoK's "separate" opcode gap turns out to be the same gap (2026-09-05, thirty-fifth)

Six Sonnet implementers on disjoint file sets for Phase A, each followed by an adversarial
verifier told to re-derive the numbers independently and try to break the tests. No Phase B
integration has run yet — every number below is Phase A, unintegrated, and several files
(`packages/engine/src/index.ts`, `apps/web/test/e2e.mjs` outside R5, `tools/goldbox_capabilities.json`
outside R6's rows, `docs.ts`) are still owed edits a single writer has not yet applied. Verdicts:
R1 SOUND_WITH_CAVEATS, R2 SOUND_WITH_CAVEATS, R3 **DEFECTIVE**, R4 SOUND_WITH_CAVEATS, R5
SOUND_WITH_CAVEATS, R6 **DEFECTIVE**. Both DEFECTIVE verdicts turn on a version of the same
mistake — a null or a "not wired" verdict presented as measured when the measurement was either
inverted or never actually bound to the shipped code — which is the reason this entry gives them
the most space.

### R1: DoK's own dialect closes the residual gap round 34 called separate, and 0x42 was never live

Buck/Matrix `wordSetOverrides[0x42] = 0` was dead code for two full rounds: `decodeInstructionAt`
resolves `opcodeOverrides ?? KRYNN_GEN1_OPCODES` and returns `badOpcode` before it ever reads
`wordSetOverrides`, so the round-32 measurement that supposedly resynced two blocks was never
consulted. Moving it into `opcodeOverrides` (mnemonic `BUCK_EXT_42`, `uncertain: true`, gated in
`vm.ts` so it can never reach the Treasures-only `LOAD_AREA_PIECES` handler — checked live, 232
Buck / 528 Matrix instructions land on `unhandled`, 0 reach the loader) took Buck deep desync
**195 → 9** and Matrix **452 → 16**. The plan's framing that misaligned jump targets would
"collapse from 108+" was itself falsified: they were already Buck 6 / Matrix 2 on HEAD, because a
bad opcode stops the walk before it can emit a bogus target — 108/247 were the alternative-wordSet
null, never a before-state. The zero-operand null the plan supplied ("this can't desync a walker")
turned out to be **larger than advertised, not smaller**: any nonzero wordSet also collapses deep
desync into the 50s/90s range, so roughly two-thirds of 195→9 is free just from giving 0x42 a
definition at all. What actually discriminates is misaligned targets (Buck 6 vs. a best
alternative of 108, 18×; Matrix 2 vs. 247, 123×) and reachable bytes — both reported beside the
headline instead of letting the desync count carry a claim it can't.

Death Knights got its first binary-derived dialect, `ECL_GEN1_SHORT_DOK`, from three handler-read
corrections (0x1f 2→1 at `0x2fc3`; 0x27 8→4 with `countAt: 3`, the count-driven tail read past the
prefetch as required; 0x29 14→0, a nine-byte handler with no far call at all) closing DoK's
residual 29 deep desyncs to **0** and its from-cold block-33 halt at `0x51b`. That also **falsifies
round 34's own claim** that "the residual 25 are a SEPARATE opcode gap": under DoK's own dialect
the pre-0x41 reconstruction is 58 of 58 first-byte 0x41 — 100%, same as CoK and Secret — meaning
there was never a second gap, only word-set drift walking DoK's decoder onto mid-instruction
bytes. Two nulls R1 ran that the plan never asked for are worth keeping: DoK's 0x1f=0 and 0x1f=1
give **identical** census numbers on every CENSUS_PINS field except reachable bytes (+3.1%), and
0x27's `countAt: 3` vs. a flat wordSet 4 differ only by 0.8% reachable bytes — both pinned as
first-class assertions so nobody later credits the corpus with a decision only the handler byte
actually made.

The verifier reproduced essentially everything to the digit, including four of R1's own claimed
mutations run independently, and confirmed the "solved but unwired" gap honestly: `index.ts` does
not export `ECL_GEN1_SHORT_DOK` yet, so nothing in the app can reach it until Phase B applies the
sizeable wiring list R1 handed off (`explore.ts`, `gen1Profiles.ts`, `build-dqk-dir.mts`, two
false 0x42 attributions left standing in `goldbox_capabilities.json` and `docs.ts` that would
become *permanently unfalsifiable* once 0x42 is live if nobody corrects them). One real defect:
R1 scored one of the plan's own null predictions ("0x1f gives deep 12 / misaligned 40 either way")
as VOID/non-reproducing — but it measured that prediction against the **fully-corrected**
dialect instead of the isolated, pre-correction frame the plan meant. The verifier re-measured in
the plan's intended frame and the numbers reproduce exactly. No shipped number or conclusion
changes, but it is a null retired on a measurement it was never about — the same failure mode
this project's own "the null decides the finding" rule exists to catch, running backward this
time. R1 also caught a stale Python mirror (`map_buck_ecl_dispatch.LONG_WORD_SETS`) that never
received round 34's `0x41: {wordSet: 2}`, meaning Gateway and Treasures had been scored against
the wrong baseline for a full round, and opened a new (unfixed, out-of-lane) finding: Pools and
Treasures both read opcode 0x29 as zero-operand from their own handlers, against the shared
table's inherited 14.

### R2: the SOUND.DAX event record is three bytes, and the census was a framing artifact — with two wrong "reasons" for the fix shipped alongside the right numbers

Disassembling the driver's own dispatch (four independent MIDI.DAX backend blocks agreeing
exactly, plus MPU-401 corroborating structurally with MIDI's own width table) settles the CoK/DoK
`SOUND.DAX` event record at **3 bytes** for Note-On/Note-Off (2 data + 1 trailing wait byte) and
**2 bytes** for program change — not the 1-byte-per-event grammar round 34 shipped. The trailing
byte is the `[0x2BD]` per-tick wait counter round 34's own `docs/midi-dax-format.md` §1.4 predicted
in July and never located (fetch `0x493`, store `0x4a0`). Every published number was a framing
artifact: 11,091 events / 14 segments / 5,538=5,538 becomes **3,700 events / 7 segments /
1,846=1,846**, with 7,860 ticks newly measurable. Round 34's *conclusion* is strengthened, not
reversed — every Note-Off now closes an open same-channel same-pitch Note-On (1846/1846 against a
seeded shuffle null of 0.540), pitches run 36–96, velocities take six discrete values — only the
counts and segment count were wrong. The 1-byte null was falsified by the handler directly (the
0x80 branch's second data byte is fetched and then skipped by a bare `inc si`, never read), not
merely outvoted by statistics, and the "clean 0xFC end, 0 malformed" evidence round 34's own docs
cited is shown to be **non-discriminating**: both framings reach the identical terminator with
zero malformed bytes.

The verifier reproduced the handler reads and the corrected census exactly, byte offset for byte
offset, and then found three defects in the *reasons* given for numbers that are themselves
correct. First, the shipped explanation for why 0xC0 events dropped 14→7 ("half were data bytes
that happened to have bit 7 set") is **false** — no byte in this buffer has bit 7 set; the seven
spurious events are running-status continuation bytes that are all literally `0x00`, misread as
events under the old 1-byte grammar. Second, "five of the seven program changes are consecutive at
the head" is false on both counts — only four are, and the memo's own byte listing fifteen lines
above the claim contradicts it (two Note-Ons intervene before the fifth). Third, and most
important: the rewrite deleted the decoder's only real validity check (data bytes with bit 7 set
are invalid) and left `malformed: 0` in its place, still presented in the census tables as a
measured column — but for any stream beginning with a status byte (this one does) `malformed` is
now *structurally* pinned at zero and cannot be otherwise. The deleted check would have been a real
discriminator against a mixed 1-byte/3-byte hybrid framing (1,561 of 12,651 slots invalid vs. 0 of
11,090 for the framings actually in play) — a control this round had in hand and did not report.
None of this moves the corrected 3,700/1,846/7,860 numbers; it does mean three sentences shipped
into research docs and (via the Phase B handoff) toward the capability ledger need their reasoning
rewritten, not their conclusion.

### R3: a "worthless null" that was manufactured, and a defect this project has a name for

R3 found and wired a real bug: all 16 DOS HLIB "method-25" composite images were assembling
correctly and then being flattened at only one of the app's decode sites (`main.ts`'s asset
browser) — the same shape as round 34's pool-amiga miss. Wiring `loadGame.ts` and `nwnPreview.ts`
recovers 12 of the 16 route-reachable (the DQK `DISK2/PICC.TLB` composites remain unreachable
because that file is in no manifest, correctly disclosed rather than hidden), plus 3 new Amiga
GLIB composites from the one WHDLoad file that carries them. A separate, real find: the hand-
maintained dispatch-site constant in `tools/test_decoded_asset_dispatch_sites.py` had drifted to 3
declared sites against 5 actual ones (the previous grep pattern missed the `!==` spelling), so the
guard against round 34's exact defect class had itself been blind to 2 of 5 sites for the whole of
round 34 — now rewritten to enumerate from source.

The DEFECTIVE verdict is for the endianness null. The plan asked for a specific, falsifiable test:
read the Amiga GLIB `0x19` composite records little-endian and check the DOS height invariant. R3
reported this null as **worthless — 3/3 both ways, discriminating nothing** — and used the DOS
twin comparison to carry the whole big-endian verdict instead. The verifier re-ran the plan's null
exactly as specified and it is **not worthless**: BE holds 3/3, LE holds **0/3**, clearing the
plan's own bar (≥2/3 LE failures) outright. R3's "3/3 both ways" was produced by *also*
byte-swapping the composite's source-image height — a value that is not a field of the `0x19`
record at all, and which cannot even be obtained consistently under the hypothesis that would
license swapping it (the same region reads a workable 8 big-endian and an impossible 2,048
little-endian, which would need 10,240 body bytes the file does not have). This is the inverse of
"the null decides the finding": here the finding decided the null, converting a real, clean
discriminator into a report that a real discriminator doesn't exist. The underlying big-endian
verdict survives — the DOS-twin match is genuine and independently reproduced — but the null as
reported is fabricated, and it is now embedded as a named, permanent assertion inside engine
source (`glib.ts`'s docblock) and a test literally titled to assert the opposite of what the bytes
show. A second, smaller instance of the same family: a test named for "the range-guard rejects an
out-of-range composite" cannot actually fail that way (no part in the fixture is out of range; the
real null comes from a decode-on-compressed-bytes path the guard never touches) — a probe that
cannot fail the way its author says it can, the exact class this project already tracks.

### R4: both titles' own race tables, both plan-supplied nulls non-discriminating, and a disclosure that got quietly destroyed

Pools of Darkness (`0xAEAD`) and Treasures of the Savage Frontier (`0xD454`) each carry their own
7-entry race table (Elf/Half-Elf/Dwarf/Gnome/Halfling/Human/Monster), independently derived and
each scoring 7/7 plausible strings at the real base against 0/16 at every ±1..±8 shift. Read
0-based, the borrowed CoAB race enum this codebase had been using is falsified 12/14: BINKY
(Pools) and CHERROD (Treasures) were rejected purely as translation artifacts (byte 5, read as
CoAB's `mountainDwarf`/`halfling`, is actually each title's own `Human`); both class-byte-3
paladins read Human under the 0-based reading and no other. Import outcome: Pools now joins 6/6
with an empty rejection list (was 5/6); Treasures joins 6 with 0 rule-rejections and exactly 2
party-cap rejections (was CHERROD+SMOKE, now OUGO+SMOKE). Separately, Buck Rogers' own `START.EXE`
carries a 7-entry career table with **Scout**, falsifying the shipped comment that its five careers
"are the only ones the real game has" — reported as exactly that (six non-monster careers exist;
whether the creation screen offers Scout is unmeasured), with no new field assigned to the record.

Both plan-supplied nulls were measured and came back non-discriminating, and R4 shipped that
finding as the deliverable rather than quietly picking a winner: the import-outcome test scores
14/14 under *both* the 0-based and 1-based own-table readings (only the CoAB enum fails, at 12/14),
so party legality cannot select the basing — only the paladin-legality and class-byte arguments
can, and are labelled "argued by consequence, indexing instruction not located" exactly as round
34's Secret finding was. The ±8 fencepost null, which worked for Secret and for two of Buck's four
tables, **fails** on Buck's own stride-5 and stride-7 tables (a ±8 window can only separate a table
whose stride exceeds 8; the tool now emits a `window_can_alias_stride` flag on every null so this
precondition is checked rather than assumed).

The verifier's two "important" defects matter more than the counts. First, the actual shipped
importer map (`POOLS_TREASURES_RACE_TO_DL` in `importPoolsTreasuresParty.ts`) has **no green gate
at all**: the engine test re-declares an identical literal locally and scores that copy, so
reinstating the exact CoAB bug in the real map leaves every engine test green and `tsc` clean —
only the two e2e cases bind the shipped code, and both are RED, deferred to Phase B. Second, R4's
own change destroyed a round-33 disclosure: OUGO (Treasures) is the hero whose class byte disagrees
with her own decoded class-level array, and before this round she joined the party carrying a
visible "class byte and level array disagree" badge; now she is a party-cap rejection and vanishes
from the panel entirely, with nothing downstream able to see her disagreement. R4 self-reported
this honestly but filed it as "a UI decision outside scope" — the verifier disagrees, since the
file is in R4's own exclusive Owns line, and calls it a real regression against this project's own
disclosure rule, not a deferral.

### R5: the plan's null was falsified 4 of 4, and the verifier caught it red on the live production site

The plan asked whether any of CoK's Throtl-arrival paths reach a block-17 VM turn that emits no
picture at all — a defect requiring zero code changes if true. Measured from the VM under each
path's own arrival memory before any host code was touched: **0 of 4 are silent.** Travel arm 11
emits picture 58; arm 3 emits 58 then 57; the post-caravan control walks 58→57→58; block-17
re-entry emits 58. The ids are path-dependent, not a constant — which matters because it means a
"pin 58 everywhere" fix would have fabricated a golden, and the null's own test data caught that
before it was written. One line in `explore.ts` (`openCokThrotlArrival` now builds its own
`DialoguePresentation` when the caller has none) turns both new e2e assertions green; the full
187-case harness runs 181/187 with every CoK case passing. DoK's overland dispatcher emits zero
picture effects across all 570 cells of its own map (nothing dropped there); Pool's regional hosts
are confirmed to drop five real, resolvable picture ids across three sectors — reported, not
wired, exactly as the plan required.

The verifier's strongest move was reproducing the RED-before-fix state by hitting the live
production bundle at dionysus.dk/greybox directly, rather than reverting and re-running locally —
stronger evidence than the report's own method, and it reproduced the exact failing JSON both new
e2e cases print. Two defects, both minor: the headline's "4 of 4 arrival paths" overcounts — one of
the four measured states is a duplicate of the arm-11 branch reached via block 17's own LEAVE-then-
re-entry, not an independent path, and the plan's actual fourth named unfixed site
(`openCokTravel.move`'s immediate-chain branch) was never separately measured, though the fix
covers it structurally. And the fix itself reproduces, in miniature, the exact silent-degradation
seam it diagnoses in `dialogue.ts`: a bare `catch { return undefined }` with no warning, and no
check that the ids this path actually emits (57, 58) are present in the loaded picture map.

### R6: a resolver with 1.000 precision on two fires, and the round's own wiring lie

R6 built a "`<symbol>` is not wired into `<path>`" prose resolver and measured it honestly against
itself: unguarded, it fires on 15 candidates at precision 0.267 (the null); with a historical-

still-true CoK `dosSong` control) — but its **recall is only 2 of 5** hand-adjudicated live stale
claims, which the verifier recomputed as 2 of **6** once R6's own §4 finding (a third live stale

an error that happens to flatter the tool. R6 also corrected three ledger `evidence_date` fields
that were all behind their own newest value-bearing commit, moved the `KNOWN_UNCONSUMED` export
count 751→754 by fixing a string-literal blind spot in the audit tokenizer (exactly {C64, TILE,
renderWallView}, both controls unmoved), and **falsified round 34's own P14**: `matrixXmi.test.ts`
was never vacuous (its guard is describe-level and correctly SKIPs), while `loadGameGlbrMusic.test.ts`
genuinely was (0 assertions executed under a fixture rename) — and R6's own first-draft vitest

Two of the verifier's defects are blocking, and the first is the reason this entry exists in its
current shape. **R6's own CLAUDE.md restatement ships a false wiring claim** — "`buildAmigaArtOverride`,

(`dqkArtMap.ts:211`) from `tools/build-dqk-dir.mts:367`, the primary deliverable's own build
executor. R6 made exactly the mistake its own task was written to catch: trusting a consumer-audit
tool's documented blind spot (never search a name's own defining file for its callers) as though it
were a fact about the tree. Worse, R6 wrote a test — `test_the_restatement_keeps_the_half_that_makes_it_honest`
— that *requires* the literal strings "reached by no product route" and "buildAmigaArtOverride" to
remain in CLAUDE.md, so the next agent who corrects the sentence turns that test red on purpose.

**This is the same defect established independently, outside this round's workflow, earlier
today.** Before reading any of R6's transcript, the same false "zero consumers" claim was found in
the checked-in `CLAUDE.md` — sourced from `KNOWN_UNCONSUMED` in `tools/test_engine_export_consumers.py`
— and traced through the identical chain (`build-dqk-dir.mts:367` → `buildPortableArtOverrides` →

The second blocking defect: the new evidence-date gate (`test_ledger_evidence_dates.py`) is
guaranteed to fail on the very commit that lands it, for 2 of the 3 files it guards.
`goldbox_corpus_routes.json` and `goldbox_campaign_matrix.json` were dated to their *previous*
