### Two corrections established outside this round's workflow

Both belong in this entry because they bear directly on what round 35 produced and on what should
run next.

First, the `buildAmigaArtOverride` wiring lie above: `CLAUDE.md` has been corrected in place. The
lesson recorded there — a literal-token consumer audit cannot see one level of indirection, so its
output is a fact about the tool, not about the tree — should travel with any future citation of
`KNOWN_UNCONSUMED`.

Second, and larger: round 35's entire plan was written against a **superseded goal**. The project
direction was corrected on 2026-09-05: the DOS deliverable is now one clean-room native DOS
Greybox engine supporting all titles (see `native/`, already 47,240 lines of x86 asm with a
runtime `/G` DOS/Amiga/C64 art switch), not CoK/DoK retargeted onto SSI's own DQK engine — a
direction parked back on 2026-06-25 but never reflected in `CLAUDE.md`, so it briefed six agents
wrongly for ten weeks. The consequence is visible in what round 35 actually produced: R1, R2 and R4
produced portable spec knowledge (ECL dialects, an audio event-frame format, two race tables) that
transfers cleanly to `native/`; R3 is half browser-only; and **R5 spent its round patching the
browser's decode-once-per-screen dialogue architecture, which is exactly the pattern the native
engine already handles better.** Round 35 spent roughly 5.6 hours and 2.15M tokens entirely inside
the browser engine while the now-primary native track received nothing, extending a gap open since
2026-08-21.

### Process note

Every implementer this round hit the same hazard from a different angle: `pnpm --filter
@goldbox/engine test` and `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` are being run against a tree five other
agents are simultaneously editing, and every one of them correctly flagged the resulting red tests
and stopped `tsc` runs as belonging to files outside their lane rather than investigating or fixing
them. That discipline held everywhere this round. What did not fully hold: several agents left
untracked `_scratch_*.test.ts` probe files inside `packages/engine/test/`, collected by the full
suite and not cleaned up before this handoff was written — the integrator needs to confirm they are
deleted before anything is committed. And twice this round a plan-supplied null was measured
correctly by the letter and reported wrong by the frame: R1 scored a null against the fully-
corrected dialect instead of the isolated change the plan meant, and R3 manufactured "3/3 both
ways" by swapping a field the record doesn't contain. Both are instances of this project's own
rule that the null decides the finding, running in reverse — the finding deciding what counted as
the null. Read every DEFECTIVE- or SOUND_WITH_CAVEATS-flagged null in this round's memos against
the plan's own wording before citing it again.

## A pin written to fail came due, and one file's byte identity had been hiding a whole format claim (2026-09-04, thirty-fourth)

Six Sonnet agents on disjoint resources for Phase A, then a serialized single-writer integration
with four more on disjoint file sets for Phase B, and three more in part 2: a plan-corrections
writer, an adversarial verifier told to falsify everything the round had just landed, and a
regression investigator. The last two earned their keep — the verifier caught the one artifact
that never got the Phase B pass, and the investigator's instrumented browser trace is what stopped
a correct golden from being re-pinned to a wrong value.

### The pin that was written to fail, and did

Round 30 measured Secret of the Silver Blades' party import at **5 of 6** and wrote down exactly why
the sixth was missing: Secret's race byte read 6, which is not a value in Curse of the Azure Bonds'
`Race` enum, so every hero defaulted to human; this ruleset implements the manual's
non-humans-only multiclass rule, so MALACHITE — the party's only fighter/thief — failed validation
as a "human" multiclass and was rejected. Round 30 then pinned that two-sided, in its own words:

> if Secret's own race table is ever located and byte 6 resolves to a demihuman, MALACHITE will
> import, this case will go RED, and whoever solved it is forced to come back here and re-state the
> count instead of quietly gaining a party member.

R3 transcribed Secret's own race string table out of its own `START.EXE` at `0xEB91`
(`SECRET_RACE_LABEL`, re-derivable from the retail bytes by `tools/secret_race_table.py`). The pin
went red on the next run, and the answer is better than the prediction: under Secret's own table
byte 6 **is** Human — CoAB's default had been right for five heroes by accident — but
**MALACHITE's race byte is 3, not 6, and 3 is Dwarf.** As a mountainDwarf the multiclass is legal.
The import is now 6 of 6 with an empty rejection list.

The re-stated case pins more than the count: the per-hero race byte *and* the label Secret's own
table gives it, so a revert to the CoAB enum fails on MALACHITE's race before it fails on party
size. It also caught something round 30 structurally could not see, having only ever measured the
five heroes that imported: **experience is not uniform.** MALACHITE ships at 100,000 where the
other five ship at 200,000.

### Opcode 0x41: declining to guess was right, and then someone went and read the handler

R1's headline was ECL opcode `0x41`, added to the **shared** Gen1 base table at `wordSet: 2`. One
entry takes Champions' deep desync sites 33 → 0, Secret's 40 → 0 and Death Knights' 72 → 29, with
no shallow-census regression anywhere. R1 shipped it as `UNKNOWN_0x41`, `uncertain: true`,
explicitly declining to assert semantics: `EclDump`'s own `SetupCommandTable` is dense only over
`0x00..0x40` — the very range the table was reverse-engineered from — so its silence about `0x41`
is a property of EclDump, not of the bytes.

Declining was right. What no single agent could see is that **seven independent derivations in this
codebase already agree `0x41` takes two operands**: Gateway (`GATEWAY_EXT_41`), Treasures
(`TREASURES_AWARD_XP`, handler at `GAME.OVR` file offset `0x2c40`), Pools of Darkness
(`POOLS_AWARD_XP`, file `0x240c`), Buck Rogers (`BUCK_EXT_41`), Matrix Cubed, DQK Gen2
(`GEN2_EXT_41`), and R1's own CoK/DoK/Secret derivation. Two of those are not operand counts at
all — Pools and Treasures each transcribed the handler from their *own* binary and found it reads
two operands, then `mov cx, 0x64`, and awards operand-2 × 100 experience. R1's own byte-shape note
(the operand word is always a multiple of 500) is consistent with that reading and was never
connected to it.

The obvious next question — do the three titles the *base* table actually serves have a `0x41`
entry in their own binaries? — had never been asked, so a follow-up asked it. All three do:
CoK `GAME.OVR` `0x4048`, DoK `0x2e0e`, Secret `0x43ff`, located by structural match against the
CoAB oracle. DoK's offset reproduces the pre-existing `build/dok-ecl-dispatch-map.json` row
byte-for-byte, which is a check on the tooling rather than a new fact; CoK's and Secret's rows had
never been generated before. Each handler reads exactly two operands from its own
`mov al,2; push ax; lcall <parser>` prologue, so **`wordSet: 2` is now confirmed from binary
ground truth**, a different evidence class from the operand-stream statistics R1 argued from.

All three implement one idiom: read a 0/1 flag and a round word amount, count the *active* party
members, divide, and `ADD`/`ADC` the share into a 32-bit per-character accumulator — flag=1 walks
the party chain, flag=0 hits a single target. CoK walks that chain through CCH `+0x17F/+0x181`,
**the same "next combatant" far pointer that CoK's already byte-verified post-combat
`calc_battle_exp` uses**, from an investigation that borrowed nothing from this one. Two
independently reverse-engineered pieces of code agreeing on a structural detail is what upgraded
this from a plausible reading to a named one: the mnemonic is now `GEN1_AWARD_XP`.

`uncertain` stays `true`, for a stated reason rather than out of habit: nothing in this repo names
the accumulator field (CoK `+0x116/+0x118`) as the canonical experience field, so what is proven is
the structure, not the label. Note also that this family *divides* where Pools' and Treasures' own
`0x41` *multiplies* by 100 — same opcode byte, different mechanics, which is why the dialects stay
separate.

And the follow-up falsified R1's own byte-shape claim rather than confirming it. "Always a multiple
of 500" is **98.4% (121/123)** on an exhaustive walk, with two genuine CoK exceptions — `ECL1.DAX`
block 32 @`0x1cec` = 300, `ECL2.DAX` block 67 @`0x1bff` = 32633 — both in the flag=0 branch.
Stratified by the flag, which R1's sample could not do, flag=1 is 95/95. The null makes the
surviving claim worth more than the original absolute did: arbitrary reached word operands in the
same blocks are multiples of 500 just **0.53%** of the time (n = 29,954), so the roundness is a
~185× enrichment specific to this argument. One caveat is kept rather than buried — that
follow-up's from-scratch walker reproduces CoK (33) and Secret (40) exactly but reads 50 DoK sites
where the engine implies 43; that is its simplified control-flow rules, and `eclReachability.test.ts`
remains the authority.

Landing it turned 20 tests red, and none was fixed by regenerating a golden. Each was adjudicated
by asking what produced the expected value: `eclGen2`'s permanently-invalid sentinel had *become
valid* and was re-anchored to `ECL_OPCODE_MAX + 1`; Gateway's mutation probe could no longer fail
and was re-armed with a wrong value instead of an absent one; Matrix's discriminating-opcode count
legitimately **shrank** 18 → 17, weakening its own claim, which is the correct direction; two
`NEWECL` cross-references appeared, corroborated by R1's independent execution trace on the same
block; and R1's own thirteen tests were preserved as a *reconstruction* of the pre-fix state, so
the evidence that justified the change stays falsifiable.

### The opcode fix broke a green route test, and the break was the point

Closing the `0x41` desync turned `cok-retail-travel` red: Champions' caravan route came back to
Throtl with `picture: null` where the case pins **58**. Text and menu choices were still exactly
right; only the art was gone. Two readings were available and both were wrong — *"the 58 is a
golden the buggy code produced, re-pin it to null"* and *"the opcode entry is bad, revert it"*.

Causation was established by experiment before any theory: deleting that one table line makes the
case pass, restoring it makes it fail. Then the VM was instrumented in a live browser run of the
real app, with and without the entry. Before, the VM **halted** at CoK `ECL1` block 16 offset
`0x79a` — "bad opcode at 1946", the exact site round 34's own Bar C had flagged as reachable from
cold. That halt reached the host as a clean `end`, which routed the return through
`openCokTravel`'s `onClose` branch — **the one call site that already forwarded a
`DialoguePresentation`**. Picture 58 rendered, correctly, for the wrong reason. With `0x41`
decoded the VM continues three instructions further and takes a genuine retail `NEWECL` from block
16 to block 17, through `remountCampaignChain`, whose `cok`/17 branch had never forwarded
`presentation` — a gap dating to `0da9504f`, one day before the native-art feature landed in
`5774016`. Block 17 mounted without its native canvas, `renderPresentation()` bailed, and
`currentPictureId` stayed `null` forever. The block-17 VM run emits `{type:'picture', id:58}`
identically in both cases; only the host wiring dropped it.

So the golden was right, the opcode was right, and the crash had been **hiding a real wiring bug
for five weeks**. The fix threads `presentation` through (`apps/web/src/ui/explore.ts`); the
assertion keeps its 58 and now reaches it by retail control flow instead of by a masked halt.

The pin needed care, because `cok-retail-travel` cannot protect its own fix: picture 58 renders
under *both* the halt path and the chain path, so deleting `0x41` again would leave that case green
while silently restoring the crash. `packages/engine/test/cokThrotlChain.test.ts` pins the
discriminating fact instead — the retail bytes at the halt site decode and lead to `NEWECL 17`.

**And the first draft of that pin was worthless.** It looked up the block with `.id` where the
field is `blockId`, found nothing, returned `null`, and both of its real assertions passed
vacuously — green even with the opcode entry deleted. Nothing caught that except mutation-testing
the pin itself, which is the whole reason this project has the rule. It now asserts the fixture is
non-null rather than skipping silently, and the revert experiment reproduces the historical
`bad opcode at 1946` verbatim.

### GLBR was five titles plus a leftover, and byte identity was doing the hiding

Round 33 decoded Buck Rogers: Countdown's and Matrix Cubed's `MUSIC.DAX` to identical numbers — 8
GLBR songs, 1959 events, 31 channel streams — noticed the files were byte-identical, correctly said
so, and then published "GLBR is a six-title format rather than four."

R4 shows the identity was the whole problem. Matrix's own unpacked `START.EXE` and `GAME.OVR`
**never open `MUSIC.DAX` by name** (0 file-open references, against Countdown's 2 — a Pascal-string
`'MUSIC'`+`'.dax'` construction found only in Countdown's loader). Matrix scores with Miles/AIL XMI:
`BUCKA/B/C.XMI` beside a 152-instrument `FATV9.AD` bank — the same container shape as DQK's own
199-instrument `INSTR.AD` — decoded by the *existing* `xmi.ts`/`instrAd.ts` with zero code changes.
GLBR is a **five**-title format (Death Knights, Gateway, Treasures, Pools of Darkness, Countdown)
**plus one leftover file**.

Phase B closed the half R4 could not: Matrix's manifest now lists its real stack, which flips
`loadGame`'s manifest-driven `hasXmiSiblings` rule, and the census becomes **21 songs / 5702 events
/ 95 channel streams** — re-measured through the shipped code path rather than the test-local clone
R4 used, agreeing per file (BUCKA 7/2684/45, BUCKB 7/2623/43, BUCKC 7/395/7). `GameMusicSummary`
gained a `format` field so the dashboard stops hardcoding "GLBR".

The single shared `MUSIC_ROW` regex in `e2e.mjs` was the artifact that made the shared claim
comfortable, and it is now two regexes that act as each other's control: Matrix's half asserts the
XMI numbers are present **and Countdown's GLBR numbers are absent**, so a silent fallback to the
leftover file fails instead of reading as a pass. `loadGameGlbrMusic.test.ts`'s clone is inverted
accordingly — the real manifest is now the XMI assertion, and the test-local clone *strips* the
`.XMI` rows to prove `hasXmiSiblings` is what drives the switch.

### R6 reopened a closed question by asking a different one

Round 33 concluded that the buffers reached through CoK's driver handshake were sound effects, not
songs. R6's finding is that this answered a different question than "are the songs *inside*
`SOUND.DAX` block 1", and it starts by voiding its own predecessor's instrument: the static
`grammar_score` detector scores its **only known positive control** at 16, below its own published
hit bar of 18. A detector that cannot clear its own bar with its own positive control is not a
detector, so every static negative that used it is void — not confirmed, not refuted.

Recalibrated, the picture inverts. `SOUND.DAX` block 1's own first word (`0x007d` = 125) is a real
stream-start pointer, seeded into the resident driver's tick cursor by `mov ax, es:[0]` at install
time; decoding from 125 runs to a literal `0xFC` terminator with **0 malformed bytes**. It ranks
**#1 of 814** corpus sources with 11,090 events, against a histogram-preserving shuffled null whose
best is 368 — and it is the only source in the corpus that terminates cleanly at all. Three of its
segments are large, balanced, five-voice passages (4,801 / 1,141 / 5,132 events).

Two nulls are reported honestly against R6's own interest. The plan's proposed
"is the header a directory" null **does not discriminate** — the stream's own event-boundary
density is already 0.796, so almost any offset lands on some boundary; only the stricter
fresh-status-byte test separates real (0.465) from a 5,000-trial histogram-preserving shuffle
(mean 0.327, max 0.44). And the header turns out to be neither alternative cleanly: driver state
**plus** one literal, disassembly-confirmed pointer field. R6 also corrects an implicit claim of
its own lineage — the `[0x2B7]` cursor cell is block-1-specific, not universal; block 3 uses
`[0x340]`.

The census is wired to the dashboard and labelled **"(decode only)"**, because that is all it is.
Death Knights' `SOUND.DAX` is byte-identical to Champions' (sha256 `7df3bde4…4246a5`), so its row
is file identity, not a second confirmation — the exact trap round 33 fell into with the shared
`MUSIC.DAX`, written down this time rather than rediscovered. An earlier draft of this round's own
ledger brief asserted a Death Knights finding on R6's authority; R6's research is Champions-only,
the agent holding that file refused to write it, and that refusal was correct. The DoK note now in
the ledger cites the byte-identity measurement made here instead, and says which.

### Wiring, because not wiring is this project's most-repeated mistake

Three Phase A modules were wired rather than pinned as unconsumed: the desync triage into the
`?ecl=` status line (it now says what *kind* of edge a deep walk stopped on), `decodeCokSoundBank`
into `loadGame`'s census, and `decodeBuckSavedCharacter` into a new `?import=buck` panel with its
own e2e case. The Buck panel is display-only on purpose — R2 declined to identify that ruleset's
race, class and ability-field **order**, so there is nothing to hand `createCharacter`; the septet
renders as an ordered tuple, never as STR/DEX/CON, and the e2e case pins the *absence* of a roster
join so that a future wiring without an order oracle has to argue with a test.

The export-consumer pin moved 739 → 751 with every round-34 addition classified rather than
absorbed: ten type-only names (this audit's documented structural-inference blind spot), four
executed through a consumed entry point but never named outside their module, and exactly **one**
genuinely unconsumed — `segmentIndexForOffset`, which needs a live DOSBox-X memory read the browser
cannot perform. It is stated, not wired, because wiring it would mean inventing a caller.

### Process note

Two tripwires fired on Phase B's own output and both were resolved by fixing the thing, not the
pin: `test_web_routes_documented.py` caught `?import=buck` as undocumented (documented, not
allowlisted — the allowlist should keep shrinking), and `test_ledger_stale_claims.py`'s four pinned
self-contradictions all cleared, moving to `FORMER_STALE_LEDGER_CLAIMS`. One gotcha is recorded
beside them: that detector's guard pairs **single** quotes, so the verbatim replacement text its own
research doc suggested silently failed to clear it — the apostrophes in "Cubed's"/"profile's" broke
the pairing. Found by running the detector, not by trusting the patch text. A suggested patch is a
hypothesis like any other.

The round's other lesson is about parallel agents and stale reads: the ledger agent finished a long
pass and reported three items as "still not applied" that had landed in commits made while it
worked — including opcode `0x41`. Acting on that report verbatim would have left three ledger
`ecl` census entries quoting pre-fix desync counts as current. Every cross-file number a long-running
agent reports has to be re-measured against the tree after it finishes, not read out of its report.

## Four route goldens were pinning a bug, and they were generated by the code under test (2026-09-04, thirty-third)

Six Sonnet agents on disjoint resources, then a serialized single-writer integration. The round's
headline is not a new capability. It is that this project's own regression suite had, for two
rounds, been protecting a defect — and the shape of how that happened is worth more than the fix.

**R2 was told the goldens were the oracle, and stopped one step short of the right answer.** Both
Pools of Darkness and Treasures of the Savage Frontier carry ECL opcode `0x27 TREASURE`. Read from
each title's own `GAME.OVR` handler — Pools at file `0x1626`, Treasures at `0x1afd`, transcribed
instruction by instruction and independently of each other — the frame is three fixed operands, then
a COUNT whose *value* governs a variable tail: `{wordSet: 4, countAt: 3}`. Measured across the 8
reached corpus sites: 8 of 8 counts are immediates (0 memory-coded), and 7 of 8 have a non-empty
tail that a flat four-word frame misparses as instructions. R2 shipped nothing, because shipping it
turned four route assertions red and its brief named those assertions as the authority.

They were not the authority.

- `poolsMiddleRoute.test.ts`'s own file header says its expectations were generated by the very VM
  under test, and that "if that VM mis-models an opcode the walk inherits the error." It disclosed
  its own limitation and then got cited as an oracle anyway.
- `treasuresQuestFlag.test.ts` pinned `status === 'halted'`, and its own comment named the cause as
  "the disclosed Sec.8.4.2 TREASURE/bad-opcode gap at 0xA1B6". `halted` carries
  `haltReason: 'bad opcode at <pc>'`. The assertion was pinning the defect **by name**.
- `treasuresEndingRoute.test.ts`'s test C had been green the whole time against a *test-local*
  dialect, proving retail block `ECL1#47` contains an explicit 1..8 count ladder. The right answer
  was sitting in the same file as the assertions that forbade it.

Two further lines were independent of all of that: R1's execution-coverage oracle found 12 Pools
offsets the VM executes but the deep walk never reaches, going to **0** under the frame; and
removing the frame turns 12 tests red while a mirror test that reconstructs the legacy flat frame
stays green. So five lines agree, four goldens were regenerated rather than obeyed, and the general
rule is now recorded: **a golden produced by the code under test cannot adjudicate that code.**

**What the fix actually plays.** Treasures' deep desync count goes 14 → 0 and Pools' 18 → 3 (shallow
3 → 1). Treasures' campaign-ending script (block 38) now runs end to end — the full retail FREEZEFIRE
denouement through "IT HAS, INDEED, BEEN GLORIOUS!", the terminal memory writes and the `NEWECL #51`
chain — where it previously died on a bad opcode. The Pools `(4,13)` ki-rin cell now awards the 15
items its own retail text promises instead of misparsing them.

**And round 32's `0x37` "falsification" fell with it.** Round 32 proposed Treasures'
`0x37 → {wordSet: 2}` from its own handler at `0x2577`, saw the real VM crash, bisected, and
retracted. That bisection toggled `0x37` while holding `0x27` at its *own* wrong base frame, so it
was never a single-variable test. With `0x27` corrected, the "falsified" override produces **0** deep
desyncs across all 30 Treasures blocks — matching R2's independent dispatch-byte reading that
`0x2577` is `0x37`'s own linear entry (`cmp al,0x37` / `call 0x2577` at `0x33c1`, sharing no target
with either neighbour). It is now shipped. Both retractions are retracted.

One trap on the way in, recorded because it reproduces round 32's crash *exactly* and would read as a
third falsification: `vm.ts`'s `case 0x37` selects the two-operand lookup by **mnemonic**. Shipping
the override with a name `vm.ts` did not know sent the instruction down the inherited three-operand
`loadPieces` path, which read an operand the frame never decoded and threw "Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'code')" — round 32's literal error text, from a plumbing bug wearing a
falsification's clothes. `vm.ts` now matches a set, so each title keeps its own label.

**Every clean-EXIT count this project has published is a lower bound.** R1's `walkEclReachable`
follows all five ECL header entry points and every `GOTO`/`GOSUB`/`ON_GOTO`/`ON_GOSUB`, where
`disassembleEclBlock` stops at each block's *first* `EXIT` and never sees the combat, quest or
descriptor subroutines placed later in a block's own bytes. Deep exceeds shallow in **6 of 11** Gen1
titles, and not marginally: CoK 33 vs 0, DoK 72 vs 1, Secret 40 vs 0, Buck 195 vs 2, Matrix 452 vs 3.
Every affected ledger entry now carries both numbers, with the note that deep counts are *sites* and
shallow counts are *blocks*. The walker was wired into the `?ecl=` inspector rather than pinned as an
expected-unreachable module — the sixth instance of "solved but unwired" this project has caught, and
the first one caught in the same round it was created.

**Three claims corrected that were already published.** Buck Rogers' containers were not
"un-reverse-engineered": 17 GEO blocks at exactly 1026 bytes, 9 WALLDEF each a multiple of 780, and
25 ECL all carrying the `0x1388` magic decode under the *same* Gen1 loaders already proven on
CoK/DoK, with 16 paired GEO/ECL areas across the six C64 sides. The project's blanket C64 rule
("always compare payloads from offset 2") was per-family, not universal — only GEO and ECL carry a
DOS-side header — and the blanket rule had been reporting Buck's `ITEMFILE00` as 72% different when
it is **byte-identical**. And two entries in the same ledger had contradicted each other for two
rounds about whether Matrix Cubed's ECL had been disassembled.

**What did not move, and is reported as a negative rather than dropped.** CoK's MIDI.DAX
music-timeline buffer is still unfound — but now for a stated reason. The CX/ES install handshake
itself is resolved: two live GameLink captures read distinct nonzero segments at the exact
`mov [0x0012], cx` cell against a universal on-disk `0x0000`. Both buffers those segments point at
decode cleanly (11,090 events, 0 malformed) and both appear verbatim inside `SOUND.DAX`'s SFX
bank. They are sound effects, not songs. Buck and Matrix Cubed's `MUSIC.DAX` *is* decoded — 8 GLBR
songs, 1959 events, 31 channel streams each — making GLBR a six-title format rather than four; but a
byte scan finds no AdLib or C/MS port immediate anywhere in their shared driver, so that is a
decode-and-census claim and the ledger says so twice.

> **Corrected by round 34 R4 (2026-09-04).** "A six-title format" was wrong, and the byte identity
> that made it look safe is exactly what made it wrong. GLBR is a **five**-title format — Death
> Knights, Gateway, Treasures, Pools of Darkness and Buck Rogers: Countdown — **plus one leftover
> file**. Matrix Cubed's `MUSIC.DAX` is byte-identical to Countdown's and its own unpacked
> `START.EXE`/`GAME.OVR` never open it by name (0 file-open references against Countdown's 2).
> Matrix scores with Miles/AIL XMI instead: `BUCKA/B/C.XMI` beside the same `FATV9` bank shape DQK
> uses, 21 songs / 5702 events / 95 channel streams. The paragraph above also reads the round-33
> `SOUND.DAX` verdict too narrowly; see round 34's entry for R6's reopening of it.

**Process, since this round's worst moment was mine.** A mutation script computed a replacement span
with `text.index(end)` on a marker that occurs *before* the start marker, producing an empty slice,
so `str.replace("", payload)` inserted the payload between every character of an **untracked** test
file — 1.5 million lines, no git baseline to recover from. The damage was exactly reversible
(`replace(payload, "")`, 31,729 occurrences = len+1, the signature of that bug) and the file was
restored byte-for-byte, but the real lesson is that Phase A's output should have been committed
before Phase B began. It is now. Two later scripts aborted *before writing* on failed occurrence
assertions, which is the pattern that should have been there from the start.

## Three plan-supplied nulls failed, and one of them retracts a shipped headline (2026-09-03, thirty-second)

Same shape as the thirtieth and thirty-first: six Fable-planned agents on one shared tree with
disjoint file ownership, then a serialized Phase B for the files they would have fought over. Plan:
`PLAN-ROUND-32.md`, which now carries its own corrections table.

**The round's real finding is about the planning step, not any one subsystem.** Three separate agents
independently discovered that a null the *plan itself supplied* was worthless, and all three said so
instead of shipping the favourable number next to it:

- **R6** was told to validate a RAM-to-file match against "100 random 32-byte RAM windows map to no
  file span", predicted ~0/100. Measured **55/100**. `GAME.OVR` and `START.EXE` overlay code is
  legitimately resident in RAM verbatim, so a random window matching a file span is the common case.
  Any "found the song buffer at file X offset Y" claim built on that null would have been about a
  coin flip. The song hunt is therefore a clean negative, not a near miss.
- **R3** was told a shuffled block-id mapping would score <= 15% on `(w,h)` agreement. It scored
  **~55%**, because many Amiga/DOS families share dimensions regardless of id. R3 replaced the
  control rather than the conclusion: restricted to discriminating ids (cpic + chead, 144 of them),
  real **100%** against shuffled **~29%**.
- **R5** found the strongest case: round 31's shipped "decisive negative" of **0 of 140** CoAB oracle
  calls landing on Borland prologues was measured against **still-EXEPACK-compressed bytes**. All
  eight Gen1 loaders are genuine Microsoft EXEPACK v1; against the unpacked image it is **66 of 140
  (47%) at shift 0 versus 0 of 140 at +/-1**. **A negative measured through an un-inverted transform
  is not a negative about the data.** Round 31 called it decisive; nothing had established that the
  bytes being searched were the bytes the loader executes. That sentence is now retracted in
  `disassemble.ts`, not merely narrowed as round 31 had already once narrowed it.

The consequence is concrete: `0x29`, `0x2c` and `0x42` move from `unknown` to a measured `wordSet: 0`
in **both** `ECL_GEN1_BUCK` and `ECL_GEN1_MATRIX` -- each justified on its own binary, since
`matrix-ecl-dispatch-map.md` measures all three from Matrix's own handlers under a stated claim
boundary that forbids inheriting from Countdown. Buck's desyncs go 4 -> 2, Matrix's 4 -> 3. R5
explicitly declined to claim the six `0x16`-`0x1b` opcodes it also measured, because the base table
already gives them `wordSet: 0` and measuring them changes no decoded byte -- the
discriminating/free distinction from round 31, applied without being asked.

**R4 rejected its own prediction, and the rejection is worth more than a hit.** It was asked to find
"at least one discriminating opcode the corpus fit got wrong" across Pools, Gateway and Treasures.
It found **zero** -- and explained why the question was mis-shaped. Every disagreement in all three
titles falls in the **free** partition: opcodes where the shipped dialect and the plain alternative
agree with each other while the binary contradicts **both**. A shipped-vs-alternative comparison is
structurally blind to those, which is why R4 had to widen `partition_opcodes`'s desync flag beyond
the discriminating bucket. Round 31's lesson was "name your alternative"; this one is that naming
*one* alternative still leaves a blind spot where both readings are wrong together. Pools' dispatcher
matches the CoAB oracle at 0.9680 (nulls 0.2948 / 0.1497), its parser at 1.0000, and all four cited
handler offsets hold the prefetch idiom with the claimed counts -- so the **docblock was right and the
capability ledger was the wrong artifact**, which is the reverse of the usual direction.

**R4 also retracted an edit by running the VM instead of reading more bytes**, and that exposed a
limit on a metric three rounds have leaned on. A proposed Treasures `0x37` crashed
`treasuresQuestFlag` and `treasuresEndingRoute` with `EclVm.rvalue: undefined operand`, because
**`disassembleEclBlock`'s census only walks each block's first `EXIT`** and never sees subroutine
bytes real quest and combat logic reaches. Every "N of M blocks reach a clean EXIT" number in this
repo -- including round 31's 29/33 for Matrix -- is an under-walk. Bisected, reverted, left open.

**R1's headline number is the one that means nothing, and it said so.** DQK's dungeon combat surface
is transcribed from `DQK.EXE`'s own cluster (dispatcher `0x02cb60`, population `0x02c397`, cell
writer `0x02bcf0`) and 20 of DQK's 21 GEO dungeon areas now fight on a real 50x25 field instead of
the flat 13x9 fallback. But the "1250 of 1250 cells agree with CoAB's builder" result is
uninformative in both directions: **the shuffled-wall null also scores 1250/1250**, because the test
area has no doors. The entire discriminating set is one crafted door cell (527) where DQK writes tile
8 and CoAB tile 2. (R1's own report said 7 and 1; the test it shipped prints 8 and 2, and the test
is what runs -- transcribing the report rather than reading the output would have published a wrong
pair of tile ids in the one place the whole claim rests.) The honest claim, and the one now in the ledger, is "CoAB's routine differing in
one helper branch, evidenced by 1 of 1250" -- not the agreement count, which is the number that
*sounds* like evidence. The plan's own predicted discriminator (the `0x16` window fill) does not
exist: CoAB writes all 1250 cells on any grid >= 13x5. Area 5 is ECL-owned wilderness with no GEO
grid and stays flat, named rather than hidden.

**R2 completed the Amiga palette story and made its one unfalsifiable number falsifiable.** Letting a
>= 32-colour fallback reach 5-plane GLIB sets flips Curse's 2097 EGA-stand-in frames, Secret's 1851,
Gateway's 2894 `NULL`s and Treasures' 1958 to a real `glib-ctab` -- four sets at 100% real palette,
with Pools and DQK proved *unchanged* by deep-equal rather than by inspection. The Gateway oracle is
the round's strongest number: **152576/152576 pixels identical** through the manifest path versus the
shipped route -- on the substitution-candidate frames the shipped mechanism actually touches, which is
the comparison it can make -- against a TITLE.TLB alternative at 33.30% and a shuffled-palette null at
8.66%. Gateway's `Sprit.tlb` is reported separately rather than folded in, because it is entirely
4-plane so the shipped formula never reached it at all: 120/120 frames upgraded, 46.16% of pixels
changing colour. The
guard count is 0 -- and R2 reported that the guard *structurally cannot fire* (5-plane admission
requires capacity >= 32, always covering a <= 31 max index), then forced a real failure anyway with a
4-colour fallback on a 4-plane file, refusing 120/120 frames. Two honest declines kept separate from
the strong numbers: the **Treasures DOS-sibling oracle was refused outright** for lack of any
verified id correspondence, and the **Secret sibling oracle is 20/21 against a shuffled null of
11/21** -- real separation, but nothing like the wall result, and it must not be carried by it.

**R3 shipped the fourth Amiga container format and found a green test that was testing nothing.**
Pool of Radiance's Amiga decoder ports to TypeScript at 426 lines: **843/843 block hashes and
1672/1672 frame hashes** identical to the Python oracle, bit-flip null 0/843, and a hintless sniff
with 23/23 true positives and **0/57 false positives** across DAX, TLB/GLB and DAA, so its
`decodeAsset` branch can safely precede `sniffDaa`. On the way in it found that
`engine_export_consumers.py`'s hyphen-blind format regex made `pool-amiga` -- the first hyphenated
`DecodedAsset.format` the codebase has ever had -- invisible to `FORMAT_REACHABILITY`, which stayed
green while exercising nothing. Reproduced before believing it: the union reads
`['hlib','glib','ilbm','daa','dax']` under the shipped regex and gains exactly `pool-amiga` once the
character class admits a hyphen.

**Phase B corrected the plan's own carried-forward number rather than pasting it.** The plan said the
export audit's blind spot was worth 19 exports and re-pinned at 672. Three of those 19 are names
appearing **only inside comments** (`ItemRecord` and `REFERENCE_DB_DETAIL_ROWS` in `e2e.mjs`, which
imports nothing from the engine at all, and `COK_WALL_SET_ID_BASE` in a `.mts` comment); the genuine
figure is 16 imports. The null that decided how to fix it: across the pre-existing roots, **0 of 925**
consumed exports were consumed only via a comment, so adding comment-stripping moves no existing
number and exists purely to stop the new root importing false positives. `tools/*.mts` was added as a
consumer root; `apps/web/test/*.mjs` deliberately was not.

One claim from an agent was checked and **not** propagated: R3 reported that e2e registration is
"four touch points, not three". The three documented sites are the runners Map, the `await` in
`main()` and `results.unshift` -- R3 counted the function definition, which is the thing being
registered. `CLAUDE.md` is correct as written and was left alone.

All ten Gold Box titles in the WHDLoad pack now have an Amiga manifest; `KNOWN_UNMANIFESTED` is
empty, and the assertion was strengthened rather than merely emptied, since "the gap set is empty"
passes vacuously if the folder glob itself breaks.

**Phase B found a decoder that was right and a router that was not, and the two are easy to confuse.**
R3's Pool of Radiance Amiga port decodes 1672 frames and its golden fixture pins all 1672 hashes
against the Python oracle. The dashboard was showing **744**. Nothing was wrong with the decoder:
`framesFromDecoded` in `loadGame.ts` had no `pool-amiga` branch, so the format fell through to the
DAX catch-all, whose `MULTI_FRAME_KINDS` allowlist admits only `animated`, `vga-compressed-picture`
and `vga-chunky-items` -- and pool-amiga's multi-frame blocks carry `kind: 'standard'`. 928 frames
were hidden across six families: `8X8D` 23 of 774, `SQRPACI` 2 of 128, `BACPAC` 1 of 21, `WILDCOM`
1 of 17, `DUNGCOM` 1 of 13, `RANDCOM` 1 of 4. This is the "solved but unwired" failure in its
subtler form -- the export IS reached, `decodeAsset` DOES route to it, every decoder test passes,
and the product still shows 44% of the content.

**The generalizable check is the asymmetry, not the allowlist.** A new container format has to be
taught **three** independent frame-flattening consumers, and R3 updated exactly one. `nwnPreview.ts`
got a `pool-amiga` branch that walks `block.frames?.length` unconditionally, which is why that
preview showed all 1672 the whole time. `loadGame.ts` (the game dashboard) showed 744. And
`main.ts` — the single-file asset browser — fell through to a catch-all whose multi-frame test is
narrower still (`animated` or `gateway-pic-multiframe` only), so it under-counted the same blocks
AND labelled every Pool of Radiance Amiga file `format: 'DAX'`, which they are not. Both were fixed
this round, each with its own branch. Three views of one decoder disagreeing was a symptom available
for free, and nothing was comparing them. Grepping for the new format string finds one branch and
reads as success; the check that works is enumerating the `decoded.format ===` dispatch sites and
confirming the count. There are three.

The fix is deliberately **format-scoped rather than a widened allowlist**, and the reason is written
into the code: `MULTI_FRAME_KINDS`'s own doc comment records that it encodes a DAX ROUTING DECISION
between two valid readings of the same bytes, and pins `8X8D1` at 6 images for 6 blocks precisely so
the sheet reading cannot be quietly swapped for the tile one. Adding `'standard'` to that set would
be a no-op for DAX today -- DAX emits fifteen kinds and `'standard'` is not among them -- but it
would silently change DAX rendering the first time one appeared. A shared set is the wrong place to
put a fact about one format.

The corrected number was then re-derived through the actual `?game=pool-amiga` path rather than
asserted from the decoder, because this repo has already published a frames-hidden figure that was
**7.5x too big for being computed through a code path the product never takes**. It reads 1672,
which independently matches the golden fixture's 1672.

**The three retracted opcodes moved two censuses, and the pin agent corrected the number it was
given.** With `0x29`/`0x2c`/`0x42` at a measured `wordSet: 0`, Buck goes **4 desyncs -> 2** (21 ->
23 clean) and Matrix **4 -> 3** (29 -> 30), both exactly as R5 predicted. Two things were kept
honest rather than folded into the headline. Matrix's block 18 is **attributed but not closed**:
decoding now runs past the old `0x29` stop at `0x135` and hits a new, later, previously-masked
desync at `0x14b0` -- a site the patch reveals rather than fixes, and counting it as progress would
count the same block twice. And the discriminating share of the 75-opcode Countdown agreement moves
**16 -> 18, not 19**: `0x42` cannot join the extension bucket because it carries a bare
`wordSetOverrides` value with no `opcodeOverrides` mnemonic entry, so the partition helper cannot
read its width at all. The agent found that discrepancy against its own first assumption and
disclosed it instead of taking the rounder number.

**The four-way null broke a tie that was never evidence.** Through round 31, `ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS`
-- a dialect that is *wrong* for Matrix -- scored exactly the same 4/29 as `ECL_GEN1_MATRIX`, and
both test docblocks warned in writing not to read the census as support for the dialect. Round 32
moves Buck/Matrix to 3/30 while Pools stays at 4/29, so Pools now trails by one block. That is
reported as what it is: the tie was not evidence, and its disappearance is not evidence either. The
same non-discriminating null simply reads one apart instead of level.

Gates: engine **241 files / 2767 tests**, `test:corpus` **1432 passed + 1 skipped** (1433
collected), e2e **185/185** (181 -> 185: the four `*-amiga-view` cases), `pnpm e2e:intros`
green, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `build:app` at the two known warnings with **23 manifests**
bundled -- the number the plan predicted. `CLAUDE.md`'s two live counts were re-measured and
corrected (e2e 181 -> 185, corpus 1378 -> 1433). Every new assertion this round was
mutation-tested and watched RED before being trusted.

Two properties of this round's own artifacts, disclosed rather than implied:
`tools/test_decoded_asset_dispatch_sites.py` is a source-structure check -- it proves each site
has a branch, not that the branch is right, and `main.ts`'s branch has **no behavioural test**
because `extractFrames` is private to the app entry and no `catalog.ts` row points at a
Pool-Amiga asset (one would hard-depend on the never-vendored `D:\Games` source). And the seven
`runAmigaManifestView` e2e cases **fail rather than skip** when that source is absent -- an
existing deliberate precedent, confirmed by tracing the helper rather than assumed from the
brief that described them as skipping.


## An adversarial pass broke this round's own headline, and the correction is the result (2026-09-03, thirty-first)

Same shape as the thirtieth: six Fable-planned agents on one shared tree with disjoint file
ownership, then a serialized Phase B for the files they would have fought over. Plan:
`PLAN-ROUND-31.md`, which now carries its own corrections table.

**R2 answered a warning instead of inheriting it, and then the warning's replacement had to be
corrected too.** Round 30 measured Matrix Cubed's `GAME.OVR` at `FBOV` — Curse of the Azure Bonds'
overlay magic, not Countdown to Doomsday's `TPOV` — and wrote into three artifacts that
`ECL_GEN1_BUCK` must NOT be assumed to transfer. R2 obeyed that and tested it: a dispatch map built
from Matrix's own binary came back **field-for-field identical to Countdown's**, 0 disagreements. A
different overlay magic did not imply a different script dialect, which is exactly why it had to be
measured rather than assumed in either direction. `ECL_GEN1_MATRIX` ships in `disassemble.ts` as
**its own literal, not `= ECL_GEN1_BUCK`** — an alias would have made R2's deep-equal pin a
tautology, the defect class round 30's probe audit was built to find, one round earlier.

Then a read-only adversarial pass was run against that claim, and it landed a hit. It confirmed the
load-bearing facts from the bytes — the three magics read directly; no circularity in how
`map_matrix_ecl_dispatch.py` locates the dispatcher (the search is seeded only from the CoAB oracle,
and Countdown's report is computed separately and consumed only for the side-by-side); the
similarity winner as the unique global maximum over 564 candidate Borland-prologue functions
(0.8885 against a mean of 0.0648 and a runner-up of 0.2583); 33/33 blocks carrying the `0x1388`
magic and the fifth far pointer at vaddr `0x8014`; the census reproducing 29/4/0 with exact offsets.

**But "53 opcodes agree on a concrete value, 0 disagree" states an agreement without naming the
alternative it beats.** The alternative is *"Matrix follows the plain Gen1 base table"*, and
Countdown's dialect never diverged from that base on most opcodes, so agreeing there costs the
alternative nothing: 56 shared opcodes carry the same width under both. **16 of 75 discriminate** —
8 override deltas Matrix's own handlers measured concretely (`0x27` alone jumps from base 8 to 2)
plus 8 beyond-`0x40` extensions the base table has no row for — and Matrix matches Countdown 16/16.
`0x3c` is the near-miss that fixes the arm at 8 and not 9: this dialect overrides it (base 1 to 0)
so it *looks* discriminating, but Matrix's own `0x3c` handler is `no_far_call` and measured nothing.
The discriminating set has to be intersected with the measured set, and a test now pins that
intersection so it cannot be quietly widened back.

**Same pass, second correction: the corpus census is not evidence for the dialect.** 29 of 33 blocks
reach a clean EXIT under `ECL_GEN1_MATRIX` — but plain Gen1 scores 26/7 on the same blocks, and
`ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS`, a dialect that is *wrong* for Matrix, ties at exactly 29/4. The four-way
null in the test file already recorded this; the published headline did not. Both corrections went
into `matrixEclDialect.test.ts` (two new tests that compute the partition rather than restate it),
the `disassemble.ts` docblock, the ledger, `supportClaims.json`, the `?ecl=matrix` docs entry and
the R2 memo, in the same pass. One thing the adversarial pass raised that does NOT stand: it noted
16 different `headerLen` candidates pass a "produces a legal first opcode" test. True and
irrelevant — `headerLen = 2 + 5*4 = 22` is pre-established Gen1 geometry shared by every Gen1
dialect, never fitted.

**The `?ecl=matrix` route nearly reproduced a bug its own neighbouring comment records.** The first
draft of `GAMES.matrix.blockIds` was `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. Block 1 is one of Matrix's four desyncs (stops
at `0x66e`) and blocks 3 and 4 are not in `ECL1.DAX` at all — a desync sample read as an existence
list, which is precisely what the `buck:` entry three lines above warns about having done, one
round after it was written down. Prose warnings did not prevent it; a test does. The route also
found a real bug on the way in: an absolute `{repo-root}/matrixcubed_extracted/...` path
403s, because the dev server's local-game bridge allowlists only `D:\Games` and the GOG root. The
manifest's own repo-relative form works in dev and in the already-bundled production copy.

**R1 partially retracts round 30's negative — and the desync count still does not move.** Round 30
reported that following Buck's three unmeasured opcodes into relocated segments failed: the best
linear `seg:off -> file offset` fit landed 9 of 103 CoAB oracle calls. R1 shows that negative was
framed too widely. The linear fit really does fail, but a non-linear resolver the codebase already
had for descriptor/stub-owned far calls resolves **3 of the 7 targets** (`0x1e0f2`, `0x1e98e`,
`0x2d9cd`), calibrated on the same oracle at **229 of 240** against a uniform-random null that
averages 0.72 and never exceeded 6 in 3,000 trials. The two findings are compatible: round 30's
negative is true of linear fits, which cannot describe a descriptor/stub lookup. What did NOT
change is the thing that would have mattered — every resolved chain ends in unread resident code,
all three verdicts stay `unknown`, the dialect table is untouched and the census stays at 4 desyncs.
An address you can name is not an address you have read. Round 30's "only `0xbe4`/`0x653` are
unresolved" is now scoped to these seven targets; Buck's binary has 16 distinct unresolved segments.

**R4 is a numbered negative and `glib.ts` is unchanged.** 305 of the 799 members of DQK's Amiga
`8X8DB`/`8X8DC` decode to degenerate 8x1 stubs. R4 built a pure-Python leaf walker that prints each
member's own `dm`/`wb`/`h`/body-length next to the DOS twin's real dimensions, and tested whether
any `(nplanes, variant)` byte-budget hypothesis computed from the DOS oracle is satisfiable by the
stub's stored bytes. **None fits any of the 305.** The decoder was left alone rather than tuned
until the numbers moved. The 305 are still counted as frames in the new DQK Amiga manifest, because
that is what they decode to — 76 are blank on the DOS twin as well and 229 are the mirror half the
Amiga master omits — and the manifest, the docs entry and the e2e pin all say so, so a later
decision to stop counting them would be visible rather than silent.

**R5's three standing audits, and the plan's estimate was off by more than 40x.** The plan predicted
`KNOWN_UNCONSUMED` — `index.ts` exports nothing outside their own module references — would be 16.
It is **692**. That was cross-checked rather than taken on faith: known-wired exports (`decodeAsset`,
`loadGame`, `EclVm`, `Explorer`) all correctly report consumed, ruling out a blanket regex failure,
and an independently written pre-existing sweep corroborates the order of magnitude by a different
code path. Phase B then shrank it to **691** by wiring one of them, and the audit reported that as
`fixed (shrink the set)` — an audit that can only detect breakage is half an audit.

**R3 shipped `?import=pools` and `?import=treasures`, and found a disclosure gap in its own memo.**
Pools imports 5 of 6 pregens, Treasures 6 of 8, and the two outliers are shown rather than smoothed:
ABAGAIL and OUGO come back `classLevelAgrees: false` with the disagreement stated. The memo
documented those two oracle misses but never mentioned that `createCharacter` rejects BINKY and
CHERROD outright for unrelated race/class-cap violations, and that SMOKE is excluded by the 6-hero
party cap — three rejections for two different reasons, none of them the oracle disagreement they
would be mistaken for. All three now appear in the docs entry and the e2e assertions.

**R6 landed three Amiga GLIB manifests and declined three.** `dark-queen-amiga` (23 files, 1497
frames, 100% under a real embedded palette), `pools-amiga` (24, 2599, 82.9%) and `curse-amiga` (27,
2209, **5.1%** — the other 94.9% render under a synthetic EGA-16 stand-in, which the docs entry says
in those words). Secret, Gateway and Treasures were staged but not landed: 86-88% of their frames
render with no palette at all. Each landed manifest got a `GAME_IDS` row in the same pass — a
manifest not in that list is reachable from no menu, the exact "solved but unwired" failure this
repo has already had with four finished manifests — plus a `loadGame()`-level pin separate from the
byte census that produced the numbers, and an e2e case comparing the dashboard's rows as a sorted
multiset. Multiset and not positional on purpose: the dashboard groups by category so DOM order is
not manifest order, and Curse ships two rows both labelled `8X8D (shared tiles)`, holding 65 and
1260 frames, which a name-keyed lookup would score against each other.

Gates: engine 2723, `test:corpus` 1378 (+1 skipped), e2e **181/181** (175 -> 181: `ecl-matrix`,
`import-pools`, `import-treasures`, and the three `*-amiga-view` cases), `tsc --noEmit` clean, build
at the two known warnings with 19 manifests bundled. Every new assertion this round was
mutation-tested and watched RED before being trusted.

## Six items, and the round's best result is a failure that was reported instead of rounded off (2026-09-03, thirtieth)

Same shape as the twenty-ninth: six agents on one shared tree with disjoint file ownership, then a
serialized Phase B for the files they would have fought over. Plan: `PLAN-ROUND-30.md`, which now
carries its own ten-row corrections table, because ten of its predictions met a measurement and
several lost.

**R4 spent the round trying to close Buck Rogers' last four ECL desyncs and did not close one.**
That is the headline on purpose. The three opcodes whose word set cannot be read from their own
handler (`0x29`, `0x2c`, `0x42`) all stop at far calls into relocated segments, so following them
needs a `seg:off -> file offset` mapping. The brief required that mapping be calibrated on Curse of
the Azure Bonds FIRST, where an oracle names the true target of every call — 103 distinct call
pairs from 52 real handler bodies. The best of nine candidate multipliers landed **9 of 103**
(8.7%), under the round's own `>= 10` bar, and its winning constant did not generalize. So no
address from that attempt appears in `disassemble.ts`, the census stays at `{desync: 4,
cleanExit: 21}`, and the negative is what shipped — into `buck_far_targets.py`, the research doc,
the ledger's gap sentence, the support claim, the `?ecl=buck` docs entry and the inspector docblock,
all in the same pass. The round's one evidence-backed opcode, `0x31 SHORT_MENU`, landed normally.
(Round 31's plan opens by claiming this negative is wrong and that 3 of the 7 targets resolve
through stub geometry. An independent read-only adversarial pass was run at the end of this round
and reproduced (a)–(f) exactly from the bytes: the calibration is NOT circular — `0x1ca15` was
originally found by scanning all 603 Borland prologues in Buck's overlay and matching instruction
shape against CoAB's oracle-named `@parse_command_sub`, a path that never touches descriptor/stub
tables, and Buck's bytes there are identical to CoAB's for the first 8; and 229/240 is not a density
artefact — oracle function starts occupy 0.31% of the span, a uniform-random null over 3,000 trials
means 0.72 hits and never exceeded 6, and perturbing the one free structural parameter resolves
ZERO targets rather than fewer. The two findings are compatible, not contradictory: round 30's
negative is true of linear fits, which cannot describe a descriptor/stub lookup. So the retraction
is justified for exactly 3 of the 7; the other 4 sit on resident segments and stay unresolved. One
correction the pass demands before it lands: "only `0xbe4`/`0x653` are unresolved" must be scoped to
these seven targets — Buck's binary has 16 distinct unresolved segments overall.)

**A probe audit found six weak probes, called them five, and the miscount is preserved.** R5's
census is the first systematic pass at "assertions that cannot fail" after three rounds of finding
them by accident. All six are replaced against measured values, and `test_e2e_probe_audit.py` was
watched RED across the change (5 failures) before going green. Its own "five" is left standing in
the file with a note, because an audit that miscounts its subjects is precisely the error it exists
to catch.

**Two of R5's proposed fixes were themselves wrong, and only measuring caught it.** It pinned the
ECL route's opening block to 34 — but 34 is where `next()` LANDS; the route opens block **18** at
vaddr `0x8014`, so pinning both would have made the assertion permanently false. It also asserted a
"terminating EXIT row" in a listing that is a fixed 13-row window centred on the PC, where no EXIT
is reachable from the head of a block. Replaced with decoded content pins, then mutation-proven:
flipping `SAVE`'s wordSet 2 -> 3 collapses the listing to 3 rows with a spurious `GOTO`, which the
old `blockId >= 0 && lines.length > 0` guard would have passed happily.

**One "weak overlay check" was weaker than described: the object did not exist.**
`runFruaHeirsRoute` read `!window.__combat?.isOverlay?.()`, and `window.__combat` is `undefined` at
both negative checkpoints — `!undefined` is `true`, so it asserted nothing. Its null is the route's
own positive branch, which waits for `isOverlay() === true`: with an intact MONST.GLB the hook IS
installed. So "never installed at all" is the discriminating statement, and that is what is pinned.
Nearby, `runNwnLibraryGameView` captured `headerText` and `statusText` and asserted neither — a
dead assignment reading as coverage. It renders exactly 0 with a specific reason, and both the
number and the reason are pinned now.

**Secret of the Silver Blades imports 5 of 6, and the missing hero is the interesting part.** The
plan predicted 6/6. MALACHITE, the party's only multiclass, is refused — for a fully located chain:
Secret's race byte reads 6, which is not a value in Curse's Race enum, so the race defaults to
human, and this ruleset implements the manual's non-humans-only multi-class rule. The unsolved race
enum is therefore not a cosmetic disclosure; it costs exactly one character. The e2e case pins the
count AND the rejected name two-sided, so if Secret's own race table is ever found and byte 6
resolves demihuman, the case goes red and whoever solved it has to come back and restate the number
rather than quietly gaining a party member.

**"0 discriminating pairs each" for Pools and Treasures was a threshold artefact, not a wrong
count.** Full n-of-n agreement really is still 0 for both and stays 0 on re-measurement. What was
never reported beside that 0 is the (n-1)-of-n tier: at the same two-field oracle Curse's own loader
rests on, class byte `0xae` + `ClassLevel[8]` window `0x151` scores 5/6 on Pools and 7/8 on
Treasures, and that clears a shuffled null built for the honest alternative ("how high can ANY pair
score by chance") rather than the null that only ever restates the zero. The two misses are reported
as misses; each is the sole example of its own anomaly, and no predicate built from n=1 can be
checked against a null without circularity.

**`?module=1` was a URL the app wrote and never read; now it is a route.** Round 29 pinned it as a
defect rather than documenting a link that did not work. `boot()` now restores the last module from
IndexedDB, re-validating the stored bytes through the ordinary text-import path rather than trusting
them. The new `module-url-reload` case carries its own null — after deleting the database the same
URL must mount nothing and say so — and was mutation-proven by disabling the arm. Its two waits use
interval polling, not puppeteer's default `raf`: the restore runs a long synchronous parse that
starves rAF callbacks and made a 20s wait time out on a module that had in fact mounted.

**Matrix Cubed is the ledger's thirteenth profile, and the detection claim it inherited was wrong.**
`profiles.ts` called it `dos-ega`; the plan called that "more likely wrong than right" and
two-sided, and the bytes falsified it — it is `dos-vga`. The DOS release was extracted once into
git-ignored `matrixcubed_extracted/` (58 files, 7 folders, 27 `.DAX`, exactly as predicted); the
source archive on the external drive is untouched and nothing auto-extracts. It landed atomically:
manifest, `PROFILES` wiring, ledger profile (**107 insertions, zero deletions** — the hand-format
survived again), `GAME_IDS`, `DETECTED_TO_MANIFEST`, docs entry, e2e case, support claim. Its
`web_level` moved `missing -> preview` because the corpus DERIVES that level, not because anyone
asserted it. The dashboard renders **685** frames across 19 art rows, all pinned as an exact set so
a new file cannot ride along uncounted — including the zero rows, since a data file that starts
rendering as art is exactly what those pins are for. Two rows differ from Countdown without
explanation (`8X8D1` 12 vs 2, `SPRIT1` 69 vs 3) and are pinned as observed rather than rationalized.

**A count was right for the wrong reason.** The plan predicted the ledger's evidence total would go
`77 -> 77 + 3..4` from Secret's work. It went to **91**, and none of the +14 is Secret's — all of it
is Matrix Cubed's profile; the Secret importer cited zero new evidence paths. A bare total cannot
catch that; the area histogram beside it (rewritten from 21 area-level rows to 33, across 6 areas
and 3 profiles) can.

**Two regressions were found by the full suite, and neither was in the file its author was
working on.** R4's brief said its opcode work must not touch any other dialect constant in
`disassemble.ts`; it added `0x31 SHORT_MENU` to `ECL_GEN1_BUCK` and **deleted the identical entry
from `ECL_GEN2`**, so DQK lost `SHORT_MENU`. `explore-dqk` went red with area 4's event text
changing from the expected `/SUPPLIES/` line to "SUDDENLY, A GROUP OF SWARTHY SAILORS...". It was
confirmed a regression rather than a pre-existing red by stashing and running the case on HEAD
(PASS), fixed, and pinned two-sided: a new test in `buckEclDialect.test.ts` asserts BOTH dialects
carry the entry, and removing `ECL_GEN2`'s again produces exactly one engine failure.

**And `?module=1` becoming a live route silently changed what `page.reload()` means.**
`frua-heirs-route` died at a 30s wait with every flag false. Bisected by reverting files to HEAD one
at a time: `library.ts` alone was innocent, `main.ts` alone reproduced it. `onLibrarySelect` has
always written `?module=1` with `replaceState`; now that boot reads it, a bare reload restores the
module instead of landing on the Library, so `.lib-entry` never appears. All six reloads in that
route are documented in their own comments as "a genuinely fresh import" / "discards the in-memory
runtime" — they meant *boot from scratch* and were relying on a query being inert. They are now
explicit `page.goto(BASE + '/')` calls with the reason recorded above them. This is the second-order
cost of fixing round 29's write-only URL, and it is the kind of change that cannot be found by
running the one case you edited.

**That fix was not the whole blast radius, and the second victim proves a green run is not a
clearance.** `greyfen-reference-campaign` failed on the NEXT full pass — with "Node is detached from
document" and `persistence=false` — in the same way, at its own post-victory reload. It had passed
in the run that found `frua-heirs-route`, on identical application code: whether the restore fires
also depends on whether an earlier case left a module in IndexedDB, so the failure is
order-dependent and one green suite does not clear it. Rather than fix a third case later,
`test_e2e_probe_audit.py` now carries the rule as a standing check — a function that mounts a module
(`.lib-entry` or `window.__module`) may not call `.reload()` unless it is in
`RELOAD_ALLOWED_IN_MODULE_CASES` with a written reason (`runModuleUrlReload`, where the reload IS
the assertion, and `runLibraryBootCompanion`, which reloads on `?create=1` before any module
exists). A second test fails the allowlist if an entry stops reloading, so it shrinks on fixes
instead of quietly granting a pass to nothing. It has its own planted null, and it was mutation-
proven on the real file: turning one `goto` back into a `reload` makes it red. Its first run also
caught it firing on the comments that explain it, which is why whole comment lines are stripped.

**Open, and deliberately not done.** Buck's 4 desyncs stand, two still UNATTRIBUTED, and the mapping
needed to attribute them is now known to be unfit rather than unattempted. Secret's race enum is
unsolved and costs MALACHITE. `explore-pool-holy-symbol-quest` still classifies "weak" — for a
limitation of the classifier (shape 2 condemns a case for containing any uncompared hook call,
including `waitForFunction` waits that DO fail by timeout), not a surviving vacuous probe;
narrowing that definition changes what the audit means and needs its own round and its own null.
Matrix Cubed has a manifest and a profile but no ECL dialect: `ECL_GEN1_BUCK` is Countdown's,
verified against Countdown's own binary, and is not assumed to transfer.

## Six items, three of them corrections to claims this project had already published (2026-09-03, twenty-ninth)

Same shape as the twenty-eighth: six agents on one shared tree with disjoint file ownership, then a
serialized Phase B for the seven files they would have fought over. Plan:
`PLAN-ROUND-29.md`, which carries its own prediction table — and which this entry has to correct in
four places, because four of its predictions were wrong and the measurements won.

**The twenty-eighth entry's closing claim was wrong on both halves, and I wrote it.** It said
`describeProvenance`'s "mixed" branch "has engine-level coverage only" and that DoK had been "the
only browser exemplar". Measured: `dungeonWallGraphicSet.test.ts` contained **zero** `'mixed'`
assertions at that commit — the string did not appear in the file — so there was no engine-level
coverage either; and `?explore=pools*` / `?explore=gateway-amiga` do mount partially-Amiga GLIB
sets, so a browser exemplar existed the whole time. Both halves false.

But the plan's replacement prediction (`art: mixed — Amiga (3), DOS-EGA (2) of 5 categories`) was
**also** wrong, and the real answer is more useful than either guess: **neither route produces a
mixed badge at all.** Pools reports ONE uniform category (`wall bricks (shared bank)`) because its
`8X8D1.DAX` block 1 is a DoK-style 256-tile single bank that collapses symbol sets 1-3; Gateway
reports THREE uniform ones because `LOAD_PIECES #3,#3,#3` decodes the same block three times with no
`singleBank`. Boot/UI sets 0 and 4 never enter either route's DOS key space — blocks 202/203 live
only in the `framePath` archive, which the wall-tile source never merges in — so there is no DOS-EGA
category available to mix with. Both semantics are now pinned in the engine from synthetic sets, and
both routes pin their exact provenance arrays in the browser.

**The two e2e probes that "covered" this could not fail.** Both read
`if (!provenance) errors.push(...)` — satisfied by any truthy value, including a wrong per-category
split. That is the third round running in which a green assertion turned out to be unfalsifiable, and
it is the same failure mode as `__combat?.open?.()` and the never-run packaged suite. Both are now
asserted on the exact structured array.

**Buck's ECL dialect: the corpus was overruled by the binary, twice, and the sweep says so.** R6
attributed 6 of the 7 known desync sites to one cause — dispatcher opcode `0x4c`, handler
`GAME.OVR:0x363b`, one of eleven Buck-only entries beyond Gen1's `0x00-0x40` ceiling. Census moved
`{desync: 7, cleanExit: 18}` → `{desync: 4, cleanExit: 21}`. The number that matters is not that
one: **a pure corpus fit would have reported `desync: 1`.** Sweeping `0x4c` over wordSet 0..8 gives
`{0:1, 1:2, 2:4, 3:7, ...}`, and the binary-verified value is 2 — more than four times worse by the
naive metric. `0x43` is starker: its binary-verified `wordSet 1` is **tied for the worst value in
the sweep**. Both were taken from the handler's own `mov al,N; push ax; lcall 0xb8,0x2a` prefetch
anyway, and both sweep tables are published next to the result. This is the `0x21` trap met head-on
rather than optimised away. Two sites (`ecl6#94@0x50`, `ecl6#99@0x2c0`) are left explicitly
**UNATTRIBUTED**, not guessed.

**Buck Rogers finally has a capability profile — and a gate that would have noticed it didn't.** The
ledger carried 11 profiles while Buck shipped two manifests, an Amiga set, a binary-derived dialect
and two browser routes, disclosing none of it. It is now the twelfth (108 insertions, **zero**
deletions — the hand-format survived, unlike two earlier `json.dumps` round-trips). More durable
than the profile: `tools/test_capability_ledger_coverage.py` pins PROFILES ↔ ledger ↔ manifests as
exact sets. It was watched RED between landing the profile and emptying `KNOWN_MISSING`, so it is
known to bite. The one remaining shortfall is real and pinned: Matrix Cubed, whose manifest is
`None` because it lives inside a `.7z` policy does not auto-extract.

**"A `?query=` URL is not a menu entry" now has a two-sided gate, and the drift was 20x the
estimate.** The carried-forward note said two `?import=` routes were undocumented. Measured: **41**
undocumented routes and **1 phantom** — a documented route the code cannot serve. `?combat=demo` was
a mnemonic no code path ever writes (the dispatcher ends in a catch-all else-arm), so the docs entry
now reads `?combat=1`, resolving the phantom and one undocumented route at once. Phase B documented
36; the set is now **4 undocumented, 0 phantom**, and the four are deliberate: three are default-arm
aliases whose documentation would make the page longer and less true, and one, `?module=1`, is a
genuine defect — `main.ts` writes it into the address bar with `replaceState` but
`params.get('module')` appears nowhere, so reloading or sharing that URL does not reproduce the view.
It is pinned as a defect, not documented as a feature.

**The plan's own null was wrong and the agent refused to chase it.** R2's brief predicted "exactly 89
`DEMOS` flags". The file had **80**. The brief also said "if your regex finds a different number, the
regex is wrong" — and the correct move was the opposite: verify by hand, pin the real number, report
the plan as wrong. It did. Tuning an extractor until it reproduces a predicted constant is how a
measurement becomes a restatement of its own prediction.

**CoAB's cross-title null is a standing test now, and the raw version of it was nearly meaningless.**
The four counts (6/6 CoAB, 1/6 Secret, 0/6 Pools, 0/8 Treasures) are pinned in
`coabSavedCharacter.test.ts`. Along the way R3 found the unfiltered offset sweep returns ~600
"full agreements" for Curse, not the predicted 1: byte value 0 is a valid `cleric` code, so any
constant-zero window trivially agrees across a 6-record party. Requiring the class byte to actually
vary — the property that makes CoAB's own oracle non-trivial — collapses Curse to exactly its two
known real offsets, which is the calibration that makes the rest trustworthy. Secret's own offsets
are `0x6c`/`0x111`, and they are **not** a single contiguous insertion relative to Curse's
`0x75`/`0x109`: the class byte moves 9 bytes earlier and the level array 8 later, with only the
17-byte gap growth matching the record-size delta. Proven a property of the bytes, not the tool, by
injecting a real 17-byte insertion into Curse records and watching the sweep track it to one
consistent `k`. Pools and Treasures give 0 discriminating pairs — a negative reported with its own
null and its nearest miss.

**21 stale DQK coordinates, out of a stated denominator.** R4 re-derived every coordinate claim on
the eight non-square GEO areas under the (height, width) stride fixed 2026-08-07: 126 raw matches,
103 unbindable, **26 classified — 21 STALE, 5 CORRECT**. The square maps are the null and returned
zero stale, as a transposition-invisible-on-squares argument requires; mutating the stride flips the
non-square bucket cleanly 4/18 → 18/4. The upstream misnaming still in the tree
(`goldbox_corpus.py:538` read `width, height = raw[0], raw[1]`) is corrected — harmless where it sat,
since the two are only multiplied, but it is exactly what a later reader copies into a coordinate.
**No accomplice was invented this time:** last round the same task attributed the bug to a
`geo.ts` comment that does not exist and it reached a commit message. This round's audit quotes file
and line for every stale claim and says "unknown" where it does not know.

**A gate caught me.** My own `docs.ts` edit shipped a broken string literal — an escape that did not
survive a scripted replacement. `pnpm test:corpus` passed 1257 tests directly alongside it; only
`tsc` failed. Worth remembering the next time a green suite feels like enough.

**Pre-existing and benign, flagged so nobody re-diagnoses it:** `pnpm test:corpus` prints a
`Windows fatal exception: access violation` C-stack dump from `unicorn.mem_map` in
`tools/test_unicorn_gateway_pic.py`. It is present on `a63efc6` before any of this round's edits, the
process survives, and all 5 tests in that file pass.

**Deployed** to https://dionysus.dk/greybox/ , bundle `assets/index-2a0Ofrvp.js`, matching
`apps/web/dist-app/index.html` exactly; root and hashed bundle both HTTP 200. Verified against
production, not just locally: the two strengthened provenance routes
(`explore-pools-graphics-switch`, `explore-gateway-amiga-graphics-switch`) 2/2, `ecl-buck` 1/1 —
which is the live proof that `?ecl=buck` now opens `ecl2.dax` rather than the `ecl1.dax` the docs
claimed — and the intro suite 10/10. One build note worth recording so it is not re-investigated: a
clean `rm -rf dist-app` rebuild reproduces the identical bundle hash, so the hash is deterministic
across this round's `docs.ts` edits rather than a stale artifact.

**Open, and deliberately not done.** `?module=1` is written but never read back — the fix is to make
`boot()` read the flag, not to document it. Buck's 4 remaining desyncs stand, two unattributed; 11 of
his extension opcodes carry `uncertain: true`, and `0x42`/`0x2c PARLAY` were disassembled and left
unmeasured because their handlers call far routines this pass could not identify. Only `0x0c` of the
dialect's own overrides is reached by the corpus at all (twice), so the override table's authority
remains the binary. No importer was built for Secret despite now knowing its offsets. Matrix Cubed
remains the ledger's one genuine gap.

**Gates on the committed tree.** Engine 231 files / 2,657 tests. `pnpm test:corpus` 1,257 passed /
1 skipped (up from 1,230 — the round added the ledger-coverage, route-documentation and Secret-sweep
suites). `tsc --noEmit` clean across the monorepo. `pnpm build:app` clean at its two documented
tolerated warnings, bundle `index-2a0Ofrvp.js`. Full browser harness **172/172** — unchanged total,
since this round strengthened existing assertions rather than adding cases. Intros 10/10. The two
strengthened provenance probes were mutation-tested at the browser layer after the full pass, by
