## Method-25 byte +6 is closed: the engine never reads it (2026-08-24, seventh)

The last open field in the HLIB composite record, and the last item on the known-issues list. §5a
had it stuck for a good reason: `compositeWidth % sourceWidth == 0` in 71/71 parts with ratios
`{2: 62, 1: 9}` is predicted *equally well* by "an independently authored canvas width" and "a value
the tool derived from the source width", and 16/16 regions is the entire corpus — no held-out case
exists to break the tie. Correctly, nobody guessed.

Settled from `DQK.EXE`, the same place `dest_x` came from. The draw routine at `0x01984C` loads the
slot header into `[bp-0x12]`, so +6 is `[bp-0x0c]` and +7 (method) is `[bp-0x0b]`. It dispatches on
`method & 0x0f == 9`; the method-25 arm (`0x198A7..0x19890D`) reads only the 6-byte record buffer at
`[bp-0x0a]`, and `[bp-0x0c]`'s **sole read in the whole function** is at `0x1990F` — the `jne`
target, i.e. the ordinary raster branch. The epilogue reads nothing. The byte cannot affect drawing.

The corpus then agrees, once asked about content rather than about the source: the declared width
**exceeds** what the parts occupy in **14 of 16** regions (exactly 2x in 12), equals it in 2, and is
never smaller. DQK `FRAME.TLB` ptr 20 declares 16 pixels for fifteen 8x8 tiles all at `dest_x = 0`.
And per part the byte is always the **source's own** width byte or twice it — 71/71, including the
`22 -> 44` case — so it tracks the source, not the composite.

**This was also a live correctness question, not only a documentation one.** `renderHlibComposite`
sizes its canvas from the parts; had it trusted byte +6, 14 of the 16 shipped composites would carry
dead columns, including an 8-pixel blank stripe down a DQK screen border. Pinned by a falsifiable
probe in `hlib.test.ts` (23 cases): swapping the renderer to `composite.widthByte * 4` turns it red
— verified by doing it — and restoring turns it green. Written up as `docs/hlib-format.md` §5b.


## TOPVIEW's "undecoded member region" was a palette record all along (2026-08-24, sixth)

The asset viewer and `docs/hlib-format.md` both carried DQK `TOPVIEW.TLB` as *20 images + 1 member
region undecoded*. There is no undecoded region. Those 8 bytes — `01 00 00 00 00 00 00 18` — are a
well-formed colour table declaring `ncolors = 0`, i.e. **"inherit the caller's palette"**, which is
the same fact `hlib-format.md` had already recorded in prose ("TOPVIEW carries no palette") without
the reader ever acting on it.

The bug: `iterLeafImages` decided "is `ptr[0]` a colour table?" by asking whether `readPalette()`
returned non-null. That function returns `null` both for *not a colour table* and for *a colour
table with nothing in it*, so the empty record fell into the cpic-style "then `ptr[0]` is an image"
branch, failed to decode (`width = 0`), and was filed as raw bytes. The previous test pinning this
spelled the byte out in its own comment — `drawMethod 0x18 = 24 = a colour-table magic with 0
colours` — and still asserted the region was undecoded. Reading a byte correctly and routing on it
are two different things; that gap is the actual lesson here.

Fixed by routing on the cmagic byte at `+7` (`isColourTable()` in `loaders/hlib.ts`), which is what
the mid-leaf branch already did. Also made an empty mid-leaf table `continue` rather than fall
through, and made `isCapturedElsewhere` accept colour tables, so nothing well-formed can be reported
as undecoded again.

**Safety measurement, because this branch is the one that would drop a real picture.** Across every
DOS HLIB container held (DQK + FRUA, 52 files, **435 TILE leaves**): the palette slot holds a
colour table in **435 of 435**, **0** leaves are cpic-style, and only **2** tables are empty — the
DQK and FRUA copies of `TOPVIEW.TLB`. The "image at `ptr[0]`" branch is therefore taken by nothing
in this corpus; it is retained rather than deleted, since removing an unexercised branch is an
unverified change, not a simplification.

**Two doc claims corrected in passing** (`hlib-format.md` §1a, new §2b). "`cpic` combat icons store
no palette" was wrong twice over: `CPIC.TLB`/`COMSPR.TLB`/`CBODY.TLB` are `magic == 1`, so they
never used the `magic == 0` branch attributed to them, and they carry **partial** palettes
(`first_col`/`ncolors` = 144/112, 64/32, 96/48) that patch a slice into the loaded palette. The
conclusion that they reuse DUNGCOM/WILDCOM was right; the stated mechanism was not.

Evidence: `packages/engine/test/hlib.test.ts` (22 cases) — the corrected TOPVIEW assertion, a
**mutation null** (set the cmagic to 0x17 and the region is reported undecoded again, so the probe
can fail), and a repo-wide sweep asserting no shipped image container leaves a member behind. That
sweep was red before the fix.


## The CoK race byte is not findable from the bytes we hold (2026-08-24, fifth)

`recalcThiefSkills` needs a race row and has never had one, so every character still gets eight
zeros for thief skills. This was an attempt to close it, and it closed as a measured negative
instead — which is worth more than another inconclusive round, because it says what to stop doing.

Found, and pinned by `tools/test_cok_start_tables.py` (with a stride null): CoK's `START.EXE`
carries the character-generator enum orders as fixed-stride length-prefixed string tables — race at
`0xC625` stride 16, alignment at `0xC69F` stride 17, deity at `0xC738` stride 12. The race table
holds only the **six demi-human races**; `"Human"` sits outside it in the adjacent menu-item list
next to `"Monster"`, so a plain 0..6 index is not automatically the encoding.

Not found, and now known to be unfindable this way: the race byte itself. Filtering all 409 offsets
(plus nibbles) by "every record's abilities must be legal for the race this byte selects", anchored
on SIR STRONGSWORD being a validated Knight and therefore human, leaves **62 of 409 byte offsets**
standing — including offset 0, the first letter of the name, and the ability scores themselves. A
filter that accepts the name as a race field is measuring nothing. Six records against seven races
with overlapping ranges cannot separate anything, and DoK's 28 records do not rescue it: that party
is maxed, every ability 18, so the range filter has exactly zero power there. **More records is not
more evidence.**

One near-miss is recorded so nobody re-finds it: offset 90 passes and reads beautifully (Human for
the Knight, Kender for the DEX-19 thief). It is the class code, already validated three independent
ways. It reads well for the same reason 61 other offsets do.

The decisive experiment is external and already known to work: read race off the retail MODIFY
CHARACTER screen for all six pregens under DOSBox-X via the focusless GameLink protocol — the same
capture route that produced the class-code label on 2026-07-27. Six labels turn an unconstrained
search into a lookup. Full writeup: `docs/engine/research/cok-character-record-race.md`.


## The `.QSV` stride is solved, and the answer is that there is no stride (2026-08-24, fourth)

The known issue the entry below deliberately left open is closed. A DQK `.QSV` roster record is
`0x1A1` fixed bytes, then `17 * byte[0x08]` inventory entries, then 9-byte affect nodes until a
6-byte NULL-pointer terminator. `walkQsvRecords()` parses it forward with no scanning at all.

It has **no stored length** — which is why no length formula was ever going to be found, and the
old negative therefore stands, explained rather than overturned. The node count is stored nowhere:
a byte-by-byte search across 57 records matches no offset, and neither does any of the 56 rotated
assignments. Re-running the original exhaustive `fixedLen + c1*byte[a] + c2*byte[b]` search while
tolerating a 0/1 residual — so `MONCHA`'s even-padding could not be the thing hiding the fit, the
most plausible reason the first search missed — still returned zero.

The evidence is two independent methods agreeing, not one method succeeding: the arithmetic walk
reproduces every boundary the content scan finds, **12 of 12** DOS saves, **69 records**, and they
share no predicate. Both are kept. Perturbing any single ingredient of the walk (fixed span 416 or
418, item stride 16 or 18, node stride 8 or 10, terminator 4 or 8, item count from `+0x07`, `+0x09`
or `+0x19F`) collapses the agreement to 1/12 — and that survivor is the party-of-one save, whose
only record start is fixed and so passes any tail model, so it is reported as noise, not as a hit.

Two things recorded here earlier turned out to be wrong in opposite directions, and both are
corrected in place:

- The inference that "something variable-size sits *inside* the record and shifts every later
  field" is **retracted**. The same-character diff that motivated it was showing stats changing
  between snapshots, not a shift. The appended-tail model that had been rejected was correct — it
  was rejected on the wrong evidence.
- The `[0xFF, 0|1, 0, 0, 0, 0]` sentinel that was demoted to "a lead, not a finding" because it fit
  only 45 of 58 records **was** the finding: it is the list terminator, two data bytes then a NULL
  far pointer. The 13 misses differ only in those two data bytes.

Also found on the way: the two bytes at `0x40D` are a little-endian party-size word duplicating the
header byte at 31 in all 13 corpus files — the test that rules out "the bytes before a record belong
to the previous one", and the only offset in the preceding 16 that does it.

The record's own pointer fields corroborate the layout, and one of them settles a live objection.
`+0x09/+0x0A/+0x0B` are zero in all 69 records, which is what rules out "byte 0x08 is just the low
byte of a far pointer" — a segment cannot be zero. And the word at `+0x06` is the segment of every
affect node in that record (57 of the 58 records that have nodes), the **only** offset in the whole
416-byte fixed part that does it: the record points into the very heap block its nodes live in. The
one exception is the party-of-one save, whose `+0x00..+0x07` pointer block is zeroed and whose
"nodes" are `FF` filler — the same save that already disagreed with its own header.

The Amiga-native variant is now partially mapped, and deliberately not claimed as solved. Its node
is 10 bytes with a 32-bit big-endian pointer at node+4, stepping by 10 across a shared pool exactly
as on DOS; every record ends immediately after its last node, so `704 + 10 * nodes` reproduces all
four measurable lengths (724, 764, 734, 724). But the split of that 704 into fixed part plus item
array is under-determined — `0x1A0 + 18x16` and `0x1B0 + 17x16` both fit, `byte[+0xC9]` is 16 in
every record, and one file cannot separate them. It needs a second Amiga save.

A lead was retracted on the way, which is the part worth remembering: "byte 15 of each item entry
holds the next entry's first byte" looked convincing on the Amiga record and would have picked the
`0x1A1`/18 split. Tested against DOS, where the item count is known independently, it holds in
**1 of 57** records — chance. The rule that saved it was cheap: a structural claim discovered on the
platform you cannot check should be tested on the platform you can.

Still **not** solved: the Amiga-native 8188-byte variant's record start. Its `+0x08`/`+0xC9` mirror
disagrees and its pointer fields are 32-bit big-endian 68000 addresses stepping by 10, not 9 — the
same structure word-aligned for a 68000. `walkQsvRecords()` returns `null` for it rather than
guessing; the scan still reads it. See `docs/engine/research/dqk-save-format.md` §5.


## The last unwired capability, and a pin that objected on its own (2026-08-24, third)

`./loaders/dqkSave.js` was one of the two genuine entries the new reachability sweep flagged: the
whole DQK `.QSV` family -- header, resume area, lead-character name, and the roster scanner --
decoded, tested, and called by nothing in `apps/`. It is wired now, as a roster view in the asset
browser rather than as artwork, reached by the catalog's explicit `kind: 'dqk-save'`.

Two things the view refuses to smooth over, because they are the most interesting things the
decoder knows:

- **The record stride is unsolved.** Deltas run 508..788 bytes and an exhaustive search for a
  MONCHA-style count formula returns zero exact fits across 58 records. Records are found by
  scanning for three simultaneous signals, and the panel says so rather than implying a walk.
  *(Superseded the same day — see the entry above. The stride is solved; the formula search's
  zero remains correct, because the record has no stored length to find.)*
- **The header's party-size byte and the scan's record count are printed separately**, with an
  explicit note when they disagree. One shipped save claims a party of 1 and yields two records
  both named CALDOR.

`renderExtracted()` returns the number of frames it blitted, which for a roster is zero -- so the
view returns the record count instead, and the e2e case asserts 6 records rather than 6 images.
That case was checked by removing the routing and watching it go red, not by watching it pass.

**The reachability pin added an hour earlier objected without being asked.** Wiring the module made
`EngineModuleReachability` fail, because `./loaders/dqkSave.js` was still in its expected-unreached
set. That is the behaviour wanted: it complains in both directions, not only when something falls
off the product. Twelve modules remain, six of them the DOS rebuild track by design.

## Making the unwired-work sweep repeatable, and what it found (2026-08-24, later)

Four solved-but-unwired formats in three days is a pattern, not a coincidence, so the ad-hoc grep
became `tools/sweep_engine_reach.py`. It walks from the names `apps/` imports out of
`@goldbox/engine`, follows engine-internal imports, and reports what it never arrives at.

**Getting it to tell the truth took four corrections, each of which had it confidently wrong:**

1. **JSDoc counted as usage.** `dqkSave.ts` says `{@link readQsvRoster}` in its own comments, so a
   function with zero callers read as internally used. Comments are stripped now.
2. **A module counted as its own consumer.** Every file contains the names it defines, so nearly
   everything landed in `engine-internal` -- 983 of 1578 exports, a number that meant nothing. With
   the defining module excluded it is 285.
3. **Following the barrel's `export ... from` lines marked all 184 modules live.** The re-export
   list *is* the barrel; only code genuinely defined in `index.ts` contributes dependencies.
4. **...but excluding the barrel entirely reported `./loaders/ilbm.js` as dead** -- a format the
   asset browser renders every day, whose only path is `decodeAsset`, which lives in `index.ts`.

Corrections 3 and 4 are the same mistake in opposite directions, which is why the gate carries a
null for each: one asserts ILBM/DAX/GLIB are reached, the other asserts the sweep does *not* reach
everything. A fifth bug was pure slapstick and worth naming because it was invisible: a patch wrote
`` into the regex as a literal **backspace character**, so `import` became `^Himport^H` and
matched nothing. The tool cheerfully reported "0 seeded by an app import, 0 reached" -- a probe that
could not succeed, presented as a finding.

Verdict: **171 of 184 engine modules are reachable from the product; 13 are not.** Six are the DOS
rebuild track and have no web consumer by design. Two are real: `./loaders/dqkSave.js` (the whole
DQK `.QSV` family -- decoded, tested, no app caller) and `./ruleset/addnd1e/thiefSkills.js`. The
module-level half runs in 0.4s and is now a gate with the set pinned and each entry carrying a
reason; the name-level half takes 87s and stays a report.

## The thief-skill mapping was not unresolved, it was unread (2026-08-24)

Chasing why `recalcThiefSkills` has no caller turned up a documentation defect rather than a wiring
one. The module transcribed all three COAB tables correctly but declared both row-index mappings
unknown -- "offsetting by the AD&D 3..18/19 range is a guess, not a verified fact." The routine's
own use sites answer it outright: `ovr026.cs:543` is `unk_1A243[player.stats2.Dex.full, skill]` and
`ovr026.cs:532/539` is `unk_1A230[(int)player.race, skill]`. **The Dex row is the raw Dexterity
score, with no offset at all**, and the race row is the game's `Race` enum ordinal. There was no
offset to find.

Corroborated independently, because one line of decompiled C# is thin evidence: read as
"row = Dexterity", the AD&D landmarks land on the row numbers their scores name -- row 9 is exactly
the published "Dexterity 9 or less" row, rows 13..15 are the all-zero band, rows 17..19 climb. The
null matters here more than usual: rows 13..15 agreeing is worth nothing on its own since they are
all zero, so the test also asserts rows 8 and 10 do *not* match row 9's signature.

Three shipped deviations from the rulebook, recorded not corrected: rows 0..8 are not the "9 or
less" row (a Dex-8 thief takes no penalty at all); row 10 has -19 for Pick Pocket where AD&D has
-10; and rows 20..21 are past the table's end -- 99s and 18s that a magically boosted Dexterity
would index. Every legitimate row stays within +/-20, which is what separates them.

This resolves COAB and does **not** unblock Krynn: CoK's Dragonlance races are a different, larger
enum than COAB's, so `recalcThiefSkills` still has no caller. The difference is that it is now a
blocked item with a named blocker instead of an oversight, and the reachability gate records it as
such. Every character the engine creates still gets `thiefSkills` as eight zeros.

## The C64 reaches the screen, and the measurement that contradicted its own comment (2026-08-24)

Fourth and largest instance of the solved-but-unwired pattern: `c64Picture.ts` has been
golden-tested since the C64 arc, the project holds **49 disk sides across seven titles**, and
`apps/web` contained the string "c64" **zero times**. Six pictures are now in the asset browser
(CoK `PIC70`/`PIC72`/`PIC79`, DoK `PIC71`, Gateway `PIC7C`/`PIC7E`) with three e2e cases, staged
into git-ignored `c64_extracted/` by `tools/c64_disk.py --extract` rather than by pulling the
`.d64` reader into `src/`, which stays out deliberately. Files are renamed `.PRG` because Vite
500s on extensionless paths.

**The comment I wrote was wrong, and measuring it is what showed that.** A C64 picture ships
glyphs `$40..$FF` only; codes `$00..$3F` come from a separate 514-byte `CHARSET`. The natural
claim — "without it every low-code cell draws as garbage" — is false for two of the three titles.
Decoding each picture twice, once with the real charset and once with an all-zero one, and
counting differing pixels of 36,480:

| picture | owed to `CHARSET` | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cok/PIC70` | 0 | 0% |
| `cok/PIC72` | 18 | 0.05% |
| `dok/PIC71` | 0 | 0% |
| `gateway/PIC7C`, `7D`, `7E` | 14,848 each | 40.7% |

`$20` is the blank glyph in both charsets, so cell count predicts nothing: DoK's `PIC71` has
**165 low-code cells and a footprint of zero**. Gateway's three share one footprint exactly —
`232 * 64 == 14848`, a single glyph code `$1C` in 232 byte-identical cell positions spanning all
15 rows and all 38 columns, i.e. a border drawn from a resident glyph. The engineering rule
survives even though the premise didn't: a missing companion must still fail loudly, because the
one case where it matters loses 40% of the image while rendering one plausible-looking frame.

Worth stating plainly: the first version of that test shipped **invented numbers** — three
per-title ratios I had not measured, written as "Measured 2026-08-23". It failed on first run.
Every figure above is now asserted exactly by `packages/engine/test/c64-picture.test.ts` tier 3.

**A hazard only the production build could see.** `bundle-assets.mjs` scrapes `catalog.ts` with a
case-sensitive `/path:/` regex. `companionPath:` does not match it, so all three `CHARSET` files
were left out of `dist-app` while their pictures were copied in — the deploy would have failed
loudly on every C64 asset. All six gates were green: the dev server serves the repo directly, so
nothing short of a real build touches the bundler. Fixed, and guarded by
`BundledCatalogCompanions` in `tools/test_goldbox_corpus.py`, which extracts the bundler's *own*
regex from its source and applies it to the catalog, with a null asserting the pre-fix pattern
misses every companion.

That makes two distinct blind spots found in two days with the same shape: a real capability with
no path from the app to it, and a check whose passing was uninformative. Gates: engine 2517,
corpus 1158, `tsc` clean, e2e 160/160, intros 6 games.

## Three more decoders that ran for nobody (2026-08-22, third pass)

Having found one solved-but-unwired format that morning, the obvious question was how many
others there were. The answer was three, all in the same afternoon, and one of them had been
sitting there for five weeks.

**`decodeAsset` never learned to sniff GLIB.** The Amiga big-endian sibling of HLIB has decoded
correctly since 2026-07-18, but the byte-sniffing dispatcher tested HLIB, ILBM, DAA and DAX and
stopped. Every Amiga container from the DQK-and-later generation answered `unrecognized container
format` from any caller on the generic path — the asset browser, `loadGame`, the NWN preview.
`explore.ts` imported `decodeGlib` directly for the Amiga wall-art routes, so those were green
and nothing pointed at the hole.

Sweep after the fix: **152 GLIB files across six distinct titles — Curse, Secret, Pools of
Darkness, Gateway, Treasures, Amiga DQK — 13,884 images, 0 throws** (177 / 16,483 counting the
German Pools pack, which duplicates the English one).

Adding the union arm made `tsc` reject three fallthrough branches that had been treating "not
hlib/ilbm/daa" as "must be dax". The compiler found them; no reading did.

Two nulls, because *"it was broken"* needs one as much as *"it works"*:

- For every real GLIB sample, `sniffHlib` / `sniffIlbm` / `sniffDaa` / `sniffDax` are **all
  false**. Nothing else was quietly taking these as the wrong format — they genuinely had no arm.
- Perturb byte 0 from `G` to `X` and `sniffDaa` **accepts** the file; it decodes as DAA. Nothing
  real hits that path, but it pins why the dispatch order is load-bearing rather than cosmetic:
  DAA's sniff is structural and will claim a GLIB-shaped file given the chance.

Both behavioural tests fail with the GLIB branch removed; the two structural nulls stay green,
as they must, since they assert properties independent of the dispatcher.

**The asset browser still called method 25 unsupported.** It printed *"draw method 25 —
known-unsupported variant; cell sized but pixels may be incomplete"* over every composite. That
note outlived the problem by a few hours: the record layout came out of `DQK.EXE` that morning
and `renderHlibComposite` has assembled them correctly ever since, with nothing calling it. The
browser now renders them — `FRAME.TLB` 40 images + 3 composites, `PICC.TLB` 47 + 4 — and
`dqk-picc`'s e2e minimum moved 47 → 51, so a regression to the old behaviour fails rather than
passing under a slack bound.

New catalog entries make all of it reachable by a human and not only by a unit test: an Amiga
GLIB group (the three files already bundled for the graphics switch, so no extra payload), plus
`FRAME.TLB` and `TOPVIEW.TLB` — the only two DQK containers whose members are not all plain
images.

**The corpus gate caught yesterday's own repair.** `_js_focused_block_lines` decides which e2e
registrations are *not* live code, and it anchored on `if (ONLY.size > 0)`. Hoisting the runner
registry out of that block — done so the full pass could check itself against it — moved the
registrations outside the anchor, and a case registered but never awaited started reading as
live again. That is precisely the hole the predicate exists to close, reopened by the fix for a
different hole. The exclusion now follows the `const runners = new Map([` declaration, which is
where it belongs, and gained a null of its own: the awaited call in `main()` must **not** be
excluded and the region must be under half the file, so an over-broad repair fails.

Gates: engine **2513**, corpus **1155**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, browser harness **157/157** with
all 156 selectable cases confirmed running in the full pass, intros all ten titles.

**The pattern worth carrying forward.** Three finds in one day, all the same shape: work that was
finished, verified, and connected to nothing that would notice if it broke. A passing unit test
proves a decoder is *correct*; it says nothing about whether anything *calls* it. The cheap check
is to ask, of any newly solved format, which app code path reaches it — and if the honest answer
is "the test", that is not done yet.


## The solved format that never reached the screen, and two gates that could not go red (2026-08-22, later)

Three things landed after the four-silent-decoders round above. None of them is a new format; all
three are the same shape of problem — **work that was finished and verified, but not connected to
anything that would notice if it broke**.

**The Amiga `*COM` backdrops now reach the combat screen.** The strip format was solved earlier this
day and the loader decoded it correctly, but nothing in `apps/web` ever asked for it:
`loadCombatAssets` hardcoded the DOS `.DAX` paths, so switching graphics mode to Amiga changed the
walls and left the combat backdrop on DOS EGA art. `combatBackdropFrom` now dispatches on the decoded
container format, and `CombatAssetPaths` carries `amigaDungcomPath` / `amigaRandcomPath` /
`graphicsMode` threaded from `gameData` through both of `explore.ts`'s `launchCombat` seams.

The bank substitution is asymmetric on purpose. A first draft did
`randcomPath = wantAmiga ? paths.amigaRandcomPath : dosRandcom`, which loads an Amiga second bank
where DOS loads none — 31 tiles against 25, and every shared index past the first bank pointing at
different art. The Amiga bank is substituted only where the DOS side already had one.

Parity, measured rather than assumed (refinement `1 − H(DOS|Amiga)/H(DOS)`, null = the same statistic
against a shuffled DOS bank):

| Game | Bank | Items | Refinement | Null |
| ---- | ---- | ----- | ---------- | ---- |
| CoK | DUNGCOM | 25 / 25 | 1.0000 | 0.1317 |
| CoK | WILDCOM | 35 / 35 | 0.9178 | 0.1086 |
| CoK | RANDCOM | 6 / 6 | 0.8978 | 0.0915 |
| DoK | DUNGCOM | 25 / 25 | 1.0000 | 0.1317 |
| DoK | WILDCOM | **45 Amiga vs 38 DOS** | 0.8520 | 0.1302 |

DoK's Amiga `WILDCOM` is a **superset, not a twin** — seven frames the DOS bank has no slot for. That
is recorded in the test rather than smoothed over, and it is the one pair a naive index-for-index
swap would corrupt.

**The e2e gate had a case registered that never ran.** `cok-combat-amiga-backdrop` went into the
`GB_E2E_ONLY` runner registry but not into the unconditional full run in `main()` — two
hand-maintained lists. `GB_E2E_ONLY=cok-combat-amiga-backdrop` ran it; the full gate did not; the
total stayed at exactly the documented 150 and nothing went red. The lists had already drifted the
other way once before, which the source comment above `gswitch` records.

The full pass now ends by comparing the ids it actually produced against the registry keys, and
**always emits a result** rather than only speaking up on failure — `all 151 selectable cases also
run in the full pass  rendered= 151 (>=151)`, so the number is readable instead of silence that looks
identical whether the check ran or not. It was not written and assumed green: **its first run failed
at 145/151**. Two of the six it named were genuine; the other four were an id-spelling split, where
the registry key is the `GB_E2E_ONLY` selector but the case returned a camelCase id (`demoCombat`,
`titleMenu`, `charedDok`, `titleMenuIdleTimeout`, `feared-party-autoflee`) — so a targeted rerun and
the printed report disagreed about what a case was called. That first failure also showed
`printResults` truncates errors to two entries, which hid four of the six ids.

Full pass afterwards: **152/152**, including a case that had never executed before.

**The C64 GCR oracle turned a shared gate red for a reason unrelated to GCR.**
`test_gcr_decoding_matches_c1541_byte_for_byte` spawned one `c1541 -read` process per file — about
130 of them, each with a 120s deadline. Under load during a full `pnpm test:corpus`, one blew its
deadline and the `TimeoutExpired` escaped as a test error. c1541 accepts a chained command sequence,
so the side now reads in a handful of processes (32 files per invocation, well inside the Windows
32KB argv limit): **9.04s → 0.76s**. The deadline is now caught and skips with "the oracle did not
run" — the test already carried a note that an oracle which did not run must be reported as an oracle
failure and not as a disagreement, and a timeout is exactly that case. Checked against its null:
hashing `read_file(...)[:-1]`, one byte short, still fails the batched form.

Gates at the end of the round: engine **2509**, corpus **1155**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, browser
harness **152/152**, intros all ten titles composing.


## Four silent decoders, and the last unsolved Krynn graphics format (2026-08-22)

Five findings landed this round. The common thread is not a format — it is that **four separate
decoders were reporting success while producing or discarding garbage**, and every one of them was
green under "does it throw?" testing.

**The Amiga `*COM` combat backdrops are solved.** `DUNGCOM` / `WILDCOM` / `RANDCOM` are not N
independent 24×24 items; they are **one strip** — a single virtual image `N·24` px wide × 24 tall,
5 contiguous bitplanes whose row stride is word-aligned across the **whole strip**
(`rowBytes = ceil(N·24/16)·2`), 73-byte preamble, 2 trailing bytes, item `t` at pixel columns
`[t·24, t·24+24)`. It is the already-solved `8X8D` convention generalised from 8 px to 24 px. Six
earlier sweeps missed it because every one assumed a per-item stride — and because `parseFrameHeader`
*succeeded* on these blocks (`height=24`, `width_div8=3` is a perfectly ordinary header) and returned
a plausible-looking, entirely wrong raster. Verified against the DOS `*COM.DAX` oracle at refinement
`1 − H(DOS|Amiga)/H(DOS)` = **1.0000** for CoK and DoK `DUNGCOM`, item-permuted nulls **0.19 / 0.18**.
Four other metrics were tried first and none discriminated: NMI on single items (0.275 vs null 0.430),
25×25 assignment (0.158 vs null 0.851), horizontal smoothness (flat), partition agreement (0.577 vs
0.588). My own first answer — preamble 75 — was *uniform across all four files* and still wrong; the
sweep picked 73. The positive control that exposed it was a bug in my own BIGPIC1 check.

**`decodeGlib` was discarding 437,680 of 439,671 bytes** across twelve shipped Amiga libraries and
reporting them fully decoded, via three bare `continue`s. Fixed by threading an `undecoded` array out
to callers. This would have bitten the Gateway/Treasures content port silently.

**`@1033` in a DQK `.QSV` is `LOAD_FILES` operand 2** — `DQK.EXE`'s handler at file offset `0x0420ac`
writes it, and each area's entry script opens with a self-referential `LOAD_FILES #<own area>, #n`.
18 hits / 0 misses across 30 retail saves; the null matters here and is stated in the test: `1` is the
modal operand, so only area 66's `5` is discriminating on its own.

**A `.QSV` carries its party inline**, and the record reuses `MONCHA`'s layout — leader's name at
`1039 + 0x68` in all 28 standard 7965-byte saves, `1030 + 0x68` in the Amiga-native one. The offset
scan behaves like a field: 104..107 all 28/28, 108 → 12/28, 103 → 0/28. The **stride is not solved**
and is pinned as such — transitions measure 506..733 bytes and `MONCHA`'s tail formula fits none of
hundreds of thousands of candidate triples — so the reader exposes record 0 only and refuses to walk.

**Two overclaims were withdrawn rather than defended.** Six docs, including the declared-authoritative
`findings.md`, described the HLIB `TILE` palette as a 6-bit DAC table; it is full 8-bit RGB, and one of
those docs would have written every converted Amiga colour into DQK at quarter brightness on roadmap
step 5. And an agent's "method 25 horizontal placement solved, ratio 1.692" did not survive: the ratio
came from a global `imgNNN → pointer index` map, and FRUA `PICD.TLB` has 29 sets that each restart
their own numbering, so the sources being divided were not the sources being composed. Re-resolved per
leaf it is an exact integer ratio, 71/71 parts, `{2: 62, 1: 9}` — a real measurement that still does
not say where a part lands. Status stays **unsolved**.

Worth carrying forward, and it is the 2026-08-08 lesson in a different costume: **a decoder that
returns something is not a decoder that works.** "Every Amiga `.DAA` file decodes" had stood since
2026-07-18 and was false for three files the whole time. The claim only became testable when it was
checked against an independent oracle instead of against itself.

## P6 reference campaign closed; two host suites were passing without testing (2026-08-08)

BUILD-QUEUE item 20 is complete. `the-greyfen-beacon.gbmod` — 1,503 bytes, sha256
`b5fdc35e…3b7c1077` — is byte-identical across Author export, browser import and packaged Electron
import, and all four acceptance surfaces pass: `pnpm e2e:author` 8/8, the engine goldens, the
browser `greyfen-reference-campaign` case, and `pnpm --filter @goldbox/electron e2e:packaged` 2/2.

The interesting part is what closing it required. Three of the four surfaces were already green;
the packaged one had simply never been run against a built `.exe`, and when run it could not work
at all. `page.waitForFileChooser()` needs Chrome's `Page.fileChooserOpened` event, which the
packaged Electron browser process does not emit — it serves `<input type=file>` from its own native
dialog — so the import click opened a modal nobody could answer. Past that, `page.click()` gates on
`isIntersectingViewport`, whose IntersectionObserver callback never fires for a window the packaged
app never composites, so every control click hung until protocolTimeout rather than failing an
assertion. Both now use the same public renderer path the dev-tree Electron suite already used:
`uploadFile` into `#module-input`, and the element's own `click()` behind an explicit visibility
assertion. Only the OS dialog and puppeteer's implicit viewport check are bypassed.

The same session repaired the DoK campaign leg, which had a matching problem in a different shape.
`window.__combat.open()` does not exist — the seam is `isOverlay()` — so every `__combat?.open?.()`
probe was permanently undefined. In `settleTravelEvent` that disabled the combat branch outright, so
the leg only reached Cekos on runs where no overland random encounter happened to fire; in
`dok-campaign-consumed-refired` and Electron's `refired` it silently made the assertion vacuous.
Neither dialogue drain had a `combat`-kind arm either, so an unhandled turn re-pushed the same line
until its guard expired. And the town walk answered Cekos's descriptor-11 street brawl with choice
0: that arm offers JOIN / SNEAK PAST / LEAVE, and both JOIN and SNEAK PAST run
`LOAD_MONSTER #33,#12,#33`, so the leg fought 12 SIVAKs four steps short of the encounter it exists
to prove. With those fixed the web case's own roster expectation turned out to be wrong as well — 6
where the retail arm loads 15 — a number that had never been reachable. `gameData.ts`'s description
of descriptor 11 as "a verified silent no-op arm" is corrected in the same commit: re-derived from
`ECL1.DAX#34`, the prompt fires for every memory state, seed, facing and `initial_entry` arm tried.

Worth carrying forward: a passing gate is not evidence until the probe it rests on has been shown to
be capable of failing. Four separate assertions here were green because their probe returned
`undefined`, and one whole suite was green because it had never been executed.

## DQK `ending` leg closed — every detected profile now passes the campaign gate (2026-08-07)

DQK's `ending` was the corpus's last `blocked` campaign leg, held through two prior investigation
rounds by one finding: nothing in the 47-area ECL corpus ever writes `[0x0032]` nonzero. The
finding was correct; the conclusion drawn from it was not. `[0x0032]` is not a story flag at all.
DQK.EXE's ECL operand resolver intercepts address `0x32` in a class-0 special-address table
(`25a4:0897`, values at `DQK.EXE` file `0x040BB3`) and dispatches it to `25a4:099c` = `a0 f3 c9`
(`mov al,[0xc9f3]`) — the wall type of the map edge the party faces, recomputed from the GEO planes
by `2f0d:0628` on every move and every turn. Its *write* path is a different table
(`25a4:06d2`, `0x0409E8`) with no entry for `0x32`, so the four corpus `SAVE #0,[0x0032]` sites are
dead stores against a byte the read path never consults. "Never armed" was structurally guaranteed
and beside the point.

The cross-check that settles it without trusting any disassembly judgement: the same table maps ECL
`[0x002d]` → `[0xc9f4]`, and `0x002d` is the Gen2 `cellDescAddr` this project established years
earlier from an unrelated direction — pinning `[0xc9f0..f4]` = X/Y/facing/wallType/cellDescriptor,
the same 5-tuple already located for DoK. And the ending never read `[0x0032]`: area 66 dispatches
on `AND #0x7F,[0x002d]->[0x009B]`, and arm 14 (`0x9D18`) is gated only on the `[0x00A0]` step
counter before `GOSUB 0x9F03; NEWECL #67` — ECL #67 being the finale, Takhisis on a burnished
throne before the portal. Arm 14's cell is the only descriptor-`0x8E` cell, 38 steps from area 66's
landing pose `(6,21)`. Anchored in `packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts` cases G and H,
including a negative control for the transient `(29,21)` animation pose, which sits in a 110-cell
region that cannot reach the ending at all. Static/byte-only; no DOSBox-X evidence is used or
implied. Full derivation: `research/dqk-0032-writer.md` §8.

**DQK is promoted `persistent` → `campaign`; all 11 detected profiles now pass the campaign gate.**
Two real bugs fell out of the verification and are fixed in the same commit `dc12cd1`: Gen2 GEO
header order is `(height, width)`, not `(width, height)` — proven from `2f0d:0628`, which clamps X
against `es[buf+1]-1` and indexes `es[buf+1]*Y+X`, corroborated by all 8 non-square retail maps
scoring higher wall-edge symmetry under that order (mean 0.877 vs 0.660, 8/8) and by area 66's own
ECL writing `X=29`, out of range under the transposed reading — **8 of the 20 DQK maps were being
transposed**; and the Gen2 operand-code table is `{1,2,3,0x80,0x81}`, not the `{1,2,3,0,0x81}`
previously recorded in `disassemble.ts` and `decompile-dqk-ecl-dispatch.md`.

Gates: 2,389 engine tests across 211 files; workspace TypeScript; 141/141 browser e2e; all ten
intro compositions locally and against production. Atomic bundle `assets/index-DzTaIxHM.js` is live,
root returns HTTP 200, and the live HTML names the same hashed bundle as the local build. Commits
`dc12cd1` and `c59aa20` are pushed.

Follow-up `c59aa20` unblocked `pnpm corpus --strict`, which had been failing at
`map_coab_oracle.py` with "expected one CoAB retail layout, found 2". The second layout was this
repo's own packaged Electron output — the asset bundler copies every absolute retail path under
`release/win-unpacked/resources/web-dist-app/assets/external/`, so packaging Electron made each
install discoverable twice — plus `apps/electron/tmp/external-cok-corrupt`, a deliberately damaged
CoK fixture, being discovered as a genuine install. Discovery now skips `release`, `web-dist-app`,
and `tmp`. Regenerating produces no diff in any tracked artifact, so the duplicate broke the tool at
runtime without corrupting committed outputs. `pnpm corpus --strict` exits 0.

**Next boundary.** The campaign gate is now universally satisfied, so the ladder's remaining rung is
`Verified`, which needs two declarations per game in `tools/goldbox_corpus_routes.json` and
`tools/goldbox_capabilities.json`: a selected-folder release contract covering all 13 checkpoints

## Electron retained-source isolation release candidate (2026-07-31)

Electron folder access no longer depends on one process-global mutable root. Every successful
native scan returns a random opaque `sourceId` owned by the invoking renderer; only the main process
retains its canonical root and normalized scanned-file allowlist. Detection magic reads, full-file
gameplay assets, and FRUA imports each close over that immutable id, so selecting source B cannot
retarget a Library entry backed by source A. A renderer-destroyed hook removes every capability it
owned, and foreign or forged ids fail closed.

Every read now requires an allowlisted relative file and checks both lexical containment and the
file's current canonical path. This rejects ordinary `../` traversal as well as a directory swapped
for an escaping junction after scan, while a legal filename such as `..notes.dat` remains readable.
Prefix lengths must be non-negative safe integers; zero reads zero bytes instead of accidentally
returning the full file. The renderer never receives an absolute selected root.

The arbitrary-path `pickFolderForTest` IPC handler and preload property are registered only when the
owning process has exact `GOLDBOX_ELECTRON_E2E=1`; the corresponding web test seams are omitted too.
Both launchers scrub inherited spellings of that variable before choosing their mode. The same
fresh portable executable passes an ungated phase proving the properties absent and a gated phase
proving real native CoK detection. The dev harness separately proves two-folder isolation, forged-id
rejection, lexical and canonical escape rejection, legal leading-dot names, prefix validation, and
source-A gameplay after source B. Focused FRUA acceptance also passes through the new id-bound path.

## 1. What this is

**Greybox** = an all-in-one Gold Box **engine + authoring suite** (web now; offline Electron
later) that plays any Krynn-trilogy game from the user's own assets, with the sibling
**PRIMARY native goal** of two DOS executables (CoK & DoK rebuilt on the DQK/HLIB engine
with the superior Amiga art). See `../../CLAUDE.md` for the full charter and the three-games
table (CoK 1990, DoK 1991, DQK 1992 = the target engine).

- **Repo:** `{repo-root}`, branch **`greybox`** (PRs target `master`).
- **Monorepo (pnpm):** pure logic in **`packages/engine`** (consumed as **TS source** —
  `package.json main = ./src/index.ts`, there is **no dist build**); browser app in
  **`apps/web`**; deploys to **https://dionysus.dk/greybox/**.
- **Live surfaces today:** the asset browser + per-game demos behind URL flags
  (`?play=cok`, `?explore=1|dok`, `?combat=1`, `?dqk=1`, `?intro=1`, `?mainmenu=1`,
  `?demo=1`, `?audio=1`, `?import=cok`, `?gswitch=1`, …) and a **project docs/status page
  at `?docs=1`** (`apps/web/src/ui/docs.ts`).

---

## 2. How the loop runs

A self-perpetuating `ScheduleWakeup` loop. Each wakeup re-fires this exact prompt:

> goldbox full-auto loop: open docs/engine/BUILD-QUEUE.md, take the top unchecked item,
> build it end-to-end per the ORCHESTRATION quality gates (tsc + vitest + e2e + build +
> deploy + commit), check it off with a one-line result, update ROADMAP/memory, then
> schedule the next iteration. Recreate all three Krynn games and all their systems. Don't
> wait for user input.

**Per-item Definition of Done (all must pass before checking off):**

| Gate | Command | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| Typecheck | `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| Engine tests | `cd packages/engine && pnpm exec vitest run` | green (**1698+**, growing — as of 2026-07-17) |
| E2E | `node test/e2e.mjs` **run from `apps/web`** | **106/106** (as of 2026-07-17, growing) |
| Build | `pnpm build:app` | succeeds |
| Deploy | atomic deploy (see §4) + `curl https://dionysus.dk/greybox/` | live **200** |
| Commit | required trailers (see §4) | pushed to `origin/greybox` |

Then: check the item off in `BUILD-QUEUE.md` with a one-line result, prepend a line to its
"Done (newest first)" list, add a `ROADMAP.md` entry, append a block to the
`goldbox-build-loop` memory, and `ScheduleWakeup(~1200s)` with the loop prompt verbatim.

**Engine-infra slices** (no web surface change — most E-phase items) still run all gates; if
`build:app` produces the **same bundle hash** the site already serves, a re-upload is a no-op
— confirm live 200 and say so, don't pretend there was a web change.

### CoK M4 combat-init bug, round 16 — no-patch WORKAROUND round: the MONCHA data-side fix is EMPIRICALLY REFUTED, and §13.4's "stale pointer" id is CORRECTED (the id is ECL-computed); root cause reframed as ECL-interpretation drift (STATIC ONLY, no DOSBox-X, 2026-07-22)

**User decision (2026-07-22, the premise of this round):** the user does **not** want a permanent
on-disk `DQK.EXE` patch ("that goes against the goal of this engine ... just use the game's assets");
they asked for "a way around it." Charter: pin the arithmetic, find a **data-side** reshape of ported
CoK content that keeps DQK's combatant-setup routine in bounds; only if data-side *provably* can't work,
fall back to a removable runtime-only in-memory poke (never touching the on-disk EXE) and flag it.

**Results (full writeup: `cok-m4-fidelity-plan.md` §24):**
- **Arithmetic pinned to the byte.** New harness probe (`2177:2665` = phys `0x033dd5`) dumps the
  0x288-byte staging buffer at the cursor-init: the runaway loop count is `staging[0x19F] = 115` (0x73).
  Buffer 648 bytes, record header 0x19E (414), 17-byte sub-records → safe count ≤ ~13; 115 overruns ~3×.
- **§13.4 CORRECTED.** The id `0x81de` is **not** a stale DGROUP shop-string pointer — it is
  `(byte[0xae6b]<<8)|byte[0xb186]`, two bytes written by an **ECL-stream bytecode interpreter** at
  `2033:0343` walking the loaded ECL script (`[0xae5c]+[0xb7f9]`). Live-confirmed: `ae6b=0x81`,
  `b186=0xde`. The value is *computed* from ECL, not left over; §13.4's "stale pointer" was a coincidence.
- **MONCHA data-side fix EMPIRICALLY REFUTED** (decisive, cheap, no DOSBox-X): modified a scratch
  `MONCHA.GLB` to add a bounded (0x1C0-byte, 0x19E/0x19F=0) member AND an id-table entry `{0x81de → it}`,
  rebuilt, re-traced — the harness confirms it loaded the modified file (`7155` bytes, up from 6695) yet
  `staging[0x19F]` stayed **byte-identical at 115**. The overflow count is **not sourced from any ported
  monster/encounter record**; the staging buffer at the crash is garbage from a failed id lookup.
- **Reframed root cause:** an **ECL-interpretation defect** — DQK's VM walking CoK's ported ECL computes a
  bogus monster id → no matching MONCHA member → garbage staging buffer → 115-count overflow. This is the
  roadmap's hardest phase (ECL operand/opcode drift), out of this bounded round's scope.
- **No fix implemented** (zero-forced-fixes rule kept): the preferred data-side reshape is refuted; a
  count-clamp runtime shim would only convert the crash into a *garbage* encounter (not faithful), so it
  is **flagged for user review, not built**. Baseline undisturbed (`cok_m4_static_verify` ALL PASSED).
- **Decision memo (for the user):** (a) reshape monster data — REFUTED; (b) the faithful fix — correct the
  ECL so the VM computes a sane id (hard, multi-round, unpinned this round); (c) removable runtime bounds
  poke — possible, leaves EXE on disk untouched, but not faithful (garbage encounter) — flagged only;
  (d) accept as a known isolated gap (standing §23.6 position). Harness probe added; `--smoke-test` PASS.

### CoK wall-art placeholder residuals CLOSED — 15/15 playable areas now carry real CoK wall art; the 7 "placeholder areas" fully diagnosed (STATIC ONLY, no DOSBox-X, 2026-07-22)

Bounded follow-up to commit `c801066`'s honest "7 areas stay on the placeholder": diagnose each of
the 7 and convert the closable ones. Outcome: **both actually-affected areas (66, 97) converted**;
the other 5 turned out to have no wall header at all (never were placeholders), so **every playable
CoK area — 15/15 — now stamps real CoK wall art** in `build/cok-dqk-release`.

**Diagnosis of the 7** (recursive-descent disassembly of every CoK ECL block's full subroutine
graph — all 5 far-pointer entries + GOTO/GOSUB/ON_* targets — plus GEO/WALLDEF/8X8D inventories):

1. **Areas 16, 17, 18, 36, 98 — NOT placeholders; no GEO member exists.** None of these ids appear
   in any `GEO{n}.DAX` (GEO ids: 32,34 / 48,49,50,64,66,67,68 / 80,81,82,96,97,99), so no Gen2 GEO
   header exists to stamp and "placeholder wall art" does not apply. 16/17/36 are overland/travel
   scripts (`LOAD_FILES(127,127,127)` — the no-map sentinel); 18 and 98 are event/cutscene scripts
   (no LOAD_FILES of a real map, no LOAD_PIECES anywhere in their full subroutine graphs, not just
   the fresh-run path). `build-dqk-dir.mts` now annotates such residuals `[script-only area: no GEO
   map, so no wall header exists — wall art not applicable]` so the distinction is visible in every
   future build log.
2. **Areas 66, 97 — real gaps, now CLOSED by an evidence-gated two-set fallback.** Their
   LOAD_PIECES operands — 66: `(21, 22, 255)`, 97: `(17, 18, 255)` — name a set-2 WALLDEF block
   (22 / 18) that exists on **no** CoK disk. The key: their resolved region siblings name the
   IDENTICAL pairs (67: `(21,22)`, 99: `(17,18)`; likewise 57/64: `(19,20)`, 96: `(15,16)`) and in
   EVERY case the "+1" set-2 block was never shipped — the siblings survive only because their own
   flag-SAVEs (`0x4be7`/`0x4be8` = 1, COAB `field_1CE`/`field_1D0`) make the engine take the
   **two-set path, which skips set 2** (COAB `CMD_LoadFiles` §3.3,
   `research/firstperson-wall-walk-cok.md` — which already documents the same shape for ECL1 block
   34's never-shipped set-2 operand 4). Blocks 66/97 simply don't re-write those REGION-PERSISTENT
   flags (they inherit them =1 from the region's entry blocks); a fresh single-block VM run
   defaults them to 0 and takes the three-set path, which the shipped data makes impossible.
   `buildCokWallArtPort` now retries the two-set mapping `[var3, Reset, var1]` when — and only
   when — the named set-2 block is absent from the caller's whole (cross-disk) lookup; the
   resolved area carries a provenance `note`. The fallback NEVER fires when the named set-2 block
   exists (guard-tested), so no real data problem can be papered over.

**Result** (`tools/build-dqk-dir.mts --wall-art`, same 22 new sets as before — zero new sets
added, the dedup proof): areas 66/97 stamp headers **byte-identical to siblings 67/99** (66/67 =
`[30, 31, 255, …]`, 97/99 = `[38, 39, 255, …]`; two ids per area because WALLDEF blocks 21/17 are
2-record blocks whose expansion fills slot 2). `build/cok-dqk-release` rebuilt with its README's
exact original flags; `tools/cok_m4_static_verify.mts` ALL CHECKS PASSED; emitted `8X8DC.TLB`
re-rendered to PNG and eyeballed — both sets are coherent wall art (66/67: mossy cavern walls +
doors; 97/99: icy crystalline cavern): `renders/cok-wallart-6697-check/_montage_area66-67.png`,
`_montage_area97-99.png`. `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean; engine suite 163 files / **1858
tests** green (3 new: synthetic fallback + synthetic never-fires guard + golden real-bytes 66≡67 /
97≡99 dedup identity). DoK unaffected (its 19/19 has no missing set-2 case; the fallback is inert
there). **Static-only, same Layer-A caveat as all wall art**: no DOSBox-X was used (slot owned by
another agent); a live visual render of areas 66/97 (walk into Throtl-region map 66 / the disk-3
ice map 97) is the natural next step for whoever next holds the DOSBox-X slot. Files:
`packages/engine/src/loaders/cokWallPort.ts` (fallback + `note` field),
`tools/build-dqk-dir.mts` (note/scope reporting, updated coverage docs),
`packages/engine/test/cokWallPort.test.ts` (+3), `docs/engine/research/dok-wall-art-cross-disk.md`
(2026-07-22 addendum), `docs/engine/ROADMAP.md` (cok.exe row), `build/cok-dqk-release/README.md`
(coverage rewritten, stale `8X8DB.TLB` mention fixed to `8X8DC.TLB`).

Web-app UI feature, additive to every existing Gen1 explore route (`cok`, `dok`, `coab`, `pool`,

  id="gen1-areasel">` appended into `mountDungeonView()`'s frame for every Gen1 route, matching
  `dqkExplore.ts`'s own picker conventions exactly. Populated **asynchronously** (starts as a

  factored out of `buildDqkGame.ts`'s own `pairedAreas` GEO+ECL pairing criterion so both callers
  share one definition). Picking a different area calls `switchGen1Area()`, which re-fetches that
  DISK's own WALLDEF/8X8D/MON/ITEM archives (a different disk means genuinely different assets)
  and re-mounts live — confirmed via Puppeteer: CoK/DoK/Treasures automap titles and rendered maps
  visibly change on selection, with an old-view-preserved + status-line error (not a crash) on the
  one deliberately-tested unbootable id (DoK area 32 — WALLDEF block 2 (set 1) not found, a real
  gap in DoK's own retail WALLDEF1.DAX, not a picker bug).
- **New Treasures of the Savage Frontier explore page** (`?explore=treasures`, no prior route
  existed): required two real engine-side format deltas, found via a genuine bootability sweep
  (pairing alone is necessary but not sufficient — proven by area 16, which pairs but is a
  dialogue/menu script with no `LOAD_FILES` at all):
  1. **`ECL_GEN1_SHORT_TREASURES`** (`packages/engine/src/ecl/disassemble.ts`) — Treasures'
     `LOAD_FILES` (0x21) only decodes cleanly under Gen2's 2-operand short frame, not Gen1's
     3-operand one; every reachable area script desyncs into a bad-opcode halt a few bytes past
     its own LOAD_FILES operands under the plain `ECL_GEN1_SHORT` frame. Scoped to Treasures only
     (DoK/Gateway/PoD stay on `ECL_GEN1_SHORT`, independently proven fine).
  2. **`loadDungeon`'s new `fallbackPieces` opt-in** (`packages/engine/src/world/dungeon.ts`) —
     none of `ECL1.DAX`'s 30 blocks ever emit a `LOAD_PIECES` effect (verified by running every
     one, even under the LOAD_FILES fix); Treasures' wilderness-encounter scripts apparently reuse
     a wall/tile set the host is expected to already have loaded. Every other caller omits the
     option and keeps the strict original throw-on-missing behavior — zero behavior change
     elsewhere.
  `eclInitBlock: 20` was **not hand-picked**: a full sweep of all 29 paired ids found areas
  20/22/24/25/34/40 the only ones that run cleanly to a real `EXIT` under the fix; 20 is the
  lowest.
  3. **A third, genuinely new, still-unsolved 8X8D sub-format**: Treasures' `8X8D1.DAX` wall-tile
     blocks (12 blocks, uniform 16818 decompressed bytes each, real distinct content per block —
     verified by MD5, ruling out a parser bug) use a header layout the standard plane-strip
     `sniff8x8dBlock` doesn't recognize (`08 01 00 00 00 00 00 01` vs. CoK's `08 00 01 00 00 00 00
     00`) — not yet reverse-engineered, and out of scope for this picker feature. Rather than hard
     -crash the whole dungeon load over undecodable wall art, `loadDungeonWalls`'s `loadTiles`
     (`packages/engine/src/world/dungeonWalls.ts`) now catches a tile-decode failure and returns
     `null` (blank tile set) instead of throwing — the map/ECL logic and the picker still work,
     wall pixel art is honestly just absent for this one title until the format is solved. Every
     currently-supported title's 8X8D blocks decode cleanly today, so this catch path is inert for
     them (confirmed: full engine suite unchanged, 152 files / 1790 tests green).
  Also required separating the wall-tile source (`sources.tileBlock`, unmerged — `tiles.blocks`
  only) from the font/frame extraction source (`tlIdx`, merged with `framePath`'s 8X8D0.DAX):
  Treasures' separate frame archive reuses block id 202 for its own non-tile-bank "frame" image,
  which would otherwise collide with `loadDungeonWalls`'s `BOOT_8X8D_SET4` (0xCA=202) boot-tile
  probe.
- `apps/web/src/ui/gen1Disks.ts` / `gameData.ts`: `eclDialect` type extended with

- `apps/web/src/ui/main.ts`: `?explore=treasures` route + `▶ Explore Treasures dungeon (walk)`

### DoK wall-set-id bank routing — real root cause found and FIXED: `id<=9` threshold, not a `>=100` split; bug was never DoK-specific, it silently affected CoK's already-shipped wall art too (2026-07-19, later round)

Root-caused and fixed the `DISK READ ERROR` the two entries below left open, using a static
Unicorn trace (`tools/unicorn_dqk_trace.py`, no DOSBox-X needed), mirroring CoK's own `50ee9ec`
debugger-breakpoint method as instructed. **Verdict: the `>=100` correlation the earlier rounds
noted was a coincidence, not the cause — and the real bug was never DoK-specific.**

**What was tested and refuted first (in order, each a real falsifiable round, not skipped):**
1. Changed `COK_WALL_SET_ID_BASE` from 100 to 20 (testing "id divides by 100 to pick the bank"),
   rebuilt, re-traced with a `--watch-dgroup-write` on the filename buffer's bank-letter byte.
   **Result: byte-for-byte IDENTICAL retry-loop trace to the pre-fix id=101 run.** The `id/100`
   theory is false — proven by direct empirical re-test, not just re-reasoning.
2. Traced `build/cok-dqk-release/DQK.EXE` (CoK's own already-shipped "13/15 areas render real
   wall art" build, ids 100-121) with the identical boot route as a control, expecting a clean
   `8x8db.tlb` load per its README's "verified both statically and live" claim. **It showed the
   exact same infinite `8x8dc.tlb`/`A:\8x8dc.tlb` retry loop as DoK's build** — proving this was
   never a DoK-only bug. Extended both traces to 60M instructions (the same budget CoK's own
   §8 investigation used to prove its original bug was a genuine infinite loop, not truncation):
   both hit **exactly 374** `8x8d` file-open attempts, confirming a real unbounded loop in both
   games, not a static-trace artifact. Commit `c801066`'s own message had honestly flagged that
   a live DOSBox-X confirmation of CoK's wall art "was assessed and skipped as genuinely
   infeasible" — so this claim had in fact never been checked against the real engine; the
   README overstated it (the actual "verified... live" run was `cok-on-dqk-m4fidelity`, the
   DQK-**placeholder**-only build, never a real-wall-art one).

**The real mechanism (proven both by pattern and by a controlled fix-and-retest):**
`DQK.EXE`'s wall filename is built from a `8x8d%c%d` format string (found via `--find` in the
executable's data). The bank LETTER is decided by a **hardcoded threshold on the id value**,
not a table search across `8X8DB.TLB`/`8X8DC.TLB`: **`id <= 9` opens `8X8DB.TLB`; any `id > 9`
opens `8X8DC.TLB`** — full stop, regardless of which physical file actually holds that id in its
own set-id table. Evidence: every id `<=9` tested (the native placeholder combo `01 02 08`) opens
`8x8db.tlb` cleanly (3 opens, no retry); every id `>9` tested (DoK's 20/21, CoK's 100-121) opens
`8x8dc.tlb` and loops. `appendHlibMasterSets`/`cokWallPort.ts` had always appended new sets to
`8X8DB.TLB` (both at `BASE=100` and the once-tried `BASE=20`) — the wrong file for any id above 9,
so DQK.EXE never even attempted to open the file the new sets were actually in.

**Fix, implemented and verified (content-port side only — no `DQK.EXE` byte was touched):**
`packages/engine/src/loaders/cokWallPort.ts` now appends new wall sets to **`8X8DC.TLB`** instead
of `8X8DB.TLB`, with `COK_WALL_SET_ID_BASE` lowered from 20 to **18** (still `>9` so the threshold
picks `8X8DC.TLB`, and clear of its native ids 10-17). `tools/build-dqk-dir.mts` and
`tools/build-cok-wallart-scratch.mts` updated to match (both the source file read and the
`overrides` map key). Proven with a pre-fix isolation test first (extracted DoK's existing id-20
leaf, hand-appended it into `8X8DC.TLB` under a fresh id 18, patched area 34's GEO header to
reference it, retraced against the UNMODIFIED `DQK.EXE`): clean 3× `8x8dc.tlb` open + a clean
`back.tlb` open, zero retry — the exact known-good signature `50ee9ec`/§8 established. Then
applied for real: rebuilt both `build/dok-dqk-release/` and `build/cok-dqk-release/` with the
library fix and re-traced each — **both now show the identical clean signature** (3× `8x8dc.tlb`
open at the new, larger file size, immediately followed by a clean `back.tlb` open, no `A:\`
retry, no loop). `packages/engine/test/cokWallPort.test.ts` (20 tests, all reference
`COK_WALL_SET_ID_BASE` dynamically) passes unchanged.

**What is still NOT proven:** this is a static-trace result, not a live DOSBox-X/GameLink
confirmation — the task brief's own tiering allowed static-first, and a clean load through the
wall-bank open + immediate backdrop load matches the exact signature that, for CoK's original
`50ee9ec` bug, DID hold up live. A live re-run of `tools/dok-dqk-live-boot-verify.ps1` against
the freshly rebuilt `build/dok-dqk-release/` (single DOSBox-X/GameLink agent only, per the
project's singleton-collision hazard) is the natural next step to close this out completely, but
was not run this round (time budget went to nailing the root cause across two games instead).
CoK's `build/cok-dqk-release/README.md` still carries the now-disproven "verified both statically
and live" wall-art claim and its wall-art-coverage numbers were generated pre-fix — both are
stale (the directory itself was rebuilt with the fix this round) and should be regenerated/
corrected the next time that build is touched (it's git-ignored, so this doesn't block a commit).

Evidence (scratchpad, not committed — disposable): `dok-trace-01/02.log` (pre/post first failed
fix attempt, identical), `cok-real-wallart-trace.log` + `-long.log` (CoK control, 60M instr, 374
opens), `dok-real-wallart-trace-long.log` (DoK, 60M instr, 374 opens), `dok-bankc-test.log` (the
isolation proof), `dok-realbuild-postfix.log` / `cok-realbuild-postfix.log` (both real rebuilds,
clean signature).

### DoK wall-art coverage gap DIAGNOSED + FIXED — 8/19 -> 19/19 playable areas, cross-disk WALLDEF/8X8D root cause (STATIC ONLY, no DOSBox-X, 2026-07-19)

Follow-up to the entry directly below (DoK.exe packaged, 8/19 wall-art coverage shipped as an
honest but UNDIAGNOSED gap). Root cause found and fixed: DoK ships **5** `WALLDEF{n}.DAX`/
`8X8D{n}.DAX` archives against only **3** `ECL{n}.DAX`/`GEO{n}.DAX` disks, and the port only ever
checked the WALLDEF/8X8D archive numbered like an area's own ECL disk — a false assumption that
happens to hold for CoK (exactly 3 WALLDEF/8X8D disks, one per ECL/GEO/MON disk) but not DoK,
whose wall-tile block-id space is split across its 5 archives by an axis unrelated to the ECL/GEO
disk number (e.g. area 32 is on `ECL1.DAX` but its `LOAD_PIECES` block only exists in
`WALLDEF4.DAX`). Verified via direct inventory that **all 11 originally-residual areas** fail for
exactly this reason, and that DoK's WALLDEF/8X8D block ids have **zero collisions** across its 5
disks (making a cross-disk fallback lookup unambiguous), while CoK's own 3 WALLDEF disks DO have
real, intentional id reuse with DIFFERENT content (e.g. `WALLDEF1.DAX` id 23 != `WALLDEF3.DAX` id
23) — so a blind merge-everything fix would have silently broken CoK's already-correct 13/15.

Fix: new `buildCrossDiskBlockSource` in `packages/engine/src/loaders/cokWallPort.ts` — indexes
every disk's blocks by id, always prefers the "own"/matching disk (zero behavior change where it
already worked), and only falls back to another disk when EVERY disk holding that id agrees
byte-for-byte (verified true for DoK, so this activates safely there; CoK's disagreeing id 23 is
correctly detected and never merged). `tools/build-dqk-dir.mts`'s `--wall-art` step now discovers
every `WALLDEF{k}.DAX`/`8X8D{k}.DAX` present (not just one per ECL disk) and wires each ECL disk's
`walldefBlock`/`tileBlock` through this cross-disk lookup.

Result: **19/19 playable DoK areas now resolve real wall art** (was 8/19). The 3 areas that stay
without wall art (16, 17, 35) are NOT among the 19 playable areas — their own ECL scripts
genuinely never call `LOAD_PIECES` (e.g. area 17 is the proven wilderness-leg entry, which has no
first-person wall view by design) — an honest ceiling, not a bug. CoK's own 13/15 is unchanged,
confirmed both by new `buildCrossDiskBlockSource` unit tests using CoK's real id-23 collision as a
synthetic case, and by re-running the existing CoK golden test unmodified.

Verification: `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean; `pnpm --filter @goldbox/engine test` — 150 files
/ 1783 tests (1777 prior + 6 new: 5 `buildCrossDiskBlockSource` unit tests + 1 golden test against

2. **Real bug found and fixed: `cokWallPort.ts`'s `resolveAreaPieces` hardcoded `new EclVm(block)`**
   with no dialect option, silently defaulting to `ECL_GEN1` (CoK's long-frame dialect) for EVERY
   caller, including a future DoK one. `EclVm`/`disassembleEclBlock` already support a `dialect`
   parameter and `apps/web/src/ui/gameData.ts`'s `dok` profile already sets `eclDialect:
   'gen1-short'` — this port module was simply never wired to it. Fixed: `buildCokWallArtPort`
   now takes an `opts.dialect` (default `ECL_GEN1`, unchanged for CoK) and threads it into
   `resolveAreaPieces`'s `EclVm` construction. `build-dqk-dir.mts` passes `ECL_GEN1_SHORT` when
   `--target dok`. A new synthetic test (`cokWallPort.test.ts`, "dialect option is threaded
   through") constructs a block using opcode 0x1D's dialect-dependent operand count to prove the
   threading actually matters — a wrong dialect here is a SILENT desync (the VM doesn't throw, it
   just decodes garbage as *something*), so a black-box "does it crash" check wouldn't have caught
   it. Empirically, DoK's own real ECL1 block 34 (the area this build's save resumes into) happens
   not to cross the dialect delta before its own `LOAD_PIECES` call, so it resolves identically
   under both dialects — documented as an honest negative in a second golden test, so a future
   reader doesn't mistake that golden for proof of the fix (the synthetic test is what proves it).

   `loadDungeonWalls` already detects DoK's shared 256-tile 8X8D bank and points
   `walls.tileSets[1..3]` all at the SAME object (built originally FOR DoK support in the browser
   engine, per that module's own doc comments) — but `cokWallPort.ts` had an early bailout
   explicitly treating `walls.singleBank` as "out of scope for CoK" residual. Removed: since CoK
   never triggers `singleBank` (confirmed unaffected — the guard was dead code for CoK), and the
   existing per-slot `encodeCokWallSet(walls.tileSets[s])` loop already handles the object
   correctly with zero new logic (three identical bank encodes → the existing content-hash dedup
   collapses them to ONE new set id shared by all three header bytes). This is the minimal
   generalization of the already-shipped, already-precedented CoK path — deliberately NOT a new

### CoK M4 combat-init bug, round 15 (FINAL) — `Invoke-Vision`'s JSON-wrapping bug FIXED generally; the falsification boot FINALLY completed; DEFINITIVE RESULT: the crash STILL FIRES at the remapped area id — id-collision theory REFUTED, chain CLOSED after 15 rounds (1 harness fix + 2 live DOSBox-X boots, 2026-07-19)

Task: fix `Invoke-Vision`'s round-14 JSON-wrapping regression in `tools/dosbot/lib.ps1` (a shared helper,
not route-specific), then spend up to 3 live boots completing the round-13/14 falsification test — does
the round-11/12 crash still fire once CoK's ported area 34 is remapped to 134? Report definitively and
close the chain — this is the final round in this specific vein.

1. **`Invoke-Vision` root-caused and fixed.** The old code extracted JSON via a greedy regex spanning the
   FIRST `{` to the LAST `}` in the whole response — fine for one clean object, but breaks the moment the
   model emits more than one JSON object back-to-back (a known LLM degenerate-repetition failure mode,
   matching round 14's 2/2-reproducible retry-path symptom). When that parse failed, the old fallback
   dumped the ENTIRE raw (still JSON-shaped) response into `visible_text` — exactly round 14's observed
   bug. Fix: new `Get-FirstJsonObject` (string-aware, brace-depth-counting scan) extracts just the first
   complete object and ignores anything appended after it — including repeated copies — plus a
   `visible_text`-salvage regex as a second-tier fallback before the final raw-dump. General fix: all 5
   existing `Invoke-Vision` callers (`tools/dosbot/{boot-test,capture-ingame,drive-test,e62b-explore,
   run-boot-tests}.ps1` + every `cok-m4-*-route.ps1`) only ever read `.screen`/`.game_title`/
   `.visible_text`/`.looks_crashed`/`.note` off the result — unaffected. Verified via
   `Parser]::ParseFile` (zero syntax errors across `lib.ps1` and all 9 caller/array-param scripts) and
   synthetic direct-invocation checks reproducing the exact round-14 failure shape (repeated-object
   concatenation) against both the old code (confirmed broken) and the new code (confirmed fixed), plus 3
   more synthetic cases (clean single object, trailing prose with a stray brace, no-braces fallback). No
   `packages/engine/**` touched, so the `tsc`/vitest gates don't apply this round.
2. **Boot 1 of 3 (`build/cok-m4-remap-confirm-run4`) — proved the fix live, hit a SEPARATE CLI-array bug.**
   Reached the dungeon and solved the journal prompt cleanly across 2 passes with zero JSON-wrapped output
   either time (the fix holds under real vision-model retries, not just synthetic tests). Then threw in
   Phase 7: this round's own nested nested-PowerShell invocation caused `-MovementKeys right,up` to arrive
   as ONE unsplit argv string (`"right,up"`) rather than a 2-element array — a related but distinct flavor
   of the same "array args don't survive an outer/child `pwsh -File` boundary" hazard rounds 13/14 each hit
   differently. Confirmed via 5 synthetic invocation-form tests that no CLI string form is reliable in this
   configuration. `dosbox-x.exe` confirmed empty after.
3. **Boot 2 of 3 (`build/cok-m4-remap-confirm-run5`) — the falsification test COMPLETED, exit code 0.**
   Fixed the array-passing issue with a one-line call-operator wrapper script (`&
   route.ps1 ... -MovementKeys @('right','up')`, literal array in PowerShell source, never crossing an
   argv boundary) — verified against a synthetic throwaway script first. The full route then ran
   end-to-end for the first time in this 15-round chain: phases 1-6 clean, journal solved (`'randomly'`,
   3 confirmation passes, all clean OCR text), and the established 2-key crash-trigger sequence
   (`right`,`up`, the remapped-build equivalent of the original `14,10→15,10 facing E`) produced, on
   screen, pixel-for-pixel confirmed: **`MONSTERS ATTACK!` then `DISK READ ERROR`** — the identical crash
   signature documented since round 9, now reproduced AT THE REMAPPED ID (134, not 34). `dosbox-x.exe`
   confirmed empty after.
4. **DEFINITIVE RESULT: the id-collision theory is REFUTED.** Round 12's leading candidate (native-id
   collision at area 34 causing DQK.EXE to consult the wrong compiled-in table) predicted the crash would
   NOT fire once the id moved 100+ away from every native occupant (native ids top out at 67). It fired
   anyway, identically. This was coincidental, not causal — round 12's own crash mechanism (§12: a local
   stack-buffer overflow driven by a bogus `0x19F` chain-count byte in an id-keyed resource record) stands
   unchanged; only "why id 34 specifically" is now closed (it wasn't the id).
5. **Chain CLOSED per this round's own charter — no round 16 in this vein.** The crash mechanism is fully
   pinned at the instruction/variable level; the one concrete, evidence-backed hypothesis this doc ever
   produced (id-collision) is cleanly tested and refuted; no further static or live lead is queued anywhere
   in 15 rounds of history. **Final recommendation:** route further work through round 12's decision memo
   paths — (a) a targeted `DQK.EXE` binary patch (needs explicit user sign-off, not attempted, address
   still not pinned) or (c) accept as a known, isolated, non-content DQK.EXE-internal gap for packaging
   purposes (the CoK content port itself — ECL/GEO/MONCHA bytes — is proven well-formed and NOT at fault,
   reconfirmed both statically and live across 15 rounds). A third, different-method option (extending the
   Unicorn static tracer further into the remapped build, rather than more live boots) is noted but
   explicitly not attempted this round — out of scope. **ROADMAP Wave-2 CoK M4 item updated to BLOCKED
   (definitive, not "do not check off yet")** — ports genuinely don't cause this; DQK.EXE itself does, for

Task: abandon the load-segment-shift arithmetic model (seven straight non-firing live addresses across
rounds 6 and 8) and instead dump the running guest's real conventional memory and search it for the
exact unique bytes Ghidra already proved for combat-setup-entry (file `0x356DC`) and its one true
caller `AddCombatantToActiveRoster` (file `0x359E6`). **Result: the technique now works end-to-end for
the first time — a live address is confirmed for one of the two targets, and the actual crash is
captured on-screen for the first time via this route — but the confirmed address's breakpoint never
fires during the crash itself, so root cause remains UNLOCATED.**

1. **New script `tools/cok-m4-memory-signature-route.ps1`.** `MEMDUMPBIN <seg>:<off> <len>` dumps the
   guest's conventional memory to a host file; a Python helper byte-searches it for each signature's
   unique prefix; any hit's linear offset directly IS the live physical address — no shift arithmetic,
   no calibration formula.
2. **Five real bugs found and fixed before the technique could actually run, none glossed over:**
   (a) debugger commands are silent no-ops while the guest is running, only processed while genuinely
   halted — corrects an assumption rounds 6-8 never had to confront; (b) DQK.EXE's general idle/
   input-wait primitive is `INT 16h` in a tight loop (new architectural fact, not combat-specific),
   which stalls naive "arm and wait" strategies badly; (c) `MEMDUMPBIN`'s size argument silently parses
   as **zero** when given a `0x`-prefixed hex literal — root-caused by reading `debug.cpp`'s
   `GetHexValue` directly: its tokenizer keeps the `x` in the token but then requires every character to
   be a hex digit, so the whole token fails and falls through to `return 0`, with **no error printed
   anywhere** (`"success"` is unconditional); (d) `[math]::Floor` returns a `System.Double`, and
   PowerShell's `{0:X4}` format specifier throws against non-integer types — crashed the script the
   instant a live match was found; (e) an unsuppressed `& python ...` call leaked stdout into a
   function's own implicit return value, silently turning a boolean control variable (`$earlyHit`) into
   a truthy multi-element array **with no exception anywhere** — this short-circuited the entire rest of
   the route from the first genuine stop onward, found only via exact-timestamp file forensics (the
   multi-second gap with zero files written in it).
3. **With all five fixed, the full route completed cleanly for the first time this chain:** title →
   menu → Load Saved Game → journal-word protection (solved live) → party menu → dungeon exploration →
   `right`/`up` movement → the exact "MONSTERS ATTACK!"/"DISK READ ERROR" crash every round since §9 has
   reported, this time captured live on-screen via this specific route (screenshot in the writeup).
4. **Signature search (640 KiB dump at Load Saved Game time):** `add_combatant_to_active_roster` found
   live and resident at a confirmed address, `2C23:0006` — the first confirmed live address for either
   target in 9 rounds. `combat_setup_entry` confirmed **not yet resident** at that same point, consistent
   with on-demand overlay loading for actual combat.
5. **A real breakpoint armed at the confirmed address never fired** through journal, party menu, dungeon
   walk, movement, or the crash itself — a genuine negative result (the same breakpoint machinery
   reliably caught DQK's own `INT 16h` idle-poll dozens of times over the same run, so this isn't a
   tooling failure). Most likely explanation: DQK's overlay manager relocates this segment between
   Load-Saved-Game time and actual combat, consistent with this whole chain's established
   overlay-placement volatility (rounds 6-8).
6. **No code fix implemented** — still correctly UNLOCATED at the live-address-that-actually-fires

### CoK M4 combat-init bug, round 7: round 6's addressing puzzle SOLVED — `2177:257C`/`25A4:018A` were never real DQK.EXE addresses; TRUE address `1F4E:47AC` (file `0x356DC`) proven twice (unique raw-byte search + fresh Ghidra headless import/analyze/decompile/xref); the one true caller found and decompiled; its own caller proven to be a genuine indirect call (STATIC ONLY, Ghidra 12.1.2, no DOSBox-X, 2026-07-18)

Task: use Ghidra's decompiler + call-graph analysis (not another ad hoc disasm scan) to settle what
rounds 4-6 couldn't. **Result: solved, with a mechanistic explanation for why round 6's live
breakpoints never fired.**

1. **The TRUE static address, proven two independent ways.** A unique raw-byte search across the
   whole 449,664-byte `DQK.EXE` (`mov ax,0x5FFD` — the `"moncha1"` pointer load — and
   `sub sp,0x288` — the routine's own frame size — both occur **exactly once** in the file) pins
   combat-setup-entry's entry at file `0x356DC`. Independently, importing `DQK.EXE` into a **fresh**
   Ghidra project via the project's existing (previously FID-only) `build/decompiler-inputs/
   dark-queen-of-krynn/manifest.json` + `ghidra_import.py` pipeline, running full `analyzeAll()`, and
   decompiling the function Ghidra itself resolves at the corresponding synthetic address reproduces
   the SAME routine byte-for-byte (same `moncha1`-loader call, same RLE-decompress, same two
   count-driven copy loops). File `0x356DC` sits in overlay descriptor index 3 (`disasm_dqk.py`'s
   `OVERLAY_DESCS`, on-disk RTLink table), true runtime segment **`0x1F4E`** — giving true
   `1F4E:47AC`, not round 4-6's `2177:257C`.
2. **Root cause of round 6's failure, now mechanistic.** `tools/unicorn_dqk_trace.py`'s overlay
   loader computes each overlay's LIVE segment dynamically (a "first free paragraph" allocator) —
   it does NOT use the fixed, file-verified `runtime_segment` DQK.EXE's own RTLink descriptor table
   specifies. For simpler earlier routes (§7-§9) the harness's guess happened to land on the correct
   `0x1F4E`; by the time a scripted route reaches deep into combat (rounds 8+), the harness's internal
   bookkeeping had drifted and it computed `0x2177` instead for the SAME overlay — a uniquely
   confusing coincidence because `0x2177` is ALSO a real, valid sub-segment used by OTHER, unrelated
   routines in that same overlay body (confirmed by direct disassembly), which is exactly why every
   earlier round's own "forward-alignment self-consistency" checks kept passing on real-but-wrong
   bytes.

   an `AddCombatantToActiveRoster(id)`-shaped routine at file `0x359E6` (true `1F4E:4AB6`), gated on a
   hard cap of 8 active slots (`DS:0xB2A4`, the SAME table §10-§11 already found and called
   "plateaus, does not fail" — its owner is now known), calling combat-setup-entry via a plain NEAR
   call (settling §12.3's whole near/far-ABI question as moot — it was never a real issue at the true
   call site) with a **hardcoded flag byte `1`** (correcting round 4/6's "unwritten flag" read, which
