   derived from the wrong address family and should be treated as unreliable going forward; the
   structural overflow mechanism it was built on is untouched and reconfirmed by this round's clean
   decompile.
4. **One hop further — genuinely indirect, an honest static limit.** Three independent exhaustive
   searches (Ghidra xrefs post-`analyzeAll()`, the manifest's own resolved resident-stub call list,
   and raw-byte scans for a far-call/data-pointer/near-call to this function anywhere in the file) all
   found **zero** static callers of the roster-add routine. Its own caller is a genuine
   computed/indirect far call — not resolvable further without either a live DOSBox-X trace (now with
   a correct target for the first time) or deeper Ghidra value-tracking. Reported as UNLOCATED, not

5. **New, precise, Ghidra-verified live-breakpoint candidates** for the next DOSBox-X round (round 6's

### CoK M4 combat-init bug, round 4: the "unbounded loop" is a real local stack-buffer overflow; the harness's own unexplained crash address finally explained (STATIC ONLY, Unicorn tracer, no DOSBox-X, 2026-07-18)

Executed §11.5's own next step (`docs/engine/research/cok-m4-fidelity-plan.md` §11.5: "trace one
level further out" from the ~530-byte per-combatant setup routine §11.3 decoded). Extended
`tools/unicorn_dqk_trace.py` with a new, general-purpose `--wide-disasm-at SEG:OFF:BEFORE:AFTER
[:LABEL]` one-shot wide-disassembly probe (reusable — not hardcoded to this one bug) and a
near/far calling-convention disambiguator (`_dqk_combat_setup_entry_text`, reads the live stack
under both interpretations rather than trusting static bytes).

**Result: found the actual overflow mechanism, not just "the caller."** §11's `[bp+8]` flag turned
out to be a red herring (a one-time mode-select byte, not a loop counter). Widening the SAME
routine's disassembly PAST §11.3's `+140`-byte cutoff revealed a second local loop, live-confirmed
at **114-115 iterations** via `--trace-flow-range`, driven by a byte at offset `0x19F` of an
id-keyed, RLE-decompressed per-record resource blob (the same signed-byte-RLE codec family DAX/DAA/
HLIB block data uses) that should hold a small "chained sub-record count" but doesn't for this
ported encounter. With zero bounds checking, this loop overruns the routine's own 0x288-byte local
stack buffer by roughly 3x, one 17-byte `memcpy` at a time — walking straight through the saved BP
and into the saved return address. **The corrupted value it pops, `614d:206d`, is now proven to be
the direct cause of the harness's own long-unexplained "614d" crash segment** (§10.5 had assessed
that as a harness-fidelity limit, not real DQK behavior — that assessment is superseded: `614d` is
literal overrun resource-blob content, not synthetic noise, meaning this bug would corrupt DQK's
own call stack in a real DOSBox session too). Also, live-checked (not assumed) that the routine's
one real call site is a genuine far call — an alarming-looking static "near call to the same
address" elsewhere in the binary was a false lead, ruled out against the live stack. And: this
corrects §11.2's dismissal of the original "CBODY icon-id mismatch" candidate — that dismissal only
examined the id-blind allocator; a genuine id-keyed resource lookup sits one step earlier that
§11.3's narrower window never captured, re-opening that candidate's general shape (not yet confirmed
to the exact byte/file). Traced the id/pointer argument (`0x81DE` at the call site) through one
wrapper hop (`035b95`, allocates from a THIRD, previously-unsurveyed table `DS:0xB7B2`) but not to
its ultimate origin — that's the concrete next step. **No code fix implemented** — the mechanism is
now precisely pinned (missing bounds check + a bad count byte) but the upstream content-port field
responsible is not yet located, so a fix would be guessing which of 3 plausible port-pipeline
locations to patch. Full writeup, all addresses, and the priority-ordered next steps: `docs/engine/
research/cok-m4-fidelity-plan.md` **§12**.

### CoK's own wall art ported into DQK's `8X8DB.TLB` bank — 15/22 areas resolved, placeholder replaced per-area (STATIC ONLY, no DOSBox-X, 2026-07-18)

Follows directly from §8/the M4 fix above: `DQK_GEO_PLACEHOLDER_SET_IDS` (`01 02 08 01 08 ff`,
a fixed DQK-native combo) is what every ported CoK area's GEO header still stamps, so ported
dungeons rendered with DQK's own wall art rather than CoK's. This round replaces the placeholder
with CoK's real wall art, per area, wherever the source data supports it — done as a
**post-processing pass**, not by editing `buildDqkGame.ts`/`geoEncode.ts`, to avoid any collision
with the live M4 fidelity agent sharing this tree.

Pipeline (new module `packages/engine/src/loaders/cokWallPort.ts`): for each CoK area, run its
own ECL init block through `EclVm` to capture the `LOAD_PIECES` (opcode 0x37) effect, resolve the
resulting `setBlockIds` via the existing `loadDungeonWalls()` (reusing its k>1-record WALLDEF
expansion quirk — a single WALLDEF block can fill more than one symbol-set slot), convert each
8×8 EGA-4bpp wall tile to a VGA HLIB `TILE` leaf (EGA index `i` → VGA `32+i`, EGA magenta/index 13
→ HLIB transparent key 255, draw method 21 matching `8X8DB.TLB`'s own), dedupe identical tile
pools by content hash, and append the new sets to `8X8DB.TLB`'s HLIB master via a new
`appendHlibMasterSets()` (existing 9 sets preserved byte-for-byte; format per `hlib-format.md`
§1c, independently verified against real `DISK2/8X8DB.TLB`/`8X8DC.TLB` bytes). New set ids start
at 100 (`COK_WALL_SET_ID_BASE`) to stay clear of DQK's shipped 1-9/10-17 space (note: direct
inspection found `8X8DC.TLB` actually holds ids 10-17, not the single id 11 assumed at task
start — handled conservatively by extending **only** `8X8DB.TLB`, since whether DQK's loader does
cross-file id lookup between the two files is unverified). `stampCokWallHeaders()` then patches
just the resolved areas' 6-byte GEO header fields (bytes 2-7) in an already-built `geoGlb`,
byte-for-byte, leaving everything else (including all encoding/assembly logic) untouched.

Result against real CoK data (`tools/build-cok-wallart-scratch.mts`, scratch out-dir
`build/cok-on-dqk-wallart-scratch`, never `build/cok-on-dqk-m4fidelity`): **15 of 22 paired areas
(68%) now carry real CoK wall art** (22 new sets, ids 100-121, 70 tiles each, appended to
`8X8DB.TLB` — bank grows from 423 to 1963 images, 9 to 31 set-id-table entries). **7 areas stay
on the DQK-native placeholder, honestly**: 5 because a fresh run of the area's own ECL init block
emits no `LOAD_PIECES` (the wall combo is presumably set by a predecessor/region-entry script, or
the area isn't a first-person dungeon view), 2 because a referenced WALLDEF block (22, 18) isn't
present in that disk's WALLDEF file. Backdrop bytes (5-7 of the header) are left on the DQK
placeholder for every area — Gen1's first-person view architecture has no CoK backdrop source, so
this residual is real, not an oversight.

Verification: `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean; new `packages/engine/test/cokWallPort.test.ts`
(10 tests: HLIB set-id-table/append round-trip, `stampCokWallHeaders` byte-patch correctness,
synthetic + golden `buildCokWallArtPort` runs) all pass, full engine suite (1755 tests) unaffected;
the scratch build's own 4 static checks (bank decodes cleanly at the expected image count, set-id
table entry count matches, every resolved area's on-disk header + referenced ids are consistent,
every residual area's header is byte-identical to the untouched placeholder) all PASS, re-verified
by re-reading emitted files straight off disk, independent of the in-memory build objects.
**No live/dynamic confirmation was attempted**: DOSBox-X was off the table per this round's brief
(shared machine-wide singleton), and `tools/unicorn_dqk_trace.py`'s file-read modeling is
explicitly self-referential-overlay-only (INT21 AH=3D/3F backed by the real `DQK.EXE`'s own
bytes) — it does not model opening arbitrary external files against a mounted directory, so it
cannot cheaply observe this scratch build's `8X8DB.TLB`/`GEO.GLB` without materially extending the
harness; recorded here as UNLOCATED rather than forced. Static structural fidelity (round-trip
byte preservation of the append, header/id consistency) is complete; live-load confirmation of
the new set ids is the natural next step for whoever next holds the DOSBox-X/Unicorn slot.

Files: `packages/engine/src/loaders/cokWallPort.ts` (new), `packages/engine/src/loaders/hlibEncode.ts`

### CoK-on-DQK M4 "DISK READ ERROR" root-caused + FIXED — Gen2 GEO header bytes 2-7 are resource-set ids, not padding (STATIC/Unicorn only, 2026-07-18)

The §7.2 blocker from the M4 live run (protection answer accepted → "DISK READ ERROR", position
stuck at 7,13, black 3-D view) is **solved without touching the DOSBox-X slot**. Root cause: the
Gen2 GEO member header's "6 reserved bytes" (offsets 2-7) are actually the area's **resource-set
id list** (bytes 2-4 → `8x8d%c` wall sets, 5-7 → `BACK.TLB` backdrops, `0xff` = none); the port
wrote zeros, set id 0 exists in no shipped bank, and DQK's not-found path is its floppy wrong-disk
retry loop — the on-screen "DISK READ ERROR". Proven by 5 Unicorn-harness runs of the full
load-save→journal route against the ported build: repro (endless `8x8db.tlb`→`A:\...` reopen
loop), save-recipe controls both ways (the QSV 240/254 "init flags" are NOT the cause — genuine
mid-game DQK saves in `cloud_saves` show they're Gen1 saved piece-ids, small values, misread by
SAVGAM.TXT as constants), and clean loads (3 wall sets + backdrop, engine reaches its render loop,
area 34 + pose 14,10 confirmed in the runtime record) after stamping a native-DQK set sextet.
Fix landed: `geoEncode.ts` exports `DQK_GEO_PLACEHOLDER_SET_IDS` (`01 02 08 01 08 ff`, native
combo, placeholder until CoK wall art is packed into the banks under CoK's own `LOAD_PIECES` ids);
`buildDqkGame.ts` stamps it on every ported area; the §1 build command gains
`--save-x 14 --save-y 10` (the "7,13" was just the pregen save's own unpatched pose).
`build/cok-on-dqk-m4fidelity` rebuilt + re-verified. Full writeup + doc corrections (SAVGAM.TXT
240/254; hlib-format §1c pointer-# is a 0-based DWORD index — an off-by-one there cost one wasted
run): `docs/engine/research/cok-m4-fidelity-plan.md` **§8**. Next: re-run the live GameLink route
(§7.4), which should now clear area-34 entry with DQK placeholder walls.

### GLIB unknowns closed — 0xD2 codec, 0x08/0xE8 colour tables (real Amiga 4-plane palettes!), 0xE1 mask polarity (STATIC ONLY, 2026-07-18)

Follow-up to the 2026-07-18 GLIB decode (commit `3442428`): all three "unknown method"
byte values and the mask-polarity question are **closed**; every previously-skipped
CoAB/Secret member (20 + 75) now decodes. `docs/glib-format.md` §4/§5/§5b/§8 rewritten;
`tools/glib_decode.py` + `packages/engine/src/loaders/glib.ts` updated in lockstep.

- **0xD2 = 4-plane RLE row-interleaved planar images** (the 4-plane sibling of 0xE2).
  Numeric proof: all 44 members RLE-expand to exactly `h*wb*4`; visual proof: CoAB's
  320×200 title screen renders pixel-perfect (SSI/AD&D "PRESENTS" screen) while the
  contiguous-planes and chunky-4bpp layouts both produce obvious garbage.
- **0x08 / 0xE8 are NOT drawing methods — they're colour-table cmagic values.** 0x08 =
  56-byte 16-colour table (same cmagic as DOS HLIB), 0xE8 = 104-byte 32-colour table.
  The five DQK FRAME.TLB "0xE8 micro-images" are `first_col=16, ncolors=16` tables
  patching colours 16–31 — member-for-member twins of DOS FRAME.TLB's cmagic-0x18
  tables at the same indices, which also proves `first_col`/`ncolors` slicing is real
  (old "vestigial" claim corrected; slots past the count are packer garbage).
- **The real 4-plane-era Amiga palettes are shipped in the data files after all** (old
  "in the executable, UNLOCATED" note obsolete): CoAB/Secret `ALWAYS.TLB` m000 = the
  game-global 16-colour palette; every Secret BIGPIC/PIC set carries its own. New
  `--pal` CLI option / `firstGlibPalette()` TS export source it for sets without one.
  Honest residual: later TITLE screens (Secret's fortress) still render implausibly
  with every shipped palette — intro-code palettes, engine behaviour, still open.
- **0xE1/0x01 mask polarity SOLVED: bit 1 = transparent (keep destination).** Corpus
  statistic across all 10,587 masked members: 1.19M mask=1 pixels carry ZERO colour
  bits vs 85% nonzero under mask=0; plus FRAME.TLB m013's exact left/right-nibble
  anti-correlation. Decoders now emit index 255 for mask=1 (was: rendered opaque).
- Survey after fixes: CoAB 2209 images/0 skipped, Secret 2025/0 (both were dozens
  skipped); remaining skips corpus-wide are only 0x19 id-lists (3), `walls.tlb`
  placeholder headers (16), and Treasures' two mis-tagged data libs (73) — all
  documented, none unknown.
- Gates: `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean; engine vitest **1745/1745** (glib golden
  suite grown 4→6 fixtures: new 0xD2 title-screen and FRAME first_col-merge/0xE1-mask
  parity targets in `make-fixtures.py`).

### CoK M4 behavioral-fidelity live run — first-ever live boot, launch/menu/roster/protection-prompt path PROVEN, "DISK READ ERROR" blocks just past it (DOSBox-X ×1, 2026-07-18)

Held the project's single DOSBox-X/GameLink slot to execute the Wave-2 CoK M4 fidelity run per
`docs/engine/research/cok-m4-fidelity-plan.md` (the plan itself was static-only prep from an
earlier round; this is the first pass that actually launched DOSBox-X against it). Rebuilt fresh
(`tools/build-dqk-dir.mts --dqk "The Dark Queen of Krynn" --src "Champions of Krynn" --target cok
--out build/cok-on-dqk-m4fidelity --save "The Dark Queen of Krynn" --save-area 34
--save-ecl-member 34 --save-dungeon --bypass-protection`), reconfirmed `tools/cok_m4_static_verify.mts`
ALL CHECKS PASSED, then drove 3 full live boots.

**Two real, project-wide-reusable GameLink bugs found and fixed:**

1. **DOSBox-X's `[sdl] mouse_emulation` defaults to `locked`**, which silently discards
   GameLink-injected mouse motion in any focusless session (it only applies cursor motion when
   `user_cursor_locked` is true — a state a real host click-to-capture sets, which headless
   GameLink never performs). Root-caused by reading `Mouse_CursorMoved()`
   (`build/tools/dosbox-x-source-2026.07.02/src/ints/mouse.cpp`) against `MOUSE_EMULATION_LOCKED`
   (`src/gui/sdlmain.cpp`). Fix: `tools/dosbox_x_debugbox_probe.ps1` gained a new optional
   `-ExtraSdlConf` passthrough param (empty by default, fully backward-compatible with every
   existing caller) — pass `-ExtraSdlConf "mouse_emulation=always"` for any mouse-driven trace.
2. **DQK's launch menu has a short idle timeout** that auto-plays an attract-mode intro
   regardless of input; a vision-model (Ollama) round-trip between "confirm title screen" and
   "click PLAY" reliably loses that race. Fix: fire the corner-reset+move+click sequence as one
   fast single Python process with zero vision call in between (verified via real pixel diffing,
   not the drifty GameLink frame-sequence number).
3. **ESC, not Enter, skips the intro/credit slides** — Enter was found to auto-play the full
   intro then loop back to an unclicked title screen.

Both (1) and (3) are documented in `docs/engine/research/dosbox-x-gamelink-automation.md`-adjacent
detail directly in the new probe script comment and in the plan doc's new §7; worth pulling into
the automation doc itself if the next GameLink-mouse trace hits the same wall.

**A real solver bug found and fixed:** `packages/engine/src/loaders/dqkProtection.ts`'s
`bodyAfter()` only read the first physical PDF line after a journal heading (`pdftotext -raw`
emits one line per physical line, not per paragraph) — DQK's real Journal.pdf has multi-line
paragraphs and a requested word can fall on a continuation line (found live: "After Combat" word
#9 is on the paragraph's second physical line). Rewrote it to join continuation lines until a
blank line or a new heading-looking line, unwrapping PDF line-wrap hyphens. All 152 existing
`dqkProtection.test.ts` cases still pass (the old fixtures were all single-line, so this was a
real, previously-untested gap, not a regression).

**Live path proven, phases 1-6 of the plan:** launch menu PLAY click → ESC-skip intro → party
menu → Load Saved Game (L/T/A/Enter) → roster screen (matches plan §4.1's predicted DQK pregen
party exactly) → Begin Adventuring (B) → DQK's own native journal-word protection prompt
(vision-reads cleanly, solver answers correctly, typed answer echoes correctly on screen before
Enter is pressed).

**Genuinely blocked, not smoothed over:** 3/3 boots, 3 different randomized protection questions,
each answered with a word independently cross-checked against both the reconstructed journal
paragraph AND the GOG `Codes.pdf` key, each confirmed via on-screen echo before submitting —
all three still produced **"DISK READ ERROR"** instead of proceeding. This rules out a wrong
answer, a keystroke-delivery bug, and CPU-cycle timing (one attempt ran with the debugger's
forced `cycles=fixed 25000` present, another with it omitted — same result both times).
Same secondary symptom every time regardless of the answer: position frozen at "7,13" (not the
plan's predicted area-34 spawn "14,10"), dungeon 3D-view pane solid black. This matches the
plan's own pre-written failure-playbook row for "Hangs at overland/dungeon load" almost exactly —
current best read: "DISK READ ERROR" here is plausibly not a protection punishment at all, but a
generic failure DQK shows when the *resumed area's own ported content* fails to load, surfacing
right at this point in the sequence independent of what was typed. **Not confirmed further** — a

### SPRIT.TLB method-23 HLIB encoder SHIPPED — byte-exact vs all 93 real streams, `buildMappedArtOverride('SPRIT.TLB', …)` unblocked (STATIC ONLY, 2026-07-18)

Wave-1 Goal-1 art item from ROADMAP's 2026-07-18 critical-path section. `hlibEncode.ts`
now implements draw method 23 ("compressed transparent", the DQK SPRIT.TLB combat-sprite
codec): 4 image sweeps, `0`-terminated rows, `c<128` literal copy, `c>=128` skip `256−c`
transparent (255) columns — the exact inverse of `hlib.ts`'s long-verified decoder.

- **The original packer's choices were recovered, not guessed** (probed against DISK2
  `SPRIT.TLB`, 96 frames = 93× method 23 + 3× method 21): transparent pixels are always
  skips (never literal 255), trailing transparent runs are dropped (the row terminator
  implies them), and chunks are **word-aligned** — exactly one `0x00` pad when
  `8 + stream` is odd (43/93 chunks; proven as a rule, zero counterexamples). With those
  choices the re-encode is **byte-identical on 96/96 chunk bodies** (`hlibEncode.test.ts`
  real-file golden, which also asserts pixel round-trip per frame). The only
  A later title-placement audit made the decoder preserve the header's two signed placement
  offsets (89/93 non-zero) on `IndexedImage`, and the encoder now reproduces those bytes too;
  documented in `docs/hlib-format.md` §5.
- **Threaded into the mapped-art-override path for free**: `buildMappedArtOverride`
  already passed `entry.drawMethod` (23 for SPRIT.TLB) through
  `amigaArchiveToHlibMaster` → `encodeHlibImage`; only the encoder's method whitelist
  blocked it. `dqkArtMap.test.ts`'s former "surfaced limitation" throw-test is now a
  positive sprite-slot test: a real `SPRIT1.DAA` 88×88 sub-frame, relocated to palette
  base 176 and cropped to 72×25, repacks into a decodeHlib-readable method-23 master.
  All four Goal-1 art repack paths (master/leaf × crop/pad) plus SPRIT now work; the
  remaining SPRIT gap is purely the human-curated slot mapping (Wave-1 sibling item).
- Gates: `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` clean; engine vitest 146 files / 1713 tests green.
  Docs: `docs/hlib-format.md` §5+§8, `research/cok-content-port-plan.md` M8.S4 note
  un-staled, ROADMAP Wave-1 item marked DONE.

### DoK `16` vs `34` start-block discrepancy RECONCILED — block 16 is the native boot cinematic, `eclInitBlock: 34` stays (STATIC ONLY, 2026-07-18)

Resolves the open discrepancy from the same-day "DoK P2 natural route" round below (native
boot-path writes literal `16` into `gbl.EclBlockId`; `apps/web/src/ui/gameData.ts` assumes
`eclInitBlock: 34`). Full write-up: `docs/engine/research/dok-natural-route.md` "2026-07-18
Update 8". Static-only; no DOSBox-X; docs-only change (no gates apply).

- **Verdict: both are right at different layers — resolution (b).** Raw `GAME.OVR` bytes
  re-confirm the literal (`c6 06 6c db 10` = `mov byte [0xdb6c], 0x10` at file offset
  `0x3692`; demo branch `…02` at `0x3681`). DoK's `ECL1.DAX` block 16 decodes (project's own
  Gen1 ECL primitives + 6-bit string codec, `cok-demo-decompile.md` §7.1 method) as **DoK's
  real opening cinematic** — Gargath Outpost celebration, Sir Karl returns as a death knight,
  `SETUP_MONSTER`+`EXIT` opening battle — and block 2 decodes as the attract-mode demo reel,
  so *both* boot literals (demo=2, fresh=16) land on exactly-matching retail content.
- **Block 16 has no GEO map** (`GEO1.DAX` = {32,33,34,36} only) and **contains zero NEWECL**;
  a full three-file NEWECL census shows **nothing ever chains to 34**. `34` (Cekos, a real
  walkable town) entered `gameData.ts` in commit `52c0809` (B1, 2026-06-22) as the documented
  "first walkable dungeon (verified loadable)" engine entry — never a native-boot claim. CoK
  is the identical shape (native boot block 16, `eclInitBlock` 34). **No code change**; the
  2026-07-17 doc claim "DoK's real game-start block is 34" was circular and is corrected in
  Update 8.
- **Side-finding needing follow-up:** DoK's ECL dialect differs from the CoK-calibrated
  `GEN1_WORD_SETS` — opcode `0x1d` takes 0 operands (not 1) and `0x2c` takes 1 (not 6) in
  DoK, proven by instruction-boundary-exact parses ending precisely at block length. Any
  prior DoK scan crossing those opcodes (e.g. `build/gen1-ecl-encounters.json`'s "block 34
  has zero combat candidates") desynced and should be re-audited; the shared tool was
  deliberately left unchanged this round (feeds live corpus gates + in-flight agents).

### CoK `seg051` RNG -- dynamic-trace round 5, selector 0xa46 fully closed + a real dice-roll caller chain reopened, still DEFERRED (2026-07-18)

dynamic-trace round 5" section. **Not cracked**, but real progress on two fronts:

- **Fixed a real methodology bug in the static scan itself.** Rounds 2-4's static scans
  disassembled overlays linearly from their file start, which walks through inline ASCII
  string/data tables mixed into the code and produces spurious `imul`/`mul` hits (opcode
  `0x69` collides with printable text). Rewrote the scan to be **prologue-anchored** (only
  disassemble from real `55 89 E5`/`55 8B EC` prologues) -- with that fix, no genuine
  LCG-shaped direct multiply (odd constant + additive constant + mask/shift) exists anywhere
  in CoK's `GAME.OVR`.

  DOSBox-X capture landed at `CS=126A` (the same live segment round 4 found, confirming
  boot-determinism) and `MEMDUMPBIN` pulled ~2 KB of real code that disassembles to
  unambiguous **Borland software long/float arithmetic** (byte-wise partial-product multiply,
  zero-checked divide, sign/exponent alignment, an error-code trampoline) with **zero
  persistent/absolute-address state anywhere** -- it structurally cannot be an LCG's own seed
  store, closing this thread for good.
- **Reopened round 3's "0x395b5 ruled out" verdict with new static evidence.** Traced a fresh
  static caller chain -- a treasure-award entry (file `0x2d21b`, called from the overlay
  immediately preceding combat) that short-circuits when its area's treasure fields are
  already zero, else falls into a classic percentile-bracketed reward table (file `0x2d765`)
  whose bracket-selecting roll is **`lcall 0xdb,0x4d` = file `0x395b5`** -- the exact function

  continues (120 total) trying to reach a real kill; still only at "LOADING...PLEASE WAIT"

  already in the tree (`tools/vroomm_layout.py`) — confirmed selectors `0xa46`/`0x521`/`0x614`
  are still `unresolved_relocated_segment` even under real fixup-table parsing (not just the
  older `0x200+sel*16` approximation), and that DoK's structurally-analogous top selector
  (`0xa07`) is equally unresolvable — closes off route (a) for good, confirming route (b) (live
  capture) was the only remaining path.

  was missing descriptor 1), including descriptor 1 (file `0xda`) → live segment `0x383E`, the
  overlay hosting both remaining candidate call sites.
- **`0x521` offset `0x9ba`** (live `0D45:09BA`, called from the overlay-1 wrapper at `383E:0000`,
  static selector `0x614`/live `0E38`) traced in full: reads the DOS clock via a far call, combines
  hour/min/sec/hundredths into a 32-bit scalar via a Borland 32×16 multiply helper (`126A:0A14`) —
  **a clock reader**, not the RNG; its caller is a **generic timed-wait/blink utility** (title
  screen), also not the RNG.
- **`0xa46:0xac4`** live-resolves to `126A:0AC4` — the *same* segment as the multiply helper above,
  and (next bullet) a `strncpy`-shaped helper — independently confirming `126A` is a **shared
  Borland-runtime-library segment** (explains its 2268-site call count project-wide), not a
  game-specific RNG. Ruled out on segment-identity grounds.
- **`0x521:0x353`** (round 3's actual originally-flagged candidate) — live `0D45:0353` — traced
  instruction-by-instruction: allocates a 260-byte local buffer, `strncpy`s a far string parameter
  into it (`126A:0ADE`), calls a second unidentified helper (`0F67:0051`), checks bytes against
  `0x27` (apostrophe `'`), then does a byte-shift-right string-insert loop. **This is a text/
  grammar formatting routine** (plausibly pluralization/possessive-suffix, e.g. "point"→"points")
  — sits adjacent to the `"HITTING FOR %d POINTS OF DAMAGE"` message-building code (explaining why
  round 2's backward-trace originally flagged it) but formats the message text, not the damage
  value. **Definitively not the RNG.**
- **Net result: every static candidate identified across all 4 rounds is now live-disproven.** The
  RNG source remains genuinely UNLOCATED. Recommended round-5 approach: trace forward from the
  damage value's true origin one level higher in the same caller (before the now-known text
  formatter is invoked), or fall back to a pure LCG-arithmetic-shape scan excluding the two
  now-proven-negative segments (`126A`, `0D45`); also consider launching with `-GameLink` next
  time to legitimately advance past the title screen's idle-wait loop instead of hoping the
  attract-mode timer resolves it, which cost significant round time.
- **New reusable DOSBox-X gotcha found:** an `F5` continue issued while CS:IP sits exactly at an
  armed breakpoint's own address re-triggers instantly (0 cycles), which looks identical to a
  frozen guest — single-step once (F10/F11) off the breakpoint address before continuing. Also: an
  early invalid typed `--command` can leave the debugger console's text-command channel wedged for
  the rest of the session (the `--key` special-key channel stays unaffected) — once that happens,
  stop sending typed commands and drive purely via `--key ENTER/F5/F10/F11`.

- **The title's "Play Demo" is a real two-hotkey (`P`/`D`) menu word pair**, byte-located in
  `START.EXE` at file offset `0x21e` (not just a hint string) — `ovr027.BuildInputKeys`'s
  uppercase-scan algorithm run on the literal `"Play Demo"` text produces exactly two
  selectable words, "Play" and "Demo". A 30-second idle timeout at the title auto-fires
  `'D'` (genuine arcade attract-mode behaviour) — COAB-sourced structure, CoK's own timeout
  constants unconfirmed (needs disassembling `START.EXE`'s resident, non-FBOV code, which
  `disasm_cok.py` can't currently reach).
- **The demo is neither a keypress-log table nor a fixed-seed replay of the untouched
  normal loop.** `ovr003.sub_29758` (COAB) shows `gbl.inDemo` selects a **different literal
  `EclBlockId`** as the ECL VM's boot entry (vs. normal play's own entry block), runs the
  *exact same* `RunEclVm` interpreter used for every other in-game script, then explicitly
  frees the whole temporary party once the script returns. **The demo is a scripted ECL
  sequence** — authored in the same data-driven bytecode as every other event/encounter,
  not a separate demo code path or an input-recording format.
- **New decoded content:** `Champions of Krynn/ECL1.DAX` block **36** is CoK's real opening
  narration ("AT THE INN OF THE LAST HOME IN SOLACE...", introducing NPC **Sir Karl
  Gaardsen**), decoded human-readable via the project's existing Gen1 ECL opcode table +

  own entry constant or CoK's normal new-game opening (with the true demo constant still

  speed-up) — the original demo paces itself deliberately slow, not fast-forwarded.

## 5. Gotchas (these cost time if rediscovered)

- **Run `.mts` tools with `npx -y tsx@4`.** There is no local tsx, and node-24's
  `--experimental-strip-types` can't resolve the engine's `.js`→`.ts` import specifiers.
- **E2E must run from `apps/web`** (`cd apps/web && node test/e2e.mjs`), not the repo root.
- **The Bash shell cwd persists and drifts** after a `cd` into a subpackage — prefix
  commands with `cd /c/Modding/GoldBox` when in doubt.
- **JSDoc comments can't contain `*/`** — e.g. writing `SPRIT*/PIC*` in a `/** … */` block
  closes the comment early and breaks esbuild. Use `SPRIT, PIC` or `SPRIT* / PIC*` with a space.
- **`LF will be replaced by CRLF` git warnings are harmless** on this Windows checkout.
- **PowerShell tools that rewrite `docs/*.md` (e.g. via `Set-Content`) can silently mangle
  encoding** — a 2026-07-16 agent edit added a UTF-8 BOM and turned every em dash (`—`) in
  `BUILD-QUEUE.md` into mojibake (`â€"`) across the *whole file*, not just the section it
  touched (`file docs/engine/BUILD-QUEUE.md` should read `UTF-8 text`, no `(with BOM)`; `grep
  -c "â€" <file>` should be `0`). Prefer `Edit`/`Write` (already UTF-8-safe) over PowerShell
  `Set-Content` for markdown docs; if a PowerShell edit is unavoidable, use
  `-Encoding utf8NoBOM`. Always check `git diff --stat` on a doc edit before committing — a
  multi-thousand-line diff for a one-paragraph addition is the tell.
- **DOSBox automation MUST use GameLink, not host input — this is a hard requirement, not a
  preference.** Use `tools/dosbox_gamelink.py` directly, or pass `-GameLink` to
  `tools/dosbox_x_debugbox_probe.ps1` (starts DOSBox-X minimized, `output=gamelink`, no visible
  window to steal focus). Full writeup: `docs/engine/research/dosbox-x-gamelink-automation.md`.
  This matters most with **multiple concurrent DOSBox-X sessions** (e.g. parallel research
  subagents) — a focus-taking window steals OS focus from every other session and corrupts their
  keypress delivery too (caught live 2026-07-17: a DoK trace script that never passed `-GameLink`
  was doing exactly this to sibling agents). Older scripts predate this and used a different,
  now-superseded workaround (spawns **two** windows — target the SDL **render** window, title
  contains "DOSBox", not "Status"; synthetic keyboard input was ignored by that SDL build, so
  mouse force-focus + real click was used instead) — do not write new automation this way; port
  old scripts to GameLink when you touch them. Ollama with `format="json"` returns **empty** —
  prompt for JSON as text and regex-extract `\{.*\}`.
- **Verify on real bytes, classify honestly.** "UNLOCATED beats invention." Verify mechanics
  against each game's **own** disassembled binary (`tools/disasm_{cok,dok,dqk}.py`) and the
  COAB decompile oracle (`coab_extracted/engine/ovr*.cs`). Split oversized items in place.

## 6. The subagent pattern that's working

For a heavy item, fan out and integrate yourself: one **goldbox-researcher** RE's a format
or binary path (writes `docs/engine/research/<topic>.md`, returns a tight summary with byte
offsets), and/or one **general-purpose** agent builds a self-contained web surface. **Keep
integration + all the gates + the single deploy + the commit to the main loop** so two agents
never race on the build or the live directory. Launch independent agents in one message so
they run concurrently. (E5.6's `.DAA` RE + the `?docs=1` page, and E6.1's new-game-entry RE,
were all done this way.)

## 15. 2026-07-22 Amiga Pool of Radiance container format SOLVED (4th and last Amiga generation)

The "4th distinct, unsolved" Amiga Gold Box container (Pool of Radiance 1989 `.dax`, WHDLoad
unpacked set) is now fully decoded — all four Amiga container generations (DAA, GLIB, DOS-side
DAX/HLIB, Pool-Amiga) are solved. Static-analysis lane only; no DOSBox-X used.

- **Container:** BE, `word0 = N*10`, TOC `{u16 id, u32 off, u16 comp_size, u16 raw_size}`,
  `data_base = 2+word0`. The 2026-07-18 first-look's "fieldA/fieldB" = comp/raw size.
- **Compression:** NOT an RLE — a **backwards bit-stream LZSS with per-block XOR checksum**
  (bits LSB-first per BE long with sentinel, output written end-to-start, 6-token grammar).
  Cracked by capstone-disassembling the Amiga 68000 `program` executable: loader in hunk 10,
  decompressor at hunk 27+0x7346. Verified 843/843 blocks across all 23 `.dax` files
  (exact size + checksum 0).
- **Known-plaintext cross-platform proof:** 28/29 Amiga `ecl.dax` blocks byte-identical to the
  DOS GOG `ECL*.DAX` decompressed plaintext (id 0 = genuinely different boot script).
- **Frames:** 4-plane (16-color) contiguous planar, 12-byte header `{h,w8,y,x,nframes,plane_size}`;
  `pic`/`final`/`sprit` use an animated `{0,nframes}` + per-frame `{u32 delay, hdr, planes}`
  variant. 1544 coherent PNGs rendered (`renders/pool_amiga/`, git-ignored).
- **Palettes:** five 16-color tables in `program` hunk 23 (+0..+128); +64 confirmed for
  pic/final (coherent demon-portrait and skeleton-scene renders); combat family (+32) coherent
  for cpic/comspr/icon/cbody. Honest open nuance: per-context palette dispatch for `head`/`body`
  paper-doll art not traced (format layer unaffected). Amiga art is genuinely redrawn vs DOS
  (same dimensions per block id, no pixel identity).

Deliverables: `tools/pool_amiga_decode.py`, `docs/pool-amiga-format.md`, verdict updates in
`docs/amiga-inventory.md` (§1 table, §3, §5).

## 17. 2026-07-22 Gateway `PIC*.DAX` pixel packing SOLVED offline — captured buffer proven to be `PIC2.DAX` id 5, decoded byte-exactly

Offline/static lane only (no emulator; the DOSBox-X slot was owned elsewhere). Part 16's
captured 7,744-byte loader buffer was matched against `PIC.DAX`/`PIC2.DAX` (hash-locked
runtime stage, byte-identical to the GOG copies): it matches NO file bytes (raw or
RLE-decompressed — it is a decoded product), has an 8-byte non-pixel metadata head
(`0000 8354 0000 01E4` — the only 3 bytes >0x1F in the whole buffer live there, which
also REFUTES the 484x16 geometry reading), and bytes 8..7743 are **byte-identical
(7,736/7,736) to a deterministic decode of `PIC2.DAX` block id 5**. The proven format:
pixels start at raw[55] — i.e. the 17/33/41-byte structure Parts 3/6 called a "trailer"
actually sits BETWEEN the 21-byte frame header and the pixels (byte arithmetic could
never distinguish the placements; this is why all 9 prior packing hypotheses rendered
noise — every one assumed pixels at raw[22], misaligned 33 bytes against the true
55-byte row grid). Packing: per row, 5 consecutive 11-byte 1-bit planes (LSB plane
first, bit4 = extension last), MSB-first bits, 88 rows x 55 = 4,840 bytes zero-slop;
output = 88x88 chunky 5-bit indices — Part 8's "7744 = chunky capacity" reading
confirmed at runtime. New committed tool `tools/gateway_pic_decode.py` (decode + render
+ `--verify-capture` oracle regression gate, passing against both independent captured
buffers); all 72 single-frame 0x0c/0x0e/0x0f blocks across `PIC.DAX`-`PIC6.DAX` fit
exactly and render coherent portraits (renders in git-ignored `renders/gateway-pic/`;
byte-exact PROOF is for `PIC2.DAX` id 5, the rest is exact-fit + coherent-render
evidence). Still open: DAC 18..31 RGB values (renders use declared gray placeholders —
newly actionable live on the proven route), prefix/head structure meaning, multi-frame
tail frames (4,833-byte payloads, 7 bytes short of a full 5-plane image). Full write-up:
`research/gateway-vga-picture-format.md` Part 17. Next bounded step: port the decoder to
`packages/engine` (goldens + round-trip), refresh BUILD-QUEUE P3.1, then a live DAC
18..31 capture when the DOSBox-X slot frees.

## 30. 2026-09-25 DQK attack-rate trace and native source implementation

Task 29's static trace now connects the retail rate bytes to attack resolution.
`LOAD_MONSTER` preserves MONCHA `+0xB3/+0xB4` in the roster node; overlay 0
normalizes them into `+0x190/+0x191` using `(rate + (AE4C & 1))/2`.
Initialization sets `AE4C=0`; round advance increments it after actors.
Per-round setup at `0x24E41` sets `(combatant+0x40)+5=2`. The ordinary actor
path `0x26636 -> 0x26177` consumes `combatant[0x18F+kind]`, decrements before
resolving, retries that kind while its allowance remains, then advances from
kind 2 to kind 1. Thus secondary attacks consume `+0x191` before primary
attacks consume `+0x190`.

The earlier overlay 9 candidate `0x537B9` is not the generic attack scheduler.
Selector 3 enters it through the `DS:BEE8` function table, but its second
argument is a 9-byte snake-effect node; `+3` is that node's remaining counter.
Its alternate `[C0E4]` callback is a separate effect path.

For an ordinary, unmodified DQK HLIB monster route with no early stop, source
allowances are: UMBER HULK `4/2` gives kind 2 then 1 as `1/2` on each of the
first two rounds; PRINCE TALHOOK `3/6` gives `3/1` then `3/2`. These count
attempts, not guaranteed hits. Equipment/effect adjustment, zero-allowance
variants, target death, NPCs, GLIB, and special reaction paths need distinct
gates or evidence. The Task 29 source now tags only a validated monster from a
native HLIB DQK CCECL `D0xx` handoff. It stores the primary rate in
`C_HALFATT`, the secondary rate in the low byte of tagged `C_ATTACKS`, and the
secondary damage profile in the existing `sec_d*` arrays. AI spends kind 2
before kind 1 with the first round at phase 0. Positive secondary rates without
a valid secondary profile reject this trusted encounter; zero rates stay zero.
GLIB and non-DQK fallbacks retain their prior behavior.

## CoK creator preview resilience — 2026-11-06

Creator preparation first requests the complete appearance. If that fails because
an optional secondary original is absent or invalid, it independently validates
the primary scope and renders only its admitted first variant. The secondary
preview remains unavailable and animation remains held. Rendering uses the
shared player-presentation resolver, so DOS, Amiga fallback, Restyle failure,
identity and per-variant admission labels stay consistent with sheet/combat.
Scope-aware retries preserve primary-only preparation. Local image-pack
invalidation clears preparation/failure caches and starts a fresh full attempt.
Identity/revision/connected-view guards also prevent delayed preparation,
Restyle completion or failure results from changing the current preview or its
completion receipt. The browser harness contains missing/hash/geometry secondary
faults, retry/invalidation, mandatory-primary rejection, and a delayed old
secondary failure after switching identity.

Focused presentation tests pass 8/8; `pnpm --filter @goldbox/web typecheck`
exits 0; `node --check apps/web/test/cok-player-appearance.mjs` exits 0;
`git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors. Astra reviewed the bounded
source changes. The browser harness was **not run** under the existing Vite
`spawn EPERM` no-retry hold. No Amiga player-icon art, new mapping, or animation
frame was admitted. This slice changes no images and does not publish the
comparison page. The worktree remains broad and dirty; nothing was staged,
committed, pushed, built or deployed.
